01Chapter 1 · Agentic AI and MCP

Agentic AI kya hai — chatbot se agent tak

Pehle LLM sirf baat karne wala chatbot tha, jo sirf apni training data se jawab deta tha. Ab wahi LLM tools use karke kaam bhi kar sakta hai, feedback se seekh sakta hai aur khud decide kar sakta hai ki aage kya karna hai — yahi badlav agent ki kahani hai.

Chatbot se shuruaat

Jab LLM pehli baar aam logon ke saamne aaye, to unse baat karne ka tareeka bahut simple tha — ek website par chat dialog kholo, sawal likho, jawab pao. Yeh chatbot sirf bol sakte the, kaam nahi kar sakte the. Inki sabse badi kami yeh thi ki inka gyaan sirf training data tak simit tha, aur training ke baad duniya me jo kuch bhi naya hua, uske baare me inhe kuch pata nahi hota tha. Galtiyan bhi aam baat thi, kyunki model ke paas apne jawab ko check karne ka koi tareeka nahi tha. Phir bhi, yeh ek badi shuruaat thi, kyunki pehli baar machine se aam bhasha me baat karna mumkin hua tha.

Is samay ke LLM ko samajhne ke liye ek simple tasveer dimaag me rakho: ek bahut hi hoshiyar kitaab, jo bahut kuch jaanti hai, lekin jiske paas na haath hain, na aankhein, na koi tareeka yeh jaanne ka ki bahar duniya me abhi kya ho raha hai. Woh sirf wahi bol sakti hai jo usne pehle padha hai. Aise system se aap sawal-jawab to kar sakte ho, lekin koi kaam karwana mushkil hai. Isi kami ko door karne ke liye aage ke saalon me kai tareeke aaye, aur unhi tareekon ne dheere-dheere chatbot ko agent me badal diya.

Agent ki definition — sabse pehle yeh tay karo

Agent shabd ka matlab har kisi ke liye alag-alag hota hai. Agar aap search karoge to har jagah alag definition milegi, aur do alag chatbot se poochoge to do alag jawab mil sakte hain. Isliye is book me ek saaf definition tay ki gayi hai, jo ek mashhoor article se li gayi hai: agent woh system hai jahan LLM khud apni process aur tool usage ko dynamically direct karta hai, aur yeh control apne paas rakhta hai ki task ko kaise poora karna hai. Matlab, agent me LLM sirf jawab nahi deta, woh khud decide karta hai ki kaunsa step lena hai, kaunsa tool use karna hai, aur kab rukna hai.

Is definition me ek aur important baat hai: tool ka matlab hai koi bhi code jo LLM ka hissa nahi hai, lekin jise LLM apni marzi se call karke task poora kar sakta hai. Tool ek file reader ho sakta hai, ek calculator ho sakta hai, web search ho sakta hai, ya database query bhi ho sakti hai. LLM tool ko call karta hai, tool ka result wapas aata hai, aur phir LLM us result ko dekhkar agla kadam decide karta hai. Yeh loop hi agent ki pehchan hai.

Augmented LLM — retrieval, tools aur memory

Agent ko samajhne ke liye augmented LLM ka concept samajhna zaroori hai. Augmented LLM woh LLM hai jiske paas teen extra taaktein hoti hain: retrieval, tools aur memory. Retrieval ka matlab hai bahar ki duniya se nayi jaankari laana, jaise kisi database ya document se relevant data nikaalna. Tools ka matlab hai kaam karna, jaise file likhna, code chalana ya kisi service ko call karna. Memory ka matlab hai pichli baatchit aur context ko yaad rakhna, taaki har baar shuru se na batana pade.

Book me ek important tip di gayi hai: sirf yeh kehna kaafi nahi hai ki LLM ke paas ek tool hai to woh agent ban gaya. Asli agent woh hai jo augmented LLM use karta hai — retrieval, tools aur memory teeno ke saath — aur jo tools ko call kar sake, feedback ko LLM tak wapas pahuncha sake, aur khud se chalne wale loops me kaam kar sake, bina har tool result ko turant user ko dikhaye. Matlab, agent beech me sochta hai, check karta hai, aur phir aage badhta hai.

Agent kahan kaam aate hain

Agents un tasks ke liye sabse zyada kaam ke hain jinme planning, decision making aur tool use chahiye hota hai. User ko bahar se zyada farak nazar nahi aata — saamne wahi chat box hota hai, wahi sawal-jawab hota hai. Lekin andar se farak bahut bada hai: agent se aap sirf sawal nahi pooch sakte, aap usse kaam bhi karwa sakte ho. Woh apne environment se tools ke through interact kar sakta hai, chahe woh files hon, ya Slack jaisi external service ho.

Agents ki khaasiyat yeh hai ki woh apne kaam ko khud chun sakte hain, bahar ki duniya se interact kar sakte hain, kai users ke saath interaction ki memory rakh sakte hain, aur web par khud research kar sakte hain. Research wale kaam me to agent kai parallel tasks chala sakta hai, jo insaan ya non-agentic system me mostly ek ke baad ek hi hote. Isi liye agents ko generative AI ki sabse exciting dishaon me se ek mana jata hai.

Agent kya enable karta hai

Ek single agent ek static LLM ko — jo sirf training data se bandha hota hai — ek aise system me badal deta hai jo nayi jaankari access kar sakta hai, tools se apne environment par action le sakta hai, aadha-autonomous tareeke se kaam kar sakta hai, aur doosre agents se communicate kar sakta hai. Yeh taakat do cheezon se aati hai: ek to agent ki architecture, khaas taur par action-feedback loop, aur doosra woh capabilities jo LLM par jodi jati hain — data retrieval, tools aur memory.

Agents se pehle, LLM se baat karna hi sab kuch tha. Model time me frozen hota tha, user ki chat history yaad nahi rakh sakta tha, aur tools use nahi kar sakta tha. RAG ne isme pehla bada badlav laaya, aur fine-tuning se model ka gyaan ya personality badli ja sakti thi. Lekin agents ne usse bhi aage badhkar yeh mumkin kar diya: khud ki judgment se deterministic code call karna, doosre agents ke saath coordinate karna, user ki chat history ki short-term memory rakhna, aur sabse important, web aur specialized tools ke through bahar ki duniya se communicate karna. Yeh saare actions agent banne ke liye zaroori nahi hain, lekin inke combination ne generative AI me sabse exciting advances ko janm diya hai, aur yeh web ki shape ko bhi badal sakta hai.

Use cases — coding, research, customer service aur copilots

Book me agents ke chaar popular use cases bataye gaye hain. Pehle, coding agents — shayad sabse common aur popular. Unsupervised apps me CLI se instruction di jati hai aur code changes background me hote hain, jaise Claude Code aur Codex. Supervised apps me code editor ke andar hi UI hota hai, jahan aap changes ko dekh aur approve kar sakte ho, jaise Cursor, Devin Desktop aur VS Code ke liye GitHub Copilot extension.

Doosre, research agents — jo kisi topic par deep research karte hain, memory, web search jaise tools, aur kabhi-kabhi extra autonomous agents ka use karke alag-alag research directions ko pursue karte hain. Ek research agent built-in aur user-provided tools ke combination se kaam karta hai, memory store se context aur current research directions ka scratchpad rakhta hai, aur subagents ko orchestrate karke alag directions par kaam karwata hai.

Teesre, customer service agents — jo ab har jagah dikhne lage hain. Zyadatar abhi bhi simple decision trees ya RAG wale chatbots hain, lekin dheere-dheere asli agent bante ja rahe hain, tool use aur memory add karke customer ke sawal ka behtar jawab de rahe hain, issue fix karne me guide kar rahe hain ya khud fix karne ki koshish kar rahe hain, aur zaroorat padne par issue ko zyada accurately escalate kar rahe hain.

Chauthe, software-specific copilots ya assistants — kai software applications aur platforms, khaas taur par enterprise customers ko serve karne wale, apne software ko use aur manage karne me madad ke liye copilot add kar rahe hain. In agents ke paas us software ke liye specific tools hote hain — koi user data se chart bana sakta hai, koi branded report generate kar sakta hai, aur koi natural language me software ka data query karne me madad kar sakta hai. Inke alawa bhi possibilities lagbhag endless hain: interactive art projects, kai interactions se bane AI personalities, 3D modeling agents, physical objects me embodied agents, aur all-in-one personal assistant agents.

SOURCESource: AI Agents with MCP, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — Agentic AI and MCP

01.1Chapter 1 · Agentic AI and MCP

LLM se agent tak ka safar — RAG aur function calling

Chatbot se agent tak ka safar ek raat me nahi hua. Pehle RAG ne model ko fresh data diya, phir ReAct ne sochne aur action karne ka pattern diya, aur phir function calling ne LLM ko structured tareeke se tools call karna sikhaya.

Stage A — sirf chatbot, koi extra system nahi

Book me Figure 1-1 ke through teen stages dikhaye gaye hain. Pehla stage, jise A label diya gaya hai, woh original commercial LLM tha: user web viewer se seedha model se baat karta tha, beech me koi aur visible system nahi hota tha. User prompt likhta tha, model jawab deta tha, bas. Is stage me model ke paas sirf training data hota tha, aur uske bahar ki koi jaankari us tak nahi pahunchti thi. Yeh simple tha, lekin iski limits bhi saaf thi — model ko naya data nahi milta tha, aur woh koi action nahi le sakta tha.

Stage B — RAG, retrieval se prompt ko enrich karna

Doosra stage RAG ka tha, jise B label diya gaya hai. RAG ka full form hai retrieval-augmented generation. Isme software user ki query ko beech me intercept karta tha, prompt se vector database me search karta tha, aur relevant data nikaal kar user ke prompt ko enrich karke LLM tak bhejta tha. Vector database me vector similarity measures ka use karke semantically similar jaankari dhoondhi jati thi, matlab sirf exact words match nahi hote the, matlab ke hisaab se milti-julti jaankari bhi mil jati thi.

RAG ka fayda yeh tha ki LLM ko woh jaankari bhi mil jati thi jo uske paas pehle se nahi thi, aur usse uske jawab guide hote the. Yeh technique aaj bhi sabse important context-modifying techniques me se ek hai. Isse aise chatbots bane jo organization ke knowledge base, support documents ya doosre data sources se sawalon ke jawab de sakte the. RAG ne LLM ko time me frozen hone se bahar nikala, lekin phir bhi model sirf bol sakta tha, kaam nahi kar sakta tha.

ReAct — reason karo, phir act karo

Ussi samay ke aas-paas ReAct aaya, jiska matlab hai REasoning + ACTing. Yeh ek aisi technique thi jisne LLM ko yeh capability di ki woh reasoning aur task-specific actions ke beech alternate kar sake. Matlab, model pehle sochta tha ki kya karna hai, phir koi action leta tha, phir uske result ko dekhkar phir sochta tha. Yeh action-feedback loop ka pehla roop tha, jo aage chal kar agent ki neenv bana.

Lekin us samay bhi yeh actions zyadatar prompt ke andar hi simit the. Model bahar ki duniya me koi real action nahi le sakta tha, woh sirf apne jawab me action ka zikr kar sakta tha. Phir bhi, ReAct ne yeh dikhaya ki LLM ko sochne aur karne ke beech ghumana mumkin hai, aur yahi pattern aage chal kar agent ke loop me badal gaya.

Stage C — function calling, structured tool use

Teesra stage function calling ka tha, jise C label diya gaya hai. Isse pehle, 2023 me ChatGPT plug-ins aaye the: third-party tools jo seedha ChatGPT ko expose kiye ja sakte the. Isme security risks nikle, isliye usi saal ke baad me function calling introduce kiya gaya. Function calling OpenAI API ka first-class member ban gaya. Isme kaam aise hota tha: aap LLM ko structured tool definitions dete the, jinme tool ke inputs bhi hote the, aur LLM structured response deta tha jisme bataya hota tha ki kaunsa function call karna hai, aur kin parameters ke saath.

Figure 1-1 ke stage C me flow aise dikhta hai: user LLM ko tool definitions ke saath query karta hai, LLM decide karta hai ki kaunsa tool call karna hai aur structured output emit karta hai — function ka naam, parameters aur parameter values. Phir compute environment tool ko execute karta hai, aur result wapas LLM ko bheja jata hai, jo use natural language me user ke saamne present karta hai. Yahi woh step tha jo augmented LLM ke sabse kareeb pahuncha: ek aisa LLM jo bahar ka data query kar sake (retrieval), actions commit kar sake (tools), aur apne local context me kya yaad rakhna hai, yeh decide kar sake.

Augmented LLM — nayi standard

Yeh augmented LLM uske baad se LLM ka standard conceptualization ban gaya. Retrieval, tooling aur memory ki capabilities sirf ek standard nahi rahi, balki har LLM provider ke liye table stakes ban gayi — matlab, inke bina koi provider compete hi nahi kar sakta tha. Is augmented LLM se zyada complex workflows banana mumkin hua, aur yahi se agent ke development ki shuruaat hui.

Is safar ko ek line me samjho: pehle model sirf bolta tha, phir usse fresh data milne laga, phir usne sochna aur action karna seekha, aur phir usne structured tareeke se tools call karna seekha. Har step ne model ko thoda aur capable banaya, aur jab yeh teeno taaktein — retrieval, tools aur memory — ek saath aa gayi, to agent ka raasta khul gaya. Aaj ke agents isi neenv par khade hain, aur MCP is neenv ko standard banane ka agla kadam hai.

SOURCESource: AI Agents with MCP, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — Agentic AI and MCP

01.2Chapter 1 · Agentic AI and MCP

Action-feedback loops aur prompt chaining

Agent aur workflow me sabse bada farak yeh hai ki control kiske haath me hai. Agent me LLM khud decide karta hai ki aage kya karna hai, jabki workflow me code pehle se tay karta hai ki kaunsa step kab aayega.

Action-feedback loop kya hai

Agent ka kaam ek loop me hota hai. LLM ek course of action decide karta hai, uska pehla step karta hai, feedback gather karta hai — aam taur par tool call ka result — aur phir decide karta hai ki result ko final answer ke roop me user ko dikhaye, feedback se koi aur action kare, ya user se aur jaankari maange. Yeh loop tab tak chalta hai jab tak task poora na ho jaye ya LLM ko lage ki ab rukna chahiye.

Is loop ki jad ReAct loop me hai, jisme aam taur par teen distinct steps hote hain, action-feedback ke do steps ke bajay. Pehla step hai Reason — model goal aur apni current state ke baare me sochta hai aur agla action decide karta hai. Doosra step hai Act — model apne environment ka use karta hai, jaise available tools, diye gaye fields, user ka prompt, pichli conversation history, aur bhi bahut kuch. Teesra step hai Observe — action ke results ko LLM ko wapas feed kiya jata hai taaki woh result ko observe kar sake, aur phir wapas reasoning par loop kare aur problem-solving process ka agla step decide kare, jisme task ko complete declare karke results user ko wapas dena bhi shaamil hai.

Coding agent ka example — teen loops

Book me ek common example diya gaya hai: aap ek AI-powered code editor me ho aur chatbot se kehte ho ki aapke code ke liye unit tests likhe. Pehla loop shuru hota hai: LLM user request ko steps me todta hai, phir decide karta hai ki feature.py ko file reader tool se padhe. Feedback me read kiya gaya code, sirf uski structure, ya file ka koi aur representation wapas aata hai. LLM use observe karta hai aur agla step decide karta hai.

Doosra loop me agent woh saare tests likhta hai jo feature.py ke contents se imply hote hain. Yahan likhna hi action hai, environment me test writing standards aur file writing tool hote hain, aur feedback me likha gaya code hota hai. Teesre loop me agent tests ko run karta hai — yeh action hai, environment test environment aur test run karne wale tools hain, aur feedback me test results, test coverage ya koi aur helpful jaankari hoti hai, jisse model agle steps decide kar sake.

Teesre loop ke baad, agar results satisfactory hain to loops khatam ho sakte hain. Agar nahi hain, to agent shayad doosra loop phir se chalayega, ya koi aur precise action lega, jaise failing tests ko fix karna, phir teesra loop phir se chalana, aur tab tak continue karna jab tak results satisfactory na ho jayein. Yahi agent ki taakat hai — woh result dekhkar apna plan badal sakta hai.

Agentic workflow — jab code control karta hai

AI loop se alag hota hai agentic workflow, ek aisa system jisme code — LLM nahi — decide karta hai ki logic kis path par jayegi, lekin phir bhi kisi hisse ka kaam karne ke liye LLM ko call karta hai. Yeh complex tasks ke liye bahut useful pattern hai, jahan code se enforce ki gayi deterministic logic ki zaroorat hoti hai. Example ke liye, ek application socho jo code ko input lekar uska equivalent doosri language me badal deta hai.

Workflow approach me pehle input code ko LLM ko diya jata hai taaki woh detect kare ki code kis language me hai, aur agar language detect nahi hoti to user ko failure message wapas kar diya jata hai. Agar LLM language detect kar leta hai aur woh language aisi hai jiske liye aapke paas deterministic parser hai, to code us parser ko feed kiya jata hai aur translated output user ko wapas kar diya jata hai. Agar aisi language detect hoti hai jiske liye parser nahi hai, to LLM ko phir se call karke use translation karne ke liye prompt kiya jata hai, aur output user ko wapas kar diya jata hai.

Prompt chaining — prompts ek ke baad ek

Prompt chaining ek common agentic workflow pattern hai, jo tasks ke liye use hota hai jinme ek ya zyada LLM calls aur code path chahiye hota hai yeh decide karne ke liye ki task poora karne ke liye agle steps kya honge. Book ke example me user software se kehta hai ki ek file ko TypeScript me translate karo. Workflow pehle chained prompt se shuru hota hai jo user ke task ko determine karta hai aur use steps me todta hai. Yeh structured output ke roop me LLM ko bheja jata hai, agle prompt ke saath jo text ki language detect karta hai.

Phir LLM structured output wapas karta hai, jisme detected language aur us prediction me model ka confidence hota hai. Yeh structured output phir se LLM ko bheja jata hai, is baar translation prompt ke saath. Translated code ko chauthi baar LLM ko bheja jata hai, validation prompt ke saath. Validated output phir user ko wapas kar diya jata hai. Is workflow me LLM calls ki ek series hoti hai, jahan prompts pichli calls ke results par build hote hain, aur workflow ki direction primarily code se driven hoti hai, LLM se nahi.

Baaki workflow patterns

Prompt chaining ke alawa book me chaar aur common workflow patterns bataye gaye hain. Parallelization me kai LLM calls ek saath kiye jate hain aur results ko combine kiya jata hai. Translation example ko hi aage badhayein to parallelization workflow ek translation request ko alag-alag independent LLM calls me fan out kar dega — shayad kai translations ek saath karke — aur results ko aggregator function se combine karke user ko deliver karega.

Routing me ek LLM input ko classify karta hai aur phir classified input ke saath kai possible LLM calls me se ek karta hai. Example ke liye, router LLM user request ko translation request ke roop me classify karta hai aur use translator LLM ko bhejta hai, jabki doosri request ko grammar-checking request ke roop me classify karke use kisi aur LLM ko bhejta hai jo us task ke liye behtar suited hai.

Orchestrator-worker workflow me ek LLM task ko todta hai, worker LLMs ko chhote tasks par kaam karne ke liye call karta hai, aur aakhir me ek aggregator LLM ko results ko ek saath rakhne ke liye call karta hai. Translation task me orchestrator chhote LLMs ko individual words ya phrases translate karne ke liye call kar sakta hai, aur aakhri LLM ko translation ko phir se assemble karne ka kaam de sakta hai — book kehti hai ki yeh bahut buri tarah se fail hoga, lekin pattern samajhne ke liye yeh ek acha example hai.

Evaluator-optimizer workflow me ek LLM user prompt ka response generate karta hai aur doosra LLM call us response ko evaluate karta hai — agar acceptable hai to user ko present karta hai, ya feedback ke saath pehle LLM conversation ko wapas bhejta hai taaki use refine kiya ja sake.

Agentic approach — wahi task, alag tareeka

Iske contrast me, ek agentic approach LLM ko language detection aur translation tools dega, aur sirf yeh kahega ki input ki language detect karo aur sahi tool use karke translation karo. User code input deta hai, LLM call hota hai, LLM reasoning step karta hai — user kya chahta hai yeh samajhna aur agla step plan karna. Agla step aam taur par ek action-feedback loop hota hai, jahan problem-solving process ke ek step ke liye action liya jata hai — agent ke environment ko dekhkar, jaise tools, user context, conversation history, files aur koi bhi aur available data — aur phir result ko observe kiya jata hai aur agent ke scratchpad me add kiya jata hai taaki agle steps ko inform kiya ja sake.

Agar feedback se yeh decide nahi hota ki task complete hai, to action-feedback loop LLM ki ek aur round planning ke baad repeat ho sakta hai. Yeh tab tak chalega jab tak poora process complete na ho jaye. Yahan sabse bada farak yeh hai: prompt-chaining workflow me LLM koi decision nahi leta, use sirf ek specified order me prompts diye jate hain, aur developer ko steps, prompts aur flow control pehle se develop karne hote hain. Agent ko agency dene se developer yeh lagbhag saara kaam LLM par offload kar deta hai. Yaad rakhne wali chief difference yeh hai: agents ek ya zyada action-feedback loops me kaunse tools use karne hain aur kaunse actions lene hain yeh decide kar sakte hain, jabki workflows code paths ka use karke decide karte hain ki kaunse tools aur actions use karne hain aur kaise.

01.3Chapter 1 · Agentic AI and MCP

M × N problem — integrations ka dard

Har model ke liye har tool ka alag connector likhna jaldi hi impossible ho jata hai. Teen model aur chaar tools ke liye 12 connector chahiye hote hain — aur yahi M × N problem hai, jise MCP khatam karta hai.

M × N problem kya hai

MCP se pehle, agentic AI abhi bhi fairly new thi, lekin jo organizations internal generative AI platforms bana rahi thi, aur LangChain jaise public frameworks, unhe users ke liye tools implement karne ke alag-alag tareeke dhoondhne padte the, aur phir unhe LLM ko dena padta tha. Har alag LLM ko apna connector chahiye hota tha. Isse M × N problem paida hui: har ek M LLM ke liye jise support karna hai, aapko har tool, data source, aadi ke liye N connectors chahiye hote hain.

Book ka example simple hai: agar aap 3 models aur 4 tools support karte ho, to aapko 12 connectors likhne honge, jo zyadatar ek jaise hi hote hain. Har naya model ya har naya tool aane par connectors ki sankhya multiply hoti jati hai, aur har connector me wahi logic dobara likhna padta hai. Isse hard-to-diagnose bugs ke chances badh jate hain, kyunki ek hi cheez kai jagah likhi hoti hai aur har jagah thodi alag hoti hai.

Figure 1-5 aur 1-6 — pehle aur baad me

Figure 1-5 me yeh design dikhaya gaya hai: 3 models ko 4 tools ki access chahiye, aur result 12 connectors hain. Har model ka har tool se seedha connection hai, aur har connection ek alag connector hai. Yeh dekhne me hi messy lagta hai, aur maintain karna usse bhi zyada mushkil hai. Koi bhi tool badlo to teen jagah badlav karna padega, koi bhi model badlo to chaar jagah.

Figure 1-6 me MCP ke baad ki tasveer hai: MCP models aur tools ke beech me baitha hai. Har model ko sirf ek connector chahiye hota hai MCP client tak, aur har tool ko sirf ek connector chahiye hota hai MCP server tak. Wahi 3 models aur 4 tools ab sirf 7 connectors me kaam kar jate hain, 12 ke bajay. Jaise-jaise models aur tools badhte hain, farak aur bada hota jata hai — 10 models aur 10 tools ke liye M × N me 100 connectors chahiye honge, jabki M + N me sirf 20.

M + N kaise kaam karta hai

Model Context Protocol, jo Language Server Protocol se inspired hai, tools, prompts aur data resources ko LLM se connect karne ke liye ek common interface deta hai. Is tareeke se, kisi bhi sankhya M ke LLMs ke liye aapko sirf N connectors likhne hote hain, aur M × N problem M + N problem me badal jati hai. Har model ya AI application ko sirf MCP server ke liye apna connector chahiye hota hai, aur MCP sabke liye available tools use karne ka common interface deta hai.

Ek simple, standard interface banakar MCP servers M × N problem ko M + N problem me reduce kar dete hain: koi bhi model jo tool use support karta hai, use MCP client ke through MCP server se connect kiya ja sakta hai, to ek single MCP server ke diye gaye saare tools ke liye sirf ek connector — client — chahiye hota hai. Har server jo tools support karta hai, woh ListTools aur CallTool endpoints expose karta hai, jise host application apne client ke through call karta hai — pehla available tools ki list lene ke liye, aur doosra unhe call karne ke liye.

Yeh problem sirf numbers ki nahi hai

M × N problem sirf connectors ginne ki problem nahi hai. Iske peeche ek deeper problem hai: integrations tightly coupled hote the application ke codebase se. Har integration ko application ke developers ko khud banana padta tha, aur har model ke liye alag tareeke se. Iska matlab yeh tha ki ek team jo ek acha tool banati thi, woh use doosri team ya doosre model ke saath easily share nahi kar sakti thi. Har team ko wahi kaam dobara karna padta tha.

MCP is problem ko isliye solve karta hai kyunki woh integrations ko application code se alag kar deta hai. Server ek common interface deta hai, aur koi bhi host application usse connect karke tools ko discover aur use kar sakti hai. Isse tools reusable bante hain, share karna aasan hota hai, aur naye models ya tools add karna bhi aasan ho jata hai. Aage ke chapters me aap dekhenge ki yeh decoupling kaise distribution aur two-way communication ko bhi enable karta hai.

01.4Chapter 1 · Agentic AI and MCP

MCP ki bhoomika aur doosre protocols

MCP LLM ko tools, prompts aur data se connect karta hai. Doosre protocols agents ko aapas me baat karne me madad karte hain — yeh MCP ke competitor nahi hain, balki uske complement hain.

MCP ke teen main components

Book me MCP ke main components ka ek short note diya gaya hai, jo agle chapter me detail me cover hoga. Pehla hai MCP server, jo tools, prompts, data resources aur aur bhi bahut kuch ek common interface ke through deta hai. Doosra hai MCP client, jo host application aur MCP server ke beech ka connector hai. Teesra hai MCP transport, jo underlying communication protocol hai jo client aur server ke beech communication allow karta hai. In teeno ko samajhna MCP ko samajhne ki neenv hai.

MCP ki bhoomika yeh hai ki woh tools ko agents se decouple kar de. Traditionally, tools agent software ke andar hi built hote the. MCP ek single target deta hai jahan saare connectors ja sakte hain. Isse M × N problem M + N me badal jati hai, aur model aur tool support ko scale karna bahut zyada tractable ho jata hai. Yahi MCP ka core promise hai.

Agent2Agent protocol — A2A

MCP ki success ke baad, doosre groups ne apne agentic protocols announce kiye. Inme sabse notable hai Google ka Agent2Agent protocol, jise A2A kaha jata hai. Jab A2A release hua, to uske creators ne saaf kar diya tha ki yeh MCP ka competitor nahi hai, balki uska complement hai. MCP is baat par focus karta hai ki LLM tools, prompts aur data resources ko kaise access aur use karein, jabki A2A is par focus karta hai ki agents ek doosre se kaise communicate karein.

Matlab, ek agent MCP ka use karke tools aur data access kar sakta hai, aur phir bhi A2A ka use karke doosre agents se communicate kar sakta hai. Dono protocols ek saath kaam karte hain, ek doosre ki jagah nahi lete. Yeh distinction samajhna important hai, kyunki kai log naye protocols ko dekhkar sochte hain ki MCP replace ho jayega, jabki asli picture yeh hai ki har protocol ek alag problem solve karta hai.

Agent Communication Protocol — ACP

Agent Communication Protocol, jise ACP kaha jata hai, A2A ki tarah agents ke beech communication par focus karta hai. Yeh is communication ke liye ek RESTful API deta hai, jo alag-alag tech stacks aur models se bane agents ko ek saath kaam karne deta hai. Iska matlab hai ki aapka agent chahe kisi bhi language ya framework me bana ho, agar woh ACP bolta hai to woh doosre ACP agents se baat kar sakta hai.

ACP ka focus interoperability par hai — alag-alag systems ko ek common tareeke se baat karwana. Yeh MCP se alag layer par kaam karta hai: MCP agent ko tools se jodta hai, ACP agent ko agent se jodta hai. Dono ka combination ek zyada complete agentic system banata hai.

Agent Network Protocol

Agent Network Protocol ek Chinese-developed protocol hai, jo phir se interagent communication ko aasan aur kam brittle banane par focus karta hai. Is protocol me identity aur authentication built-in hai, aur yeh agents ke beech encrypted communication support karta hai. Identity aur authentication ka built-in hona ek badi baat hai, kyunki agents jab ek doosre se baat karte hain to yeh jaanna zaroori hota hai ki saamne wala agent kaun hai aur kya woh trusted hai.

Encrypted communication se agents ke beech ki baatchit private rehti hai, jo enterprise ya sensitive use cases ke liye bahut important hai. Yeh protocol bhi MCP ka competitor nahi hai, balki ek alag problem — agents ke beech secure communication — ko solve karta hai.

MCP vs baaki protocols — web ki nayi shape

MCP, iske contrast me, agents ko traditional web se tools ke through connect karta hai. Individual agents ab web ki structure ka hissa hain, bilkul users, documents aur API ke through web ko expose kiye gaye programs ki tarah. A2A aur ACP, doosri taraf, agents ki ek nayi web banane ka vaada karte hain, jahan agents ek doosre se communicate karte hain taaki jaankari access kar sakein, user tasks poore kar sakein, aur shayad isse bhi zyada kuch.

Yeh protocols interesting hain aur shayad ek overall agentic protocol tech stack ka hissa ban jayenge — bilkul Internet Protocol tech stack ki tarah — jisme MCP aur, agar hum internet ke raaste par chalein to, kai aur purpose-built protocols honge. Lekin yeh doosre protocols is book ka focus nahi hain. Book aapko challenge karti hai ki aap inhe explore karo, aur figure out karo ki inhe MCP ke saath kaise incorporate kiya ja sakta hai. Samajhne wali baat yeh hai ki MCP ka sabse bada community hai, aur woh tools aur data ko LLM tak pahunchane ka standard ban chuka hai.

02Chapter 2 · An Introduction to the Model Context Protocol

MCP kya hai — genesis aur history

MCP ka janm ek chhoti si frustration se hua tha — Claude Desktop aur code editor ke beech baar-baar copy-paste karna. Us frustration se ek aisa protocol bana jo aaj agents ki duniya ka standard hai.

Context ka matlab — naam me kya hai

MCP ka full form hai Model Context Protocol. Model ka matlab hai LLM, protocol ka matlab hai woh niyam jinse communication hota hai, lekin context ka matlab kya hai? MCP ke liye context woh saari jaankari hai jo ek user query ke liye model ko di jati hai, jisme query ya prompt khud bhi shaamil hai. Model ka context window woh amount hai, aam taur par tokens me, jo model ek baar me le sakta hai. Ise model ki working memory samjho — woh saari jaankari jise model seedha use kar sakta hai jab woh user query par kaam kar raha ho.

MCP ke liye context me tool names aur definitions, prompts, data URIs aur aur bhi bahut kuch ho sakta hai. Isi se context engineering ka practice aata hai, jo is baat se concerned hai ki model ko diya gaya poora context kaise define aur design kiya jaye taaki agent ko sahi outcome tak accurately guide kiya ja sake. Ek mashhoor researcher ne ise aise describe kiya tha: context engineering woh delicate art aur science hai jisme context window ko agle step ke liye bilkul sahi jaankari se bhara jata hai. Yahi woh kaam hai jo MCP enable karta hai.

Genesis — ek engineer ki frustration

MCP ka janm Anthropic ke andar ek internal project se hua. Wahan ek software engineer Claude Desktop ka use karke apne day-to-day kaam me madad le raha tha — developer tools likhna. Lekin woh is baat se frustrated tha ki use baar-baar Claude Desktop aur apne code editor ke beech code copy-paste karna padta tha. Agar aapne LLM-powered coding tools ki current wave se pehle AI-assisted coding ki hai, to aapne shayad wahi frustration mehsoos ki hogi.

Us engineer ne ek LSP project par bhi kaam kiya tha, aur wahi inspiration uske dimaag me thi jab woh apni problem ke baare me soch raha tha. LSP ka full form hai Language Server Protocol — ek open protocol jo JSON-RPC ka use karke client aur server ke beech communication enable karta hai, taaki IDE ko advanced language knowledge mil sake. Agar aapne kabhi non-LLM autocomplete use kiya hai, ya kisi variable ya function call par hover karke uski definition dekhi hai, ya ek variable ke saare instances ko IDE se rename kiya hai, to aapne shayad LSP aur ek ya zyada language servers ka use kiya hai. Yeh protocol Microsoft ne VS Code ke liye develop kiya tha aur 2016 me standardize hua tha, aur jaldi hi IDEs ko advanced language-specific capabilities dene ka de facto standard ban gaya tha.

LSP se MCP tak ka idea

Apni problem par sochte hue, woh engineer zyada broadly soch raha tha ki Claude Desktop ke liye, aur aam taur par LLMs ke liye, integrations banana kaise aasan banaya jaye. Usne notice kiya ki LLMs ke liye integrations likhna, khaas taur par ek se zyada LLMs ke liye, M × N problem paida karta hai — har ek M LLM ke liye aapko N integrations ke liye M × N connectors likhne hote hain. LSP project abhi bhi uske dimaag ke peeche tha, aur use samajh aaya ki LSP jaisa protocol M × N problem ka perfect solution ho sakta hai.

Isse M × N problem M + N problem me badal jayegi: ab integrations ko har LLM ke liye unique connectors ki zaroorat nahi hogi, bas ek shared protocol par communicate karne ki ability chahiye hogi, jo integrations aur LLMs ko apne connectors implement karne ke liye ek common interface dega. Yeh connectors sirf MCP servers se interface karenge, LLM aur integration ke har combination se nahi.

Usne apna idea ek aur engineer ko bataya, aur dono ne milkar woh neenv rakhni shuru ki jo MCP banne wali thi. Us saal ke baad me, MCP ke initial release se pehle, Anthropic me ek internal hackathon hua. Kai teams ne turant MCP adopt kar liya aur Claude Desktop ke liye har tarah ke tools aur integrations banane ke liye MCP ka use karna shuru kar diya. Yeh rapid, organic adoption peeche mudkar dekhne par aane wali cheezon ka sign tha — sirf ek mahine baad, jab MCP pehli baar public ko release kiya gaya.

Public release aur ecosystem ka explosion

MCP release hone se pehle, kuch vendors ko early access mila tha aur woh Anthropic ki madad se apne applications ke liye clients aur servers bana sake the. MCP ka kai major IDEs aur doosre tools me turant integration, jo developers daily use karte the, MCP ki runaway success ka ek bada contributor tha. Doosra, aur shayad bada contributor, yeh tha ki MCP ne MCP servers ke roop me naye tools banana aur distribute karna kitna aasan bana diya tha.

Is ease of creation se MCP servers aur unhe banane ke tutorials ki near-immediate proliferation hui, aur ecosystem ka janm hua. Is ease of use se kuch issues bhi aaye: kuch servers bina kisi authentication ya authorization ke bane the, kuch sensitive jaankari leak karte the, aur kuch bas expected tareeke se kaam nahi karte the. Lekin isse community ruki nahi. Jaise-jaise developers ko zyada experience mila, unhone Reddit par communities banayi, aur ek community-run MCP Discord server banaya taaki apne experiences share kar sakein aur ek doosre ki madad kar sakein. Unhone development ke liye best practices aur standards develop kiye, aur MCP documentation, protocol specifications, SDKs aur aur bhi bahut kuch me contribute kiya.

Linux Foundation ko donation — neutral rehna

MCP ki kahani entertaining hai, lekin yeh MCP ki jagah ko samajhne ke liye important context bhi deti hai, larger generative AI tooling ecosystem me. Yeh REST API nahi hai; yeh LSP jaisa hai, jo remote servers ko bhi exist karne deta hai. Yeh ek protocol hai, kisi specific SDK ya implementation se bandha hua nahi hai.

MCP isliye exist karta hai taaki woh open rahe, aur agents ko tools, prompts aur data discover karne de, aur decide karne de ki unhe kab aur kaise use karna hai. Specifically, MCP isliye design kiya gaya tha taaki LLMs ke liye integrations likhna aasan ho, agents aur servers ke beech two-way communication allow ho, aur teams apne tools, prompts aur data sources ko doosri teams aur public ko easily distribute kar sakein. Is openness ki spirit me, Anthropic ne MCP ko Linux Foundation ke Agentic AI Foundation ko donate kar diya, taaki yeh ek vendor- aur service-neutral protocol bana rahe jo poore agentic AI ecosystem ko serve kare.

Book me ek note bhi hai jo batata hai ki book kyun likhi gayi: jab book ke author ne MCP se banana shuru kiya tha, to servers banane ke bahut se tutorials the, lekin clients banane par bahut kam resources the — jabki zyadatar log sirf un applications me servers integrate kar rahe the jinme clients pehle se built-in the. Isi gap ko bharne ke liye yeh book likhi gayi, taaki log MCP ko deeply samajh sakein, uske har component ko samajh sakein, aur protocol ko Python SDK ke through wield kar sakein.

02.1Chapter 2 · An Introduction to the Model Context Protocol

MCP kin problems ko solve karta hai

MCP sirf copy-paste ki problem solve karne ke liye nahi bana tha. Uske peeche teen badi problems thi — integrations banana mushkil tha, unhe distribute karna mushkil tha, aur agents aur servers ke beech do-tarfah baatchit ka koi standard tareeka nahi tha.

Problem 1 — integrations banana

Agents aur generative AI ke sabse exciting developments me se ek yeh hai ki woh doosre applications ko superpowers dete hain. Aap apne notes se sawal pooch sakte ho, apne IDE se function likhwa sakte ho, agent se apna calendar organize karwa sakte ho ya files prune karwa sakte ho. Lekin in sab uses ke liye application aur LLM ke beech integrations chahiye hote hain. Historically, yeh integrations application ke developers khud banate the aur woh application ke codebase se tightly coupled hote the.

Isse kai downstream issues hote the, lekin sabse important yeh tha ki agar ek application kai models support karna chahta hai, to developers ko har integration ke liye har model ke liye ek connector likhna padta tha. Yahi woh M × N problem hai jo Chapter 1 me discuss ki gayi thi, aur jo ek point par integrations banana untenable bana deti hai. MCP is problem ko MCP server se address karta hai. Server tools, prompts aur data sources jaise integrations ko discover aur use karne ke liye ek common interface deta hai.

MCP use karne wale application developers ko ab har model ke liye aur har integration ke liye custom connectors likhne ki zaroorat nahi hoti. Iske bajay, woh sirf server se connect karte hain, server jo integrations provide karta hai unki lists lete hain, aur phir integration use karne ke liye wahi function call karte hain — jaise Python me tools ke liye use_tool() jisme tool ka naam aur arguments parameters ke roop me pass kiye jate hain. Is universal connector architecture ko aksar integrations ke liye USB-C architecture kaha jata hai, kyunki connector saare integrations ke liye ek jaisa hota hai.

Ek note me saaf kiya gaya hai ki is chapter me integrations aur tools ko kuch had tak interchangeably use kiya gaya hai. Tools ek type ke LLM integration hain — deterministic code ki units, aam taur par functions, jo LLM call aur execute kar sakta hai. Integrations ek zyada general term hai, jisme tools bhi aate hain, lekin saath me data sources jaise prompt context bhi aata hai, jo LLM request me integrate kiya ja sakta hai.

Problem 2 — distribution

Pehle, agents ke saath kaam karne wali teams ko apne tools aur connectors khud banane padte the. Kyunki yeh aksar bespoke aur environment specific hote the, woh reusable nahi hote the aur isliye teams ke beech distribute karna mushkil hota tha, public ki to baat hi chhodo. MCP ke saath, hum tools, prompts, data resources aur aur bhi bahut kuch share kar sakte hain — ya to indirectly GitHub jaise code-sharing platform ke through, ya ek running server ke roop me jisse models seedha connect kar sakte hain.

Kyunki MCP integrations ko discover aur use karne ke liye interface ko unify karta hai, integrations khud application code se decoupled ho sakte hain, aur integrations consume karne wale kisi bhi agent ko bas yeh discover karna hota hai ki kya available hai, aur phir appropriate integration use karna hota hai. Isse teams aur individuals ke liye ek force-multiplier effect unlock hota hai. Koi bhi apne datasets ya tools ko MCP server likhkar AI ready bana sakta hai aur use duniya ke saath share kar sakta hai.

Badi organization ke andar teams khud ko MCP servers likhne aur doosri teams ko distribute karne ke liye dedicate kar sakti hain, ya teams MCP servers par collaborate karke unhe poori organization me share kar sakti hain, aur poore business ke liye tools, prompts aur data ko standardize kar sakti hain. Yahi distribution ki taakat hai — ek baar banao, har jagah use karo.

Problem 3 — two-way communication

Kai communication protocols ki tarah, MCP bhi two-way communication ke liye design kiya gaya hai. MCP servers sirf host application aur LLM ko jaankari bhej nahi sakte, balki unse jaankari receive bhi kar sakte hain. Yeh autonomous communications protocols ke liye zaroori hai, kyunki dono parties ko aksar basic tasks karne ke liye ek doosre ko data bhejna padta hai — jaise connection establish karna ya connected MCP server se available tools ki list maangna.

Kyunki MCP ek protocol hai, MCP khud sirf yeh require karta hai ki client aur server ke beech communication bidirectional ho. Implementation transports ke dwara handle ki jati hai, jo client/server communication ke underlying details ko handle karne ke liye responsible hote hain, jaise connections maintain karna aur established communication channel par messages pass karna. MCP do default transports ke saath aata hai: Streamable HTTP, jo remote MCP servers se connections allow karta hai, aur standard input/output (stdio), jo local MCP servers ke liye use hota hai. Users apne transports bhi implement kar sakte hain, jo existing MCP SDKs me plug kiye ja sakte hain. Transports ke baare me aap Chapter 8 me aur seekhenge.

Teeno problems ek saath

In teeno problems ko ek saath dekho to MCP ki picture saaf hoti hai. Pehle, integrations banana mushkil aur repetitive tha. Doosra, bane hue integrations ko share karna mushkil tha. Teesra, agent aur tool ke beech baatchit ka koi standard tareeka nahi tha. MCP teeno ko ek saath solve karta hai: server ek common interface deta hai, integrations ko application code se alag karta hai, aur transports ke through two-way communication ka standard deta hai. Isi liye MCP sirf ek aur library nahi hai, balki ek protocol hai jo poori ecosystem ko ek saath laata hai.

02.2Chapter 2 · An Introduction to the Model Context Protocol

MCP architecture — host, client, server, transport

MCP ki architecture me teen bade components hain — client, server aur transport — aur unke upar host application baithi hoti hai. Yeh design LSP se inspired hai, lekin MCP zyada general hai aur local aur remote dono servers support karta hai.

LSP se MCP tak — design ki jad

MCP ek client/server architecture follow karta hai, jisme ek client application jaise IDE ya chat agent ek local ya remote server se connect karke uske saath messages exchange kar sakta hai. LSP ka design is architecture ko samajhne ke liye ek acha introduction deta hai. LSP se pehle, language-specific IDEs common the, kyunki language support har language ke liye alag se banana padta tha — M × N problem ka ek aur classic example.

LSP ne is problem ko solve kiya, host applications ko alag processes me chal rahe language servers se ek standard JSON-RPC communication interface ke through communicate karne diya. Yeh host application ke saath included client code se kiya jata tha, jo language servers se connections manage karta tha, aur servers jo alag processes ke roop me launch aur run hote the. Language servers host application ko us language ke liye additional capabilities dete the, ek universal messaging language aur format ka use karke.

LSP aur MCP me farak

MCP ki architecture LSP se bahut milti-julti hai: host applications, client software jo servers se connections manage karta hai, servers jo host application ko additional capabilities dete hain, aur ek JSON-RPC communication layer. Lekin MCP me significant differences bhi hain. LSP IDEs ki capabilities extend karne par focus karta hai, jabki MCP is baat me zyada agnostic hai ki kis tarah ki host application use use karti hai. MCP use karne ki ek hi soft requirement hai: host application ko kisi na kisi tareeke se agentic hona chahiye, lekin technically kuch bhi aapko non-agentic host system me use karne se nahi rokta.

LSP me servers aam taur par host application ke local processes ke roop me run hote hain — jab aap apna IDE start karte ho, to aapke language servers bhi aapki machine par start ho jate hain. MCP, doosri taraf, local aur remote dono servers support karta hai. Jab user Claude Desktop jaise host application me ek local server add karta hai, to woh ek server definition add karta hai jisme server start karne ka command aur start-time parameters hote hain. Messages ek local transport layer, aam taur par stdio, par bheje jate hain. Remote servers, doosri taraf, ek URL se define hote hain aur aksar kisi form ki authentication support karte hain, jaise API keys ya OAuth tokens, aur JSON-RPC messages pass karne ke liye Streamable HTTP jaise remote transport layers ka use karte hain.

Host application aur MCP client

Host applications technically MCP architecture ka hissa nahi hain, lekin MCP use karne ke liye zaroori hain. Host applications woh applications hain jo ek MCP client host karti hain aur MCP servers se interact karke apni capabilities extend karti hain. Host applications kuch bhi ho sakti hain — koi restrictions nahi hain. Common types me IDEs, Claude Desktop jaise chatbot applications, agents banane ke frameworks, aur Warp AI jaise AI-powered terminals aate hain.

Clients host application ka hissa hote hain aur MCP servers se connections manage karne ke saath-saath LLM se requests ko appropriate server tak route karne aur wapas LLM tak pahunchane ke liye responsible hote hain. Ek client instance ek single server ke saath one-to-one connection maintain karta hai, host application aur server ke beech messages relay karta hai. Clients decide kar sakte hain ki server ki kaunsi features host application aur LLM tak pahunche. Kuch clients sirf server ke tools ko use karne dete hain, chahe server ke saare building blocks — tools, prompts aur resources — available hon, jabki kuch saare building blocks ko use karne dete hain.

Book me ek note me saaf kiya gaya hai ki kuch sources kisi bhi application ko jo MCP clients ke dwara provide kiya gaya context consume karti hain, use client kehte hain, aur kuch contexts me yeh valid usage hai. Lekin kyunki yeh book code par heavily focused hai, isme client ko do distinct concepts me alag kiya gaya hai: host application aur MCP client. Host application MCP client code ko host karti hai aur LLM se interact karke apne users ko functionality deti hai. LLM ke saath interaction point ke bahar, baaki application code MCP client ki presence se completely agnostic ho sakta hai. MCP client, phir, host application ke andar woh specific code hai jo MCP servers se connect karta hai aur unse communicate karta hai.

Client ki extra features — sampling, roots, elicitation

Clients servers ko kuch features bhi provide karte hain, jo unki functionality ko augment karte hain. Yeh features hain sampling, roots aur elicitation. Sampling ek server ko host application ke language model ko calls karne deta hai. Isse servers apne tools ke andar complex, AI-enabled workflows provide kar sakte hain, aur user decide kar sakta hai ki tool kaunsi jaankari consume kare. Example ke liye, report generation socho: ek MCP server ke paas organization ke sales data ke database ki access hai. Aap apni application ko prompt kar sakte ho ki pichle chhe mahine ki sales ki report banaye. Application sales reporting tool ko call karegi, jo database se raw data retrieve karegi, phir use server me stored templates aur ek aur prompt ke saath client ko wapas bhejegi, jo host LLM ko batata hai ki prompt, raw data aur report template dekhkar report generate kare.

Roots clients ko filesystem ke specific parts mark karne dete hain, jin tak connected server ki access hoti hai. Yeh kai workflows me useful ho sakte hain, jaise automatically ek server ki access ko ek specific project directory tak restrict karna, ya users ko specific files aur directories select karne dena taaki woh application aur is tarah kisi bhi connected server ko available ho sakein. Yeh servers ko filesystem context dene ka ek powerful tareeka hai, lekin yeh malicious server ke blast radius ko limit karne ka secure tareeka nahi hai. Iska reason yeh hai ki MCP specification sirf yeh kehti hai ki servers ko client ke dwara diye gaye roots ko respect karna chahiye, lekin yeh require nahi karti. Yeh shayad un servers ke liye compatibility feature hai jo filesystem access nahi karte, lekin roots ke ignorable hone se woh proper access control system ka poor substitute ban jate hain.

Elicitations MCP client feature set me relatively naye hain. Elicitations purpose me sampling jaisi hain: jahan sampling server ko host application ke language model ko call karne deti hai, wahin elicitations server ko client ke through host application me wapas reach karke user se input maangne deti hain. Iska matlab hai ki servers, jab clients se connect hote hain jo is feature ko support karte hain, sirf complex LLM-powered workflows hi nahi, balki aise workflows bhi bana sakte hain jinme human feedback shaamil ho, jo host applications ko aur zyada flexibility aur out-of-the-box functionality deta hai — bas shart yeh hai ki application ka client aur host application dono is feature ko support karein. Host application kyun chahiye? Kyunki elicitations ko user se jaankari communicate karne aur retrieve karne ke liye kisi UI ki zaroorat hoti hai, jo MCP client akele nahi kar sakta.

Ek important tip yeh hai ki sampling aur roots dono is likhne ke samay deprecate hone ki process me hain. Woh kam se kam July 2027 tak support kiye jayenge, lekin un par specification level ya SDK level par koi additional kaam nahi hoga.

MCP server — teen building blocks

Servers MCP architecture ka sabse visible hissa hain. LSP me servers ki capabilities aam taur par language specific hoti thi — code completion, documentation tool tips aur aisi cheezein. MCP me servers ko host application ke local run karne ki zaroorat nahi hoti, aur servers ke paas capabilities ki bahut zyada broad range hoti hai. Yeh capabilities aam taur par teen categories me aati hain: actions, data aur language model prompts. Yeh teen categories teen major MCP server building blocks se match karti hain: tools, resources aur prompts.

  • Tools — actions: self-contained functions jinhe host application ka language model remote procedure call ke through call kar sakta hai. Inke naam aur descriptions LLM ko client ke through diye jate hain, aur user prompt ke basis par LLM decide kar sakta hai ki tool call karna hai ya nahi. Agar tool call kiya jata hai, to woh wahin run hoga jahan MCP server run ho raha hai, aur results client aur application ko wapas bheje jayenge. Tools MCP servers me sabse common building block hain, kyunki application ki capabilities ko augment karne ka sabse versatile aur common tareeka uske actions ko expand karna hai.
  • Resources — data: text files, blob files jaise PDFs, database schemas, code documentation aur aur bhi bahut kuch. Agar tools MCP server ki grammar ke verbs hain, to resources nouns hain. Resources ko seedha LLM ko aur context dene ke liye use kiya ja sakta hai, ya tools ke dwara data par operate karne ke liye, ya LLM calls ke size aur cost ko reduce karne ke liye ek cache ke roop me bhi.
  • Prompts — language model prompts: woh prompts jo host application apne LLM se interact karne ke liye use kar sakti hai. Yeh sampling se bahut similar lag sakta hai, lekin dono ka purpose bahut alag hai. Sampling server ko host application ke LLM ko seedha call karne deti hai, jabki server-provided prompts application ya user ke control me hote hain: woh decide kar sakta hai ki server ke diye gaye prompts ko kab aur kaise use karna hai. Yeh useful hote hain jab server kisi specific service ya application ke liye bana ho aur builders use itni achi tarah jaante hon ki unhone us service ke saath interact karne ke liye tested aur optimized prompts bana liye hon.

Building blocks ke alawa, MCP servers utilities bhi provide karte hain jo server development aur debugging me madad karte hain. LSP ko ek strong nod dete hue, MCP servers ek completions capability provide kar sakte hain, jo prompts aur resources ke liye users ko autocompletion suggestions deti hai. MCP servers logging capabilities bhi implement kar sakte hain, jo clients ko connected server se structured logs receive aur filter karne deti hain. Aakhri server utility hai pagination — agar aapne web APIs ya databases ke saath kaam kiya hai to aapne ise pehle bhi dekha hoga. Pagination servers ko response ka ek subset requesting client ko wapas karne deti hai, saath me ek token jo overall response data me current position ko represent karta hai. Yeh bade datasets ke saath performance improve karne me madad kar sakta hai, local aur remote dono jagah. Logging bhi deprecate hone ki process me hai, lekin kam se kam July 2027 tak support ki jayegi.

Transport — communication layer

Transports MCP ki communication layer implement karte hain. Basic level par, woh client aur server ke beech messages bhejne aur receive karne ke liye responsible hote hain. MCP SDKs do default transports ke saath aate hain: local connections ke liye stdio aur remote connections ke liye Streamable HTTP. Yeh sabse commonly used transports hain, lekin protocol custom transports ki implementation bhi allow karta hai, jo un use cases ko support kar sakte hain jinme default transports kam suited hon, bas shart yeh hai ki underlying communication channel bidirectional message passing allow karta ho.

Book me ek note hai ki jab aap client ya server bana rahe ho, to aap ek hi transport use karne tak limited nahi ho. Multiple transports support karke aap apne users ko flexibility dete ho ki woh apne use case ke liye best transport choose karein. Anthropic strongly recommend karta hai ki stdio transport hamesha support kiya jaye, aur aap Streamable HTTP transport ka support add kar sakte ho agar aap remote server deploy karne ya apni application me remote servers add karne ka support dene ka plan rakhte ho.

Transports ka main functionality, halanki, connections manage karna aur messages handle karna hai. Chahe koi bhi transport use ho, client aur server ke beech bheje gaye messages hamesha JSON-RPC messages hote hain. Iska matlab hai ki transport messages ko us format me load karne ke liye responsible hai jo client aur server samajh sakein, jo built-in transports khud handle karte hain. MCP me teen main types ke messages hote hain: requests, responses aur notifications. Requests 2026-07-28 specification se pehle client ya server dono se bheje ja sakte the, aur us specification version se sirf client se bheje ja sakte hain. Requests connected entity se koi action initiate karne ke liye use hote hain. Responses requests ke replies hote hain, aur inme ya to operation ka result hota hai ya error information hoti hai agar operation fail ho gaya ho. Notifications one-way messages hote hain aur client ya server dono se bheje ja sakte hain, aam taur par receiver ko state me change ke baare me notify karte hue.

Transports ko ek security boundary ke roop me sochna chahiye, aur agar aapki security needs built-in transports se zyada hain, to apna transport banana ek acha option hai. Aap apna transport tab bhi bana sakte ho jab aap MCP ko kisi existing system se integrate kar rahe ho jo pehle se koi communication protocol ya messaging system use kar raha ho. Transports ki structure aur messages ke baare me aap Chapter 8 me aur seekhenge.

SOURCESource: AI Agents with MCP, O'Reilly, Chapter 2 — An Introduction to the Model Context Protocol

02.3Chapter 2 · An Introduction to the Model Context Protocol

Connection lifecycle aur two-way communication

Pehle MCP connection ke teen phases hote the — initialization, operation aur shutdown. Naye stateless model me initialization phase khatam ho gaya hai, lekin har request me version aur capabilities bheji jati hain.

Purana lifecycle — 2026-07-28 se pehle

2026-07-28 specification se pehle, connection lifecycle teen major phases me batta tha, aur har phase ka naam hi batata tha ki usme kya hota hai. Pehla phase tha Initialization: client aur server messages exchange karte the taaki yeh establish ho sake ki kaunsi protocol versions compatible hain, supported capabilities ko share aur negotiate kiya ja sake, aur koi bhi implementation details share ki ja sakein jo connection ke liye relevant hon.

Doosra phase tha Operation: yeh main loop hai jahan sab kuch hota hai. Initialization phase se negotiated capabilities ke basis par, client server ko ek request bhejta hai, aur server ek response ke saath reply karta hai, jisme requested operation ke results ya error ho sakta hai agar failure hua ho. Teesra phase tha Shutdown: client protocol connection ko terminate karta hai, aur transport layer is termination ko server tak communicate karne ke liye responsible hota hai.

Naya lifecycle — fully stateless model

2026-07-28 specification ke fully stateless connection model me transition ke baad, yeh lifecycle poori tarah badal gaya hai, jabki har phase me kai wahi features bane hue hain. Initialization phase khatam ho gaya hai. Iske bajay, protocol version compatibility har request me client aur server dwara bheji jati hai, aur capabilities client dwara har request ke saath server ko bheji jati hain, jabki server ko ek server/discover endpoint implement karna hota hai jise client up front compatibility check karne ke liye call kar sakta hai. Yeh strictly necessary nahi hai, kyunki server un capabilities ke liye requests ko bas reject kar sakta hai jo uske paas nahi hain.

Shutdown abhi bhi exist karta hai, lekin Streamable HTTP servers ke liye ab koi durable connection close karne ke liye nahi hota; client bas server ko POST messages bhejna band kar deta hai. Agar aap apne client ya server ke liye built-in transports use kar rahe ho, to connection lifecycle lagbhag poori tarah aapke liye manage kar liya jata hai, aur yeh kam important ho jata hai. Iske bajay, aap apni pasand ki language ke SDK dwara provide kiye gaye appropriate built-in session manager se connect aur disconnect karne par focus kar sakte ho.

Two-way communication kaise kaam karta hai

MCP isliye design kiya gaya hai taaki communication do-tarfah ho. Servers sirf host application aur LLM ko jaankari bhej nahi sakte, balki unse jaankari receive bhi kar sakte hain. Yeh zaroori hai kyunki dono parties ko aksar basic tasks ke liye ek doosre ko data bhejna padta hai — jaise connection establish karna ya available tools ki list maangna. Protocol khud sirf yeh require karta hai ki communication bidirectional ho; implementation transports handle karte hain, jo connections maintain karte hain aur messages pass karte hain.

Messages teen types ke hote hain. Requests kisi action ko initiate karte hain — purane spec me client ya server dono bhej sakte the, naye spec se sirf client bhej sakta hai. Responses requests ke replies hote hain, jinme result ya error hota hai. Notifications one-way messages hote hain, jinme koi response nahi chahiye hota — jaise state me change ki khabar dena. Client aur server dono notifications bhej sakte hain, aur receiver unhe jaise chahe handle kar sakta hai.

Authorization transport layer par

Protocol transport layer par authorization bhi enable karta hai, aur jo transport developers authorization include karna chahte hain, unhe OAuth 2.1 authorization support implement karna required hai. Clients ke liye authorization implement karna Chapter 4 me cover hoga, aur servers ke liye Chapter 7 me. Yeh ek important point hai: security protocol ke andar ek afterthought nahi hai, balki transport layer par hi built-in hai, taaki remote servers ko safely expose kiya ja sake.

Protocol utilities — cancellation, ping, progress

Base protocol me kuch common utilities bhi hain jo client aur server dono use kar sakte hain, aam taur par connection ki state ke baare me feedback lene ya use badalne ke liye. Pehli utility hai cancellation: yeh client ya server se ek notification message ke roop me aati hai, jisme request ID aur cancellation ka reason hota hai, aur iska use un requests ko cancel karne ke liye hota hai jo abhi bhi work ho rahi hain.

2026-07-28 specification release se pehle, ping ek parameterless JSON-RPC message ke roop me available tha, jo client ya server dono se bheja ja sakta tha taaki check kiya ja sake ki connection abhi bhi alive hai ya nahi. Fully stateless connections ki taraf move ke saath, yeh ab support nahi kiya jata, halanki legacy servers aur clients abhi bhi ise support kar sakte hain. Aakhir me, progress reporting bhi protocol level par available hai, aur yeh clients ya servers ko user ko ek accurate progress bar dikhane deta hai jo kisi bhi operation ki progress communicate karta hai. In sabke baare me aap Chapter 6 me aur seekhenge.

Ek note me bataya gaya hai ki agar aap task cancellation, pings aur progress reports use karna chahte ho, to aapko ensure karna hoga ki client aur server dono unhe support karte hon. Legacy clients aur servers ke liye, yeh connection process ke dauraan automatically establish ho jata hai, jabki modern ones ke liye jo sirf stateless connections support karte hain, mutual compatibility client ke dwara server ko server/discover message bhejkar aur use apni list se compare karke establish ki ja sakti hai.

SOURCESource: AI Agents with MCP, O'Reilly, Chapter 2 — An Introduction to the Model Context Protocol
