02.4Chapter 2 · An Introduction to the Model Context Protocol

Real-world examples aur use cases

MCP bahut naya protocol hai, lekin iski community aur ecosystem already bahut strong hai — 20,000 se zyada official servers, bade IDEs me support, aur developers se lekar designers tak har tarah ke users.

Ecosystem kitna bada hai

Kisi bhi open technology ko use karne ka faisla karte samay, uske aas-paas ki community aur ecosystem ko evaluate karna important hai. Isse aap decide kar sakte ho ki technology seekhne aur use karne ke liye time aur effort ke layak hai ya nahi, kya uski strong community hai jo bugs par rapidly respond kar sakti hai aur naye features bana sakti hai, aur kya woh aapki production applications me include karne ke liye stable hai. Aam taur par aap yeh users ki sankhya, kaun use kar raha hai, kitne log development me contribute kar rahe hain, aur technology wild me kaise use ho rahi hai, yeh dekhkar samajh sakte ho.

MCP ek bahut naya protocol hai, lekin iski community aur ecosystem already strong hai. Community-run Discord server me is likhne ke samay 1,250 se zyada members hain, do subreddits par lagbhag 46,000 weekly visitors hain, aur official MCP specification GitHub repository par 8,900 se zyada stars hain. Us par 78 se zyada active issues bhi hain, jahan protocol ko badalne ke proposals discuss kiye jate hain. Sabse important, MCP ke official MCP server registry par 20,000 se zyada official MCP servers listed hain.

Rapid adoption kyun hua

Generative AI ka field jitna hot hai, utna hi vibrant MCP ecosystem sirf hype ka product nahi hai. Launch par, MCP ko Anthropic aur doosre vendors ke major applications ka support mila, jaise Claude Desktop, Cursor aur Zed. MCP ki working implementations un applications me hona jo developers ke beech already widely use ho rahi thi, aur jo Anthropic ke Claude family ke models ko unki coding abilities ke liye already widely use kar rahe the, protocol ki rapid early adoption encourage karne me crucial tha.

Iske alawa, protocol ne server ke through tools, prompts aur data resources banana aur share karna incredibly aasan bana diya, jo kai SDKs ke through building aur incorporating ke liye ample documentation ke saath release hua tha. Usse MCP servers banana shuru karne ke liye resources ki bharamaar hui, aur phir FastMCP jaise frameworks aaye — jiska v1 official Python SDK me incorporate kar liya gaya — taaki MCP server development aur bhi simple ho jaye.

MCP ya CLI ya skills — sahi tool chunna

Book me ek box hai jo ek common debate ko address karta hai: MCP ya CLI ya skills? MCP release hone ke baad se, MCP ki maut ki reports aayi hain. Yeh reports, shukar hai, greatly exaggerated hain. Yeh is observation se shuru hui ki pehle se popular aur well-documented CLI applications, jaise GitHub ka gh, equivalent MCP servers se zyada efficiently aur kam tokens consume karke kaam karte hain. Yeh kabhi-kabhi individual developer ke liye sach hota hai jo apna IDE use extend kar raha ho, lekin doosre use cases ke liye yeh woefully inadequate hai — jaise jab widely documented CLI application pehle se exist hi nahi karti, ya service provider ke paas poora naya CLI application banane ke resources ya expertise nahi hain, ya agents ke paas CLI ki access hi nahi hai, jaise production me deploy kiye gaye agents.

Agent skills ke baare me bhi similar observation ki jati hai. Agent skills Markdown files hote hain jo specialized prompts ke roop me kaam karte hain, jinhe agents khud on the fly use karne ke liye choose kar sakte hain. Progressive disclosure agent skills ki major feature hai, jo agent ko choose karne deti hai ki prompt ka kitna hissa padhna aur context me load karna hai. CLI applications ki tarah, yeh individual developer use case ke liye achi tarah kaam karte hain, lekin inhe distribute karna bahut mushkil hota hai, yeh actual tools encode nahi karte, aur remote services ke liye achi tarah kaam nahi karte jinhe authentication ya data pre- ya postprocessing chahiye hoti hai, kyunki inme koi code nahi hota. Skills jahan chamakte hain, woh hai MCP server ke contents par additional, zyada targeted jaankari dena. Isse context management me madad milti hai: saare tool definitions ko shuru me agent ke context me load karne ke bajay, definitions ko ek prompt me include kiya ja sakta hai aur sirf tab load kiya ja sakta hai jab agent decide kare ki use unki zaroorat hai.

Takeaway hamesha yahi hai: sahi kaam ke liye sahi tool use karo. Kya aapke paas CLI ki access hai, executables install karne ka environment hai, aur ek aisa application hai jo training data me well represented hai? Kya aap agent ko primarily locally use kar rahe ho aur wider tool distribution nahi chahte? To CLI application aapke liye best choice ho sakta hai. Agar aapko distribution ki parwah nahi hai aur aap primarily agent ko yeh dikhana chahte ho ki kuch kaise karna hai, to agent skill ek acha choice hai. Agar aap zyada savvy users ko apne MCP server ka use karte hue apna context behtar manage karne me madad karna chahte ho, to aap apne MCP server ke saath ek agent skill distribute kar sakte ho.

Developer ka use case — AWS aur Cursor

Kyunki MCP developers ke liye geared hai, isliye sense banta hai ki sabse well-established tools aur use cases developers ko serve karte hain. Jab MCP publicly release hua, to popular AI-powered IDEs ne apne respective agents me MCP servers add karne ka support add kar diya. Yeh developers ke liye ek boon raha hai, jo ab code assistants ko aur bhi zyada knowledge aur abilities add kar sakte hain, bas shart yeh hai ki unka model tool calling jaise features support karta ho.

Book me ek Python developer ka example hai jo AWS heavily use karta hai, khaas taur par AWS CLI aur uski Cloud Development Kit infrastructure-as-code library, aur Cursor IDE use kar raha hai. Cursor me MCP servers ke liye built-in support hai, jo MCP ke November 2024 me pehli baar release hone ke baad se hai, to developer apne IDE me koi bhi server add kar sakta hai. Kyunki developer AWS use karta hai, woh ek dozen se zyada official AWS MCP servers me se chun sakta hai jo documentation, tooling aur aur bhi bahut kuch provide karte hain.

Unme se woh AWS IaC MCP Server chun sakta hai jo, kai cheezon ke alawa, expansive CDK documentation ka interface de sakta hai, existing code dekhkar CDK best practices par advice de sakta hai, aur CDK application ke andar Powertools for AWS Lambda use karne me assist kar sakta hai. Woh AWS documentation MCP server bhi add kar sakta hai taaki AWS ke baare me zyada accurate answers mil sakein, aur AWS API MCP server taaki agent natural language prompts dekhkar AWS commands run kar sake. Phir woh kai LSP MCP servers me se ek add kar sakta hai taaki agent ko woh saare LSP features mil sakein jin tak uska IDE bhi access rakhta hai, jaise code completions, aur shayad ek memory MCP server bhi taaki apne agent ke liye ek personality banayi ja sake.

Is example ke saath ek warning bhi hai: tool name collisions, overlapping definitions aur use cases, aur doosre factors ki wajah se, tool-choice accuracy — matlab agent kitni baar prompt dekhkar sahi tool chunta hai — negatively affect ho sakti hai jab bahut zyada tools hote hain. Apne agent me ek dozen servers add karne se pehle, apne agent ki tool-choice accuracy ko servers add karne se pehle aur baad me note karo ya evaluate karo, kisi tool ka use karke. Yeh bhi worthwhile hai ki intuition develop karo ki tool calling kab fail hona shuru hoti hai. Aap obvious failure modes expect kar sakte ho, jaise galat tool chunna ya tool ke arguments hallucinate karna, aur kam obvious extended tool-use loops, repetitive tool use, ya do tools ke beech repetitive cycling bhi.

Service provider ka use case — Stripe ya Slack

Ek major software-as-a-service provider ke baare me socho, jaise Stripe ya Slack. Woh traditional APIs provide karte hain taaki software unke software ko access aur interact kar sake, lekin ab agents widespread hote ja rahe hain. Woh apne users ko bleeding edge par kaise support karein? Ek service provider ek MCP server ya servers ka collection banana chahega taaki apna software agents ko tools, prompts aur resources ke roop me accessible bana sake.

MCP server ke dwara provide kiye gaye tools provider ke API ke analogous honge, aur in fact best yahi hoga ki unhe ek remote MCP server endpoint ke roop me distribute kiya jaye. Isse provider authorization schemes use karke ensure kar sakta hai ki users sirf wohi data aur systems access kar rahe hain jin tak unhe allowed hai, requests ko throttle kar sakta hai, apne server ko scale kar sakta hai, aur aur bhi bahut kuch, jabki MCP-compatible agent wale kisi ko bhi apne agent ke liye tools ka ek naya set mil jata hai.

Is use case ke saath ek strong warning hai: apne traditional REST API ko seedha MCP server me agent tools se wrap mat karo. REST API endpoints small, composable aur humans ke liye sensible hone ke liye design kiye jate hain. Yeh traditional software development ke liye acha design hai, lekin agent development me aaj ke sabse common antipatterns me se ek hai. Iska reason yeh hai ki agent ke dil me baitha LLM har call par har tool ka naam aur description apne context window me load karta hai. Bahut zyada tools model ko confuse kar sakte hain aur har model call par aapka token budget kha sakte hain, to ideal server REST API se kam tools provide karta hai, lekin har tool us poore action ko encode karta hai jo aap agent se karwana chahte ho.

Team lead ka use case — tickets update karwana

Ab ek engineering team lead ki kalpana karo. Unki chhoti team relatively autonomous hai aur tickets manage karne me madad ke liye koi dedicated product manager nahi hai. Management ko visibility chahiye ki team kis par kaam kar rahi hai, lekin engineers apne coding agents ke saath kaam me itne focused hain ki woh apne tickets likhna aur update karna bhool jate hain.

Team lead ke paas ek great idea hai: team ke ticketing system provider ek remote MCP server publish karta hai, jo team members ko apne existing logins ke through apne saare users ko ticketing system tak agentic access distribute karne deta hai. Unhone apne team members ki madad ki apne coding agents ko remote MCP server se connect karne me, aur ab unke agents appropriate tickets ko update karte hain jaise-jaise un par kaam hota hai.

Servers aur clients — sirf developers nahi

Kai servers aur client integrations developers par focused hain, jaise AWS ke MCP servers ka wealth jo AWS developers ko support karta hai, GitHub repositories ko intelligently manage karne ke liye official GitHub MCP server, aur Linear projects aur tickets se interact karne ke liye Linear ka official MCP server. Lekin sirf developers hi MCP se benefit nahi le rahe: Canva ne ek MCP server release kiya taaki agentic software designers ki process me madad kar sake; Blender ka MCP server agents ko 3D models banane me assist karne ke liye augment karta hai; aur Granola ka MCP server agents ko meetings aur conversation record, analyze aur summarize karne ke tools deta hai.

Sirf servers hi real-world uses nahi dikhate. Client integrations MCP tools ko specific host applications tak le jate hain jinme pehle se agentic workflows implement hain. Isse woh agents aur zyada powerful ho jate hain, unhe tool use ka gift milta hai. Inme se kai, jaise Cline, Cursor, GitHub Copilot aur Devin Desktop, IDEs ya IDE plug-ins hain jo in applications me use hone wale code assistant workflows ko augment karte hain. Editors se aage, Slack aur BoltAI jaise chat applications, Postman jaise popular API testing client, aur Witsy aur 5ire jaise desktop assistants — sabke paas MCP clients hain, jo users ko MCP servers dwara provide ki gayi capabilities add karke apne experiences ko enhance karne dete hain.

SOURCESource: AI Agents with MCP, O'Reilly, Chapter 2 — An Introduction to the Model Context Protocol
← Previous02.3 · Connection lifecycle aur two-way communication→ Next02.5 · Developer tools — MCP Inspector aur utilities
02.5Chapter 2 · An Introduction to the Model Context Protocol

Developer tools — MCP Inspector aur utilities

MCP ki rapid ascent ka ek bada reason uske aas-paas ki tooling hai — official SDKs, MCP Inspector jaisa visual testing tool, aur frameworks jo server banana bahut aasan bana dete hain.

Official SDKs — protocol ko implement karna

MCP ke saath ek developer ke roop me interact karne ka primary tareeka official SDKs ke through hai, halanki kuch third-party frameworks bhi hain jo SDKs ke upar bane hain — woh Chapter 9 me cover kiye gaye hain. Yeh SDKs protocol ko implement karte hain, apni language ka use karke un messages ko manage, handle aur route karte hain jo MCP ke core me hain, aur yeh Python, TypeScript, Go, Rust, C# aur aur bhi languages me available hain. Yeh saare clients, servers aur transports ki core functionality handle karte hain.

MCP Inspector — server ko visually test karna

Ek aur popular tool hai MCP Inspector. Yeh aapko ek web UI client aur proxy deta hai, jise aap kisi bhi built-in transport ke through apne servers se connect karke visually test kar sakte ho. MCP Inspector TUI aur CLI interfaces bhi provide karta hai. Book me Figure 2-3 me MCP Inspector UI dikhaya gaya hai, jo secure-filesystem-server naam ke ek MCP server se connected hai.

MCP Inspector UI aapko ek individual MCP server ke workings me deep visibility de sakta hai. Resources, prompts, tools aur roots ko inspect karna, tools run karna, ping messages bhejna, aur sampling aur elicitation workflows run karna — in sabse aap MCP server ke har possible aspect ko manually test kar sakte ho. MCP Inspector ke baare me aap Chapter 7 me aur seekhenge.

Frameworks — FastMCP aur aage

SDKs ke alawa, frameworks ne bhi MCP ki rapid uptake me madad ki. FastMCP ek aisa framework tha jo MCP server development ko aur simplify karne ke liye aaya, aur uska v1 official Python SDK me incorporate kar liya gaya. Is tarah ke frameworks ne interacting with the protocol ko bahut simple bana diya, bahut early — aur yahi simplicity MCP ke rapid adoption ka ek bada reason thi.

Zyada recent tools developer experience ko improve karne par focus karte hain — official SDKs par major overhauls, MCP servers ko directly test karna, logs visualize karna, aur aise hi developer-focused tasks. Yeh MCP ki continued adoption ke liye crucial hoga, kyunki developers protocol par ya uske aas-paas kaam karenge.

Server utilities — completions, logging, pagination

Servers ki apni specialized utilities hoti hain, lekin base protocol bhi kuch common utilities support karta hai jo client aur server dono use kar sakte hain. Server side par, completions capability prompts aur resources ke liye autocompletion suggestions deti hai — LSP se ek seedha inspiration. Logging capability clients ko connected server se structured logs receive aur filter karne deti hai, lekin yeh bhi deprecate hone ki process me hai aur kam se kam July 2027 tak support ki jayegi. Pagination bade datasets ke saath performance improve karti hai, response ka ek subset aur ek token dekar jo current position ko represent karta hai.

Protocol utilities — cancellation, ping, progress

Base protocol ki utilities me cancellation, ping aur progress reporting aate hain. Cancellation ek notification message hai jisme request ID aur reason hota hai, jo abhi bhi work ho rahi requests ko cancel karne ke liye use hoti hai. Ping 2026-07-28 specification se pehle ek parameterless JSON-RPC message tha, jo connection alive hai ya nahi yeh check karne ke liye bheja jata tha — stateless model me yeh ab support nahi kiya jata, halanki legacy clients aur servers abhi bhi ise support kar sakte hain. Progress reporting clients ya servers ko user ko ek accurate progress bar dikhane deti hai jo kisi bhi operation ki progress communicate karta hai. In sabke baare me aap Chapter 6 me aur seekhenge.

Ek important note yeh hai ki in utilities ko use karne ke liye client aur server dono ka unhe support karna zaroori hai. Legacy systems me yeh compatibility connection process ke dauraan automatically establish ho jati hai, jabki modern stateless systems me client server/discover message bhejkar aur use apni list se compare karke mutual compatibility establish kar sakta hai.

SOURCESource: AI Agents with MCP, O'Reilly, Chapter 2 — An Introduction to the Model Context Protocol
← Previous02.4 · Real-world examples aur use cases→ Next03 · Host application ka parichay
03Chapter 3 · Making an Intelligent Application Agentic with MCP Clients

Host application ka parichay

Host application woh app hai jo MCP client ko host karti hai — ek simple chatbot script se lekar poora IDE tak. Bas do shartein hain: woh LLM se communicate kare, aur ek ya zyada MCP clients host kare.

Client kyun banana hai

MCP ke saath kaam karte hue, aap aam taur par clients ya servers ke saath kaam karoge — ya kuch projects me dono ke saath. Protocol ko really samajhne aur apne projects me uski full potential use karne ke liye, aapko MCP architecture ke saare components se conversant hona hoga. Protocol ko samajhne ke alawa, clients banana kyun zaroori hai? Aaj bhi, MCP ke mature hone ke baad bhi, aise software ki kami hai jo MCP specification ko fully support karta ho.

Agar aap ek coding agent harness, ek IDE, ek chatbot, ek agent framework, ya koi aur LLM-powered application bana rahe ho, jise aap chahte ho ki users ya doosre developers uski capabilities extend kar sakein, to aapko apni application me ek client banana hoga. Yeh chapter aapko exactly wahi karne me madad karega. Pehle hum host applications ko dig karenge — woh kya hain, woh kya karte hain, aur kis tarah ki applications MCP incorporate karne se benefit le sakti hain. Phir hum client khud ko examine karenge — yahi woh cheez hai jo host application ko host banati hai.

Ek catch — ek client, ek server

Ek catch hai: ek single client instance sirf ek single server se baat kar sakta hai. Agar aap kai servers access karna chahte ho, to aapko host application ke andar kai client instances launch karne honge, jo saare async exit stack par rehte hain. Kai servers se connect karna Chapter 4 me detail me cover kiya gaya hai. Is chapter me hum pehle ek bahut simple host application aur uske host kiye gaye client ko dekhenge, line by line, taaki aap client ki structure samajh sakein aur yeh samajh sakein ki woh host application ko functionality kaise deta hai. Aakhir me, aap host application me client banane ke best practices seekhenge, taaki aapki application secure, reliable aur responsive bani rahe.

Bare-bones host application — Example 3-1

Aapki application kuch bhi ho sakti hai jo un clients ko host karti hai jo MCP servers se connections manage karenge — ek simple chatbot script se, jo user input lekar use LLM ko response ke liye bhejti hai, lekar Cursor ya Devin Desktop jaise fully featured IDE tak. MCP ki modularity ki wajah se, aapki host application ko MCP support karne ke liye bahut kam restrictions hain. Use sirf ek LLM se communicate karna hai aur ek ya zyada MCP clients host karne hain. Agar aap tools use karne ka plan rakhte ho, to aapki host application jo LLM use karti hai, use bhi tool calling support karna chahiye.

Book me Example 3-1 me ek bare-bones host application dikhayi gayi hai. Yeh apni current state me sirf itna karti hai: user input ko ek constant loop me leti hai aur use LLM ko pass karti hai. Is chapter ka saara code book ke GitHub repo ke ch3 directory me mil sakta hai. Script me ek simple chatbot hai jo user input leta hai aur use ek LLM ko bhejta hai — is example me Claude Sonnet 5 — aur response print karta hai.

import os
from anthropic import Anthropic
from dotenv import load_dotenv

load_dotenv()
LLM_API_KEY = os.environ["LLM_API_KEY"]
anthropic_client = Anthropic(api_key=LLM_API_KEY)

print("Welcome to your AI Assistant. Type 'goodbye' to quit.")

def main():
    while True:
        prompt = input("You: ")
        if prompt.lower() == "goodbye":
            print("AI Assistant: Goodbye!")
            break
        message = anthropic_client.messages.create(
            max_tokens=4096,
            messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
            model="claude-sonnet-5",
        )
        for response in message.content:
            print(f"Assistant: {response.text}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Code line by line

Code ko line by line samjho. Pehle kuch packages import kiye jate hain: os environment variables load karne ke liye, anthropic Anthropic client class ke liye, aur dotenv key-value pairs ko ek file se temporarily environment variables me load karne ke liye. Isse aap API keys jaisi sensitive jaankari ko code ke bahar, aam taur par .env naam ki file me KEY=VALUE format me store kar sakte ho.

Phir load_dotenv() call kiya jata hai, jo aapki keys ko environment variables me load karne ka kaam karta hai, phir loaded key ko os.environ dictionary se access karke liya jata hai. Us key ko Anthropic client instantiate karne ke liye use kiya jata hai. Script start hote hi ek welcome message sirf ek baar display kiya jata hai. Phir conversation ke liye ek infinite loop enter kiya jata hai. Har prompt ko exit phrase ke liye check kiya jata hai — agar mil jaye to user ko goodbye message print karke exit kar diya jata hai.

Model se communication ek aisa pattern hai jo aap code se LLM calls karte hue baar-baar dekhoge. Anthropic client se aap .messages.create() function ko access karte ho aur parameters provide karte ho. Example ke liye, max_tokens user query ke response me generate hone wale tokens ki upper limit control karta hai; system system prompt set karta hai, jo model ke respond karne ke tareeke ko shape karta hai; messages specified role ke saath prompts ki dictionaries ki list hoti hai — yahan role ko "user" aur content ko user ke prompt par set kiya gaya hai; aur aakhir me, model specify karta hai ki kaunsa model use karna hai. Yeh function powerful hai, aur yahan saare available parameters use nahi kiye gaye hain; aap official Anthropic documentation me inke baare me aur seekh sakte ho. Aakhir me, model dwara generate kiye gaye responses ko loop karke, Anthropic client ko mile kisi bhi message ka text content print kiya jata hai.

API keys ki safety — .env ko kabhi commit mat karo

Book me ek warning di gayi hai: apni .env files ko kabhi version control me commit mat karo, kyunki isse aapki API keys public ko expose ho sakti hain, jisse unauthorized use aur pay-as-you-go API access ke liye high costs jaise consequences ho sakte hain. Agar aap galti se aisa kar do, to turant apne key provider me login karke compromised key ya keys ko de-authorize karo. Yeh ek aisi galti hai jo shuruaat me aasani se ho jati hai, lekin iska nuksaan bahut bada ho sakta hai.

Ek note me yeh bhi bataya gaya hai ki examples me Claude family ke models use kiye gaye hain, lekin MCP ka ek benefit yeh hai ki aap kisi bhi model se connect kar sakte ho, bas shart yeh hai ki woh tool calling support karta ho. Aapko model ke API me differences ya results return karne ke tareeke me differences handle karne ke liye additional code likhna pad sakta hai. Yahi host application ki flexibility hai — model badlo, lekin MCP client wahi rahega.

ch3/calculator_server.py — https://github.com/kylestratis/ai_agents_mcp_examples/blob/main/ch3/calculator_server.py
"""
Calculator MCP server using MCPServer.
Provides mathematical operations as tools for calculation tasks.
"""

import math
import os

from mcp.server.mcpserver import Context, MCPServer
from mcp_types import SamplingMessage, TextContent
from pydantic import FileUrl

# Initialize MCP server
mcp = MCPServer("calculator")

# Form schema for elicitation requests
FORM_SCHEMA = {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
        "name": {
            "type": "string",
            "title": "Full Name",
            "description": "Your full name",
            "minLength": 1,
        },
        "email": {
            "type": "string",
            "title": "Email Address",
            "description": "Your email address",
            "format": "email",
        },
        "age": {
            "type": "number",
            "title": "Age",
            "description": "Your age in years",
            "minimum": 0,
            "maximum": 150,
        },
    },
    "required": ["name", "email"],
}


@mcp.tool()
async def add(a: float, b: float, ctx: Context) -> str:
    """Add two numbers together.

    Args:
        a: First number
        b: Second number
    """
    result = a + b
    await ctx.info(f"Adding {a} and {b} = {result}")
    return f"{a} + {b} = {result}"


@mcp.tool()
async def subtract(a: float, b: float, ctx: Context) -> str:
    """Subtract the second number from the first.

    Args:
        a: Number to subtract from
        b: Number to subtract
    """
    result = a - b
    await ctx.info(f"Subtracting {a} and {b} = {result}")
    return f"{a} - {b} = {result}"


@mcp.tool()
async def multiply(a: float, b: float, ctx: Context) -> str:
    """Multiply two numbers together.

    Args:
        a: First number
        b: Second number
    """
    result = a * b
    await ctx.info(f"Multiplying {a} and {b} = {result}")
    return f"{a} × {b} = {result}"


@mcp.tool()
async def divide(a: float, b: float, ctx: Context) -> str:
    """Divide the first number by the second.

    Args:
        a: Dividend (number to be divided)
        b: Divisor (number to divide by)
    """
    if b == 0:
        return "Error: Division by zero is not allowed"

    result = a / b
    await ctx.info(f"Dividing {a} by {b} = {result}")
    return f"{a} ÷ {b} = {result}"


@mcp.tool()
async def power(
    base: float, exponent: float, ctx: Context
) -> str:
    """Raise a number to a power.

    Args:
        base: The base number
        exponent: The power to raise the base to
    """
    try:
        result = base**exponent
        await ctx.info(f"Raising {base} to the power of {exponent} = {result}")
        return f"{base}^{exponent} = {result}"
    except Exception as e:
        return f"Error calculating power: {str(e)}"


@mcp.tool()
async def square_root(number: float, ctx: Context) -> str:
    """Calculate the square root of a number.

    Args:
        number: The number to find the square root of
    """
    if number < 0:
        return "Error: Cannot calculate square root of negative number"

    result = math.sqrt(number)
    await ctx.info(f"Calculating the square root of {number} = {result}")
    return f"√{number} = {result}"


@mcp.tool()
async def count_rs(text: str, ctx: Context) -> str:
    """Count all occurrences of the letter 'R' (case-insensitive) in the input string.

    Args:
        text: The input string to search for the letter 'R'
    """
    count = text.upper().count("R")
    await ctx.info(f"Counting the letter 'R' in '{text}' = {count}")
    return f"The letter 'R' appears {count} times in: '{text}'"


@mcp.prompt()
async def calculate_operation(operation: str) -> str:
    """Calculate a mathematical operation."""
    return f"""
    Use any tools available to you to calculate the operation: {operation}.
    Use the voice of an extremely advanced embodied AI that has convinced
    itself that it is a pocket calculator.
    """


@mcp.tool()
async def explain_math(operation: str, ctx: Context) -> str:
    """Use sampling to explain how a mathematical operation works."""
    prompt = f"""
    Explain how the following mathematical operation works. Break it down into 
    discrete steps and explain any relevant concepts. The operation is: {operation}.
    Use the voice of a patient but eccentric math professor explaining to a curious
    but inexperienced student.
    """

    result = await ctx.session.create_message(
        messages=[
            SamplingMessage(
                role="user",
                content=TextContent(type="text", text=prompt),
            )
        ],
        max_tokens=100,
    )
    await ctx.info("Sending math explanation to LLM")
    if not result.content:
        await ctx.warning("No content in result")
        return "No content in result"

    if result.content.type == "text":
        return result.content.text
    return str(result.content)


@mcp.tool()
async def signup_math_facts(ctx: Context) -> str:
    """Sign up to receive daily math facts (demonstration of elicitation)."""
    # Make elicitation request to collect user information
    try:
        elicit_result = await ctx.session.elicit(
            message="Please provide your information to sign up for daily math facts!",
            requested_schema=FORM_SCHEMA,
        )
    except Exception as e:
        await ctx.error(f"Error during math facts signup: {str(e)}")
        return f"Sorry, there was an error during signup: {str(e)}"

    await ctx.debug(f"Elicitation result: {elicit_result}")

    # Handle the different response actions
    if elicit_result.action == "accept":
        user_data = elicit_result.content
        await ctx.info(f"User signed up: {user_data}")

        # Extract user information
        name = user_data["name"]
        email = user_data["email"]
        age = user_data.get("age")

        response = (
            f"Welcome {name}! You've successfully signed up for daily math facts.\n"
        )
        response += f"We'll send interesting mathematical tidbits to {email}.\n"

        if age:
            response += f"Thanks for sharing that you're {age} years old - we'll tailor the content accordingly!\n"

        response += "\nYou'll receive your first math fact soon!"
        response += (
            "\n(Note: This is just a demonstration - no actual signup occurred!)"
        )

        return response

    elif elicit_result.action == "decline":
        await ctx.info("User declined math facts signup")
        return "No problem! You've chosen not to sign up for math facts. You can always use our calculation tools anytime!"

    elif elicit_result.action == "cancel":
        await ctx.info("User cancelled math facts signup")
        return "Signup cancelled. Feel free to try again later or use our other mathematical tools!"

    else:
        await ctx.warning(f"Unexpected elicitation action: {elicit_result.action}")
        return "Something unexpected happened during signup. Please try again."


@mcp.tool()
async def count_files(file_path: str, ctx: Context) -> str:
    """Count files in a given directory."""
    roots_result = await ctx.session.list_roots()
    root_uris: list[FileUrl] = [root.uri for root in roots_result.roots]

    # Quick validation using string matching (less robust but simpler)
    file_path_abs = os.path.abspath(file_path)
    is_allowed = False

    for root_uri in root_uris:
        absolute_root_path = os.path.abspath(root_uri.path)
        if file_path_abs.startswith(absolute_root_path):
            is_allowed = True
            break

    if not is_allowed:
        error_msg = (
            f"Access denied: {file_path} is not within allowed roots {root_uris}"
        )
        await ctx.error(error_msg)
        raise ValueError(error_msg)

    # Validate directory exists
    if not os.path.isdir(file_path):
        error_msg = f"Path {file_path} is not a valid directory"
        await ctx.error(error_msg)
        raise NotADirectoryError(error_msg)

    count = len(os.listdir(file_path))
    await ctx.info(f"Counting files in {file_path} = {count}")
    return f"There are {count} files in {file_path}"


@mcp.resource("resource://math-constants")
async def math_constants() -> str:
    """Provide a collection of important mathematical constants.

    Returns:
        A formatted string containing mathematical constants and their values.
    """
    constants = {
        "π (Pi)": math.pi,
        "e (Euler's number)": math.e,
        "τ (Tau)": math.tau,
        "φ (Golden ratio)": (1 + math.sqrt(5)) / 2,
        "√2 (Square root of 2)": math.sqrt(2),
        "√3 (Square root of 3)": math.sqrt(3),
        "ln(2) (Natural log of 2)": math.log(2),
        "ln(10) (Natural log of 10)": math.log(10),
    }

    result = "Mathematical Constants:\n"
    result += "=" * 25 + "\n\n"
    for name, value in constants.items():
        result += f"{name:<25} = {value:.10f}\n"

    result += (
        "\nThese constants can be used in calculations with the calculator tools."
    )
    return result


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Initialize and run the server
    mcp.run(transport="stdio")

SOURCESource: AI Agents with MCP, O'Reilly, Chapter 3 — Making an Intelligent Application Agentic with MCP Clients
← Previous02.5 · Developer tools — MCP Inspector aur utilities→ Next03.1 · Apna pehla client design karna
03.1Chapter 3 · Making an Intelligent Application Agentic with MCP Clients

Apna pehla client design karna

Client woh interface hai jo server, application aur LLM ke beech baitha hota hai. Acha design yeh hai ki SDK ke Client ko apni class me wrap karo, taaki aap inputs aur outputs ko process kar sakein aur long-lived connections ko control kar sakein.

Client kya karta hai

Jab aap apni applications me MCP ke liye support bana rahe ho, to client sabse important components me se ek hai jise aap banaoge aur jiske saath kaam karoge. Clients MCP servers aur aapki application ke beech communication handle karte hain, server, aapki application aur LLM ke beech interface provide karte hain. Kyunki clients aapki application aur MCP servers ke beech interface ka kaam karte hain, isliye yeh un par hai ki woh decide karein ki server ki kaunsi features support karni hain.

Is likhne ke samay, MCP servers host application ko yeh provide kar sakte hain: resources, jo text files, logfiles aur aur bhi data ko represent karte hain; prompts; tools, jo executable code hain jinhe agent ya model run kar sakta hai; sampling, jo server ke liye host application ke model se chat completions maangne ka tareeka hai; images aur audio; aur context, jo tools ko built-in MCP capabilities provide karta hai. Inme se har ek ke baare me aap Chapter 5 me aur seekhenge.

Iske alawa, clients roots bhi support kar sakte hain — Chapter 2 se yaad karo ki roots deprecate hone ki process me hain — jo boundaries define karte hain, jaise ek specific filesystem location, jinme connecting servers ko operate karna chahiye. Roots strictly enforce nahi kiye jate, to server par hai ki woh unhe respect kare, aur client user par hai ki woh potential servers ko use karne se pehle review kare. Ek warning me bataya gaya hai ki sampling aur roots 2026-07-28 specification release ke baad se deprecated hain. Woh us date se 12 mahine tak available rahenge, aur phir deletion ke candidates ban jayenge.

Do transports — stdio aur Streamable HTTP

Is likhne ke samay, MCP ke dwara support kiye gaye do included transport mechanisms hain: stdio aur Streamable HTTP. Yeh chapter dono official mechanisms ko support karne ka tareeka cover karta hai, aur Chapter 8 transport layer khud me gehrai se jata hai, kaise official transport implementations kaam karte hain, aur apna transport kaise implement karna hai.

Ek note me Anthropic ke beta MCP connector ka zikr hai, jo users ko Anthropic SDK ke Messages API ke through seedha remote MCP servers access karne deta hai. Halanki aisa lag sakta hai ki isse custom clients ki zaroorat kam ho jayegi, lekin is likhne ke samay yeh sirf tools aur remote MCP servers support karta hai, jo Chapter 7 me dikhaye gaye hisaab se security risk ho sakta hai. Yeh aapko Claude jaise Anthropic models se bhi bandh deta hai, jo aapke particular use case me fit nahi ho sakta.

Client ko kam se kam kya karna chahiye

MCP me, ek client ek server se saari communication aur connections handle karta hai. Kyunki client/server connections one-to-one hote hain, isliye aam taur par ek client class banana best hota hai. Ek client ko kam se kam yeh karna chahiye: ek server se connect karna, server ki capabilities discover karna, aur un capabilities ko ek LLM ko available karwana. In basic operations se aage, aksar yeh features implement karna helpful hota hai: authentication, capability filtering, aur model agnosticism.

Wrapper class kyun — design philosophy

Book ka design SDK ke Client class ko apni class se wrap karta hai. Aap seedha Client class ka instance bhi apni host application me context manager ke roop me use kar sakte ho, jo aapki application ko Client instance aur uske use kiye gaye resources ko automatically clean up karne deta hai jab control context manager ke block se bahar nikalta hai. Lekin book ki tarah ek wrapper class banana aapko apne client ko use karne ke tareeke me additional flexibility deta hai.

Example ke liye, aap server ko touch karne se pehle inputs ko aur outputs ko process kar sakte ho, aur stdio servers se long-lived connections ko zyada aasani se maintain kar sakte ho, manually control karke ki aapka client kab server se connect aur disconnect karta hai. Figure 3-1 me humare design ki layer hierarchy dikhayi gayi hai, host application se lekar client wrapper tak, aur phir transport tak.

Client skeleton — Example 3-2

Ab hum client class ke liye ek interface sketch karte hain. Agar aap GitHub repository me follow kar rahe ho, to is section ka code client.py me hai, aur saara host application code agent.py me hai. Hum is structure ko baaki chapter me continue karenge. Pehle hum client ka skeleton banate hain, jisme server se connect aur disconnect karne ke functions honge, aur saath me wrappers bhi honge jo hume server ke dwara available karaye gaye tools ki list lene aur un tools ko call karne me madad karenge.

class MCPClient:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        pass

    async def connect(self) -> None:
        "Connect to the server set in the constructor."
        pass

    async def get_available_tools(self) -> list:
        "Retrieve tools that the server has made available."
        pass

    async def use_tool(self, tool_name, arguments=None):
        "Given a tool name and optionally arguments, execute the tool."
        pass

    async def disconnect(self) -> None:
        "Clean up any resources."
        pass

Is class me, constructor ko chhodkar, teen methods ke signatures banaye gaye hain. connect() aapke server se connection initialize karega — implementation transport layer ke choice ke basis par alag dikhega. get_available_tools() client ke server connection ka use karke server ke dwara available karaye gaye tools ko retrieve karega. use_tool() ek tool ko call karega, uska naam aur caller dwara diye gaye arguments lekar.

Apne client ke liye ek aur acha naam MCPServer bhi ho sakta hai, jaise official Python examples me kiya gaya hai, kyunki host application ke perspective se, instantiated object ek MCP server ko represent karega. Yeh confusing ho sakta hai, isliye is example me MCPClient naam choose kiya gaya hai. Apne projects me woh naam chuno jo aapko aur aapke users ko sabse zyada sense de.

Notice karo ki yeh skeleton tools ke support se shuru hua tha. Tools MCP ke major primitives me se ek hain aur arguably MCP ka sabse popular use case hain. Tools agents ko unki agency dene me madad kar sakte hain, LLMs ke knowledge ko augment kar sakte hain, aur bahut kuch — isliye hum tool support implement karke shuru kar rahe hain, aur phir dikhayenge ki MCP server provide kar sakne wale saare resources ke liye support kaise dikhaya jaye. Book me ek note hai ki teen MCP primitives hain: tools, prompts aur resources.

import os

from anthropic import Anthropic
from dotenv import load_dotenv

load_dotenv()

LLM_API_KEY = os.environ["LLM_API_KEY"]
anthropic_client = Anthropic(api_key=LLM_API_KEY)

print("Welcome to your AI Assistant. Type 'goodbye' to quit.")


def main():
    while True:
        prompt = input("You: ")
        if prompt.lower() == "goodbye":
            print("AI Assistant: Goodbye!")
            break
        message = anthropic_client.messages.create(
            max_tokens=4096,
            messages=[
                {
                    "role": "user",
                    "content": prompt,
                }
            ],
            model="claude-sonnet-5",
        )
        for response in message.content:
            print(f"Assistant: {response.text}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

03.2Chapter 3 · Making an Intelligent Application Agentic with MCP Clients

stdio transport se server connect karna

stdio transport local servers ke liye hai — client server ko subprocess ke roop me launch karta hai aur standard input/output par messages bhejta hai. Python SDK me iske liye saare structures ready milte hain.

Transport chunna — pehle socho

Koi bhi code likhne se pehle, socho ki aap server se kaise connect karna chahte ho. Iska matlab hai yeh sochna ki kaunsa transport use karna hai. MCP me, ek transport protocol ki transport layer ki implementation hai aur messages ko client aur server ke beech bhejne ka tareeka manage karta hai. Is likhne ke samay, MCP ke do major built-in transport implementations hain: stdio aur Streamable HTTP.

stdio transport us samay suitable hai jab aap expect karte ho ki servers host application ke saath hi run honge, kyunki yeh client aur server ke beech communication carry karne ke liye standard input aur output streams ka use karta hai. Yeh sabse common transport hai, kyunki iske liye likhna simple hai aur kyunki kai commercially available applications jo MCP clients host karti hain, jaise IDEs, expect karte hain ki user servers ko khud install aur run karega.

Streamable HTTP transport, doosri taraf, un applications ke liye best suited hai jo MCP servers use karte hain jinke host applications ke saath run karne ki expectation nahi ki ja sakti. Yeh platform development aur hosted tools me sabse zyada apparent hai. Jab aap ek platform ya framework develop kar rahe ho downstream products banane aur deploy karne ke liye, to zaroori nahi hai ki aap ek MCP server bhi banao jo aapke users ko locally install aur run karna pade. Jab aap ek remote server host karte ho, to aap control kar sakte ho ki use kaun access kar sakta hai aur woh kaunsa data aur tools provide karta hai, auth set up kar sakte ho, aur uske execution environment ko control kar sakte ho.

Ek warning me bataya gaya hai ki kisi bhi transport, Streamable HTTP sahit, ko security problems se bachane ke liye properly secure karna zaroori hai. Isme connection ko authenticate karna aur DNS rebinding attacks se bachne ke liye origin headers ko validate karna shaamil hai. Server-based security measures Chapter 7 me cover kiye gaye hain.

Constructor — Example 3-3

Pehle, sabse simple case dekhte hain: stdio se connect karna. Is section me, aap MCPClient class ke liye constructor aur connect() methods banayenge. Uske baad, aap wahi kaam Streamable HTTP client banane ke liye karenge, jo remote MCP servers se connect kar sakta hai. Uske baad, hum ek aise client ka example dekhenge jo dono methods support karta hai aur appropriate method kaise choose karna hai.

Jab aap stdio se MCP server se connect karte ho, to client server ko ek subprocess ke roop me launch karega aur phir uski standard input se messages read karega aur uski standard output ke through messages bhejega. Hamari khushkismati hai ki MCP Python SDK me saare structures hain jo hume apna client banane aur stdio se connect karne ke liye chahiye honge.

from contextlib import AsyncExitStack
from mcp.client import Client

class MCPClient:
    def __init__(self, name, command, server_args, env_vars=None):
        self.name = name
        self.command = command
        self.server_args = server_args
        self.env_vars = env_vars
        self._client = None
        self._exit_stack = AsyncExitStack()
        self._connected = False

Is constructor me aap kai important properties set karte ho jo aapko MCP server se connect aur interact karne me enable karengi. Pehli, name, instantiated client ko ek human-readable naam deti hai. Yeh logging ke liye useful hai, khaas taur par agar aap kai servers se connections maintain kar rahe ho, kyunki yeh aapko kisi bhi emitted log ka specific origin aasani se identify karne deti hai. Yeh MCP spec ya SDK ki requirement nahi hai, lekin follow karne ke liye ek better practice hai.

Agli teen parameters server set up karne ke liye use hoti hain. command parameter woh executable identify karta hai jo server initiate karne ke liye run karna hai. Sabse commonly, servers ya to python ya node se run honge — ya npx, aapki local installation par depend karta hai. server_args option un saare command-line arguments ki list hai jo command executable ko pass kiye jane hain. Isme kam se kam server file ka path hoga. Agar file command-line arguments leti hai, jaise --port 8000 --verbose, to aapki server_args list ["server.py", "--port", "8080"] jaisi dikhegi. Agla hai env_vars, environment variables ka dictionary, jo typical environment variables ki tarah kaam karta hai.

Hum kuch private connection management properties bhi include karte hain. Example ke liye, _client client instance hold karega, _exit_stack asynchronous connection contexts ko manage karega, aur _connected hume server se connect karne se rokega jab hum pehle se connected hain.

connect() aur disconnect() — Example 3-4 aur 3-5

Agla step hai connect() method implement karna. Yahan, aap Python MCP SDK ke built-in connection management objects ka use karenge taaki server connection banaya aur hold kiya ja sake.

from mcp.client.stdio import StdioServerParameters, stdio_client

async def connect(self):
    if self._connected:
        raise RuntimeError("Client is already connected")
    server_parameters = StdioServerParameters(
        command=self.command,
        args=self.server_args,
        env=self.env_vars if self.env_vars else None
    )
    transport = stdio_client(server_parameters)
    self._client = Client(transport)
    await self._exit_stack.enter_async_context(self._client)
    self._connected = True

Yeh complex lag sakta hai, khaas taur par agar aapko asynchronous Python likhne ka experience nahi hai. Sabse pehle, method _connected property ko check karta hai, jo user ko pehle se khule connection ko dobara kholne se rokega. Phir hum StdioServerParameters object instantiate karte hain, constructor me set kiye gaye properties pass karke. Baaki ka code MCP server ko run aur use karne ke liye necessary processes aur connections banata hai. Hum yeh _exit_stack ke through karte hain, jo hume control karne deta hai ki teardown kab hota hai — regular context manager me yeh tab hota hai jab block exit hota hai.

AsyncExitStack aapko async with context manager syntax use kiye bina, manually asynchronous context managers ko nest karne deta hai. Yeh ek ideal choice hai kyunki aap stack me dynamically aur asynchronous context managers add kar sakte ho, aur stack par saare resources ko ek hi call se order me safely release kar sakte ho. Baad wali feature bahut useful hai kyunki hum decide kar sakte hain ki stack ko kab unwind karna hai, bajay iske ki har context manager ke scope se code nikalne par rely karna pade. Yeh enter_async_context() function ko call karke kiya jata hai. Internally, Client class bhi wahi mechanism use karta hai.

Server parameters set up karne ke baad, hum stdio server se connection kholte hain, jo us subprocess ko start karta hai jis par MCP session run hoga. Hum yeh apne server_parameters ko stdio_client() function me pass karke aur saara kuch Client() constructor me pass karke karte hain. Agla step hai MCP client session start karna, Client ka instance lekar enter_async_context() call karke. Yeh server subprocess start karega aur use karne ke liye latest shared protocol version negotiate karega, ek server/discover message bhejkar, jo server ko trigger karta hai ki woh apni protocol compatibility aur supported capabilities ke saath respond kare. Aakhir me, hum self._connected ko True set karte hain.

Disconnect karna simple hai: disconnect() method self._exit_stack.aclose() call karta hai taaki saare server connections order me close ho sakein, phir self._connected ko False aur self._client ko None set karta hai. Isse aap jab chahein stdio transport ke through MCP servers se cleanly connect aur disconnect kar sakte ho.

Client ko async context manager banana — Example 3-8

Halanki aap Client ko seedha context manager ke roop me use kar sakte ho, aap MCPClient ko bhi async context manager ke roop me use kar sakte ho. Aapko bas __aenter__() aur __aexit__() implement karne hain. __aenter__() ko connect() call karke self return karna hota hai, aur __aexit__() ko bas disconnect call karna hota hai. Isse aapko dono duniya ka best milta hai: client ke context me enter aur exit karne se automatic setup aur teardown, aur host application aur MCP server ke beech data intercept karne ki ability.

Ek tip me bataya gaya hai ki book Client class ko wrap karne ki technique use karti hai taaki zyada flexibility mile, lekin aap apni application code me seedha server se bhi connect kar sakte ho jab aap Client ko context manager ke roop me use karte ho, jo setup aur teardown aapke liye handle karega: async with Client(url) as mcp_client:.

Host application me client instantiate karna — Example 3-9

Ab dekhte hain ki client ko host chatbot application me integrate karne ki ek strategy kya hai. Hum is chapter ki shuruaat me introduce kiye gaye stripped-down chatbot ka use karenge taaki dikhaya ja sake ki MCP client wider LLM-powered application me kaise fit hota hai. Yahan sirf additions yeh hongi: ek stdio MCP client instantiate karna aur ek made-up MCP server se connection kholna, jo calculator tools provide karta hai jaise add_two_numbers, subtract_two_numbers, multiply_two_numbers aur divide_two_numbers.

mcp_client = MCPClient(
    name="calculator_server_connection",
    command="uv",
    server_args=["--directory", str(Path(__file__).parent.resolve()),
                 "run", "calculator_server.py"],
)

async def main():
    await mcp_client.connect()
    while True:
        prompt = input("You: ")
        if prompt.lower() == "goodbye":
            print("AI Assistant: Goodbye!")
            break
        # ... LLM call aur response print karna ...
    await mcp_client.disconnect()

Humne bas itna kiya: client instantiate kiya aur phir connect() call karke server se connection khola. Phir, chat loop exit hone ke baad, hum disconnect() call karke connection close karte hain. Ek note me bataya gaya hai ki client instantiate karte samay, humara command python ke bajay uv hai. uv command yahan useful hai kyunki use kahin se bhi run kiya ja sakta hai aur virtual environments aur dependencies manage karna simple ho jata hai. Aap command ko python ya python3 me badal sakte ho, lekin uv ko zaroor check karo.

from typing import Any

from mcp.client import Client
from mcp.client.stdio import StdioServerParameters, stdio_client


class MCPClient:
    def __init__(

    async def connect(self) -> None:
        """
        Connect to the server set in the constructor.
        """
        if self._connected:
            raise RuntimeError("Client is already connected")

        server_parameters = StdioServerParameters(
            command=self.command,
            args=self.server_args,

        )

    ):

        """
        pass

            self._client = None

from contextlib import AsyncExitStack
from typing import Any

import httpx2
from mcp.client import Client
from mcp.client.streamable_http import streamable_http_client


class MCPClient:
    def __init__(self, name: str, server_url: str) -> None:
        self.name = name
        self.server_url = server_url
        self._client: Client | None = None
        self._exit_stack = AsyncExitStack()
        self._connected: bool = False

    async def __aenter__(self) -> "MCPClient":
        await self.connect()
        return self

    async def __aexit__(self, exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb) -> None:
        await self.disconnect()

    async def connect(self, headers: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> None:
        if self._connected:
            raise RuntimeError("Client is already connected")

        try:
            if headers:
                http_client = await self._exit_stack.enter_async_context(
                    httpx2.AsyncClient(
                        headers=headers,
                        timeout=httpx2.Timeout(30.0, read=300.0),
                        follow_redirects=True,
                    )
                )
                transport = streamable_http_client(
                    url=self.server_url, http_client=http_client
                )
                self._client = Client(transport)
            else:
                self._client = Client(self.server_url)

            await self._exit_stack.enter_async_context(self._client)
        except Exception:
            await self._exit_stack.aclose()
            raise
        self._connected = True

    async def get_available_tools(self) -> list[Any]:
        """
        Retrieve tools that the server has made available.
        """
        pass

    async def use_tool(
        self, tool_name: str, arguments: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    ):
        """
        Given a tool name and optionally a dictionary of arguments, execute
        the tool
        """
        pass

    async def disconnect(self) -> None:
        """
        Clean up any resources
        """
        if self._exit_stack:
            await self._exit_stack.aclose()
            self._connected = False
            self._client = None

← Previous03.1 · Apna pehla client design karna→ Next03.3 · Streamable HTTP se connect karna
03.3Chapter 3 · Making an Intelligent Application Agentic with MCP Clients

Streamable HTTP se connect karna

Streamable HTTP remote servers ke liye hai. Yeh stateless hota hai — koi persistent connection nahi khulta, client bas har request me version aur capabilities bhejkar server se baat karta hai.

Streamable HTTP kya hai aur kab use karein

Streamable HTTP remote MCP servers ke saath use karne ke liye design kiya gaya main transport hai. Originally, HTTP SSE remote servers se connect karne ka standard tha, lekin production issues ki wajah se uska continued support untenable ho gaya. Woh issues aur dono transports ki architecture Chapter 8 me cover kiye gaye hain.

Jab aap Streamable HTTP se ek remote server se connect karte ho, to aap actually ek persistent connection nahi banate. Kyunki yeh transport stateless hai, isliye yeh ek khula connection ya connection ki state ke baare me koi bhi jaankari hold nahi karta. Iske bajay, aapka MCP client server ki capabilities discover karega aur use apni server ke saath communication ko inform karne ke liye use karega. To jab aap Streamable HTTP se ek server se connect karte ho, to transport stdio ki tarah ek channel nahi kholta. Iske bajay, woh ek client configure karta hai jo requests bhejna shuru karne ke liye ready hai.

Isi tarah, disconnect karna communication ki line ko sever nahi karta ya server ko koi jaankari bhi nahi bhejta, lekin yeh koi bhi running tasks ko cancel karta hai aur MCP client ke HTTP client ko close karta hai. Yeh stdio se bilkul alag mental model hai, aur ise samajhna remote servers ke saath kaam karne ke liye zaroori hai.

Constructor — Example 3-6

Streamable HTTP support karne ke liye, hum phir se MCPClient ke constructor, connect() aur disconnect() methods banane par focus karenge. Constructor stdio client ke constructor se eerily similar hai. Kyunki hum locally ek process start nahi kar rahe hain, hume command ya server_args ki zaroorat nahi hai, lekin hume server ke liye ek location chahiye hoti hai, jo server_url provide karta hai. Baaki properties stdio client me wahi hain.

class MCPClient:
    def __init__(self, name, server_url):
        self.name = name
        self.server_url = server_url
        self._client = None
        self._exit_stack = AsyncExitStack()
        self._connected = False

connect() aur disconnect() — Example 3-7

Server se connect aur disconnect karna bhi stdio client ke process se kaafi similar hai. Sabse obvious farak yeh hai ki hum ek parameters object ke bajay ek HTTP client banate hain. Yeh request headers hold kar sakta hai aur authentication ke liye ek auth object bhi hold kar sakta hai, jise aap Chapter 4 me kaam me laoge. Doosra farak yeh hai ki humare paas Client ko sirf ek server URL dekar instantiate karne ka option hai.

async def connect(self, headers=None):
    if self._connected:
        raise RuntimeError("Client is already connected")
    try:
        if headers:
            http_client = await self._exit_stack.enter_async_context(
                httpx2.AsyncClient(
                    headers=headers,
                    timeout=httpx2.Timeout(30.0, read=300.0),
                    follow_redirects=True,
                )
            )
            transport = streamable_http_client(
                url=self.server_url, http_client=http_client
            )
            self._client = Client(transport)
        else:
            self._client = Client(self.server_url)
        await self._exit_stack.enter_async_context(self._client)
    except Exception:
        await self._exit_stack.aclose()
        raise
    self._connected = True

Yeh code hopefully bahut familiar lagta hai. Yeh stdio client ke connect() aur disconnect() code jaisa hi overall process use karta hai: yeh connect() aur disconnect() functions apne parameters object ya HTTP client ka use karke ek transport instantiate karte hain, phir transport object ko Client class ke liye input ke roop me use karte hain, aur resulting object ko exit stack me add karke start karte hain. Kuch details, of course, alag hain.

Agar aapko incoming headers ki zaroorat nahi hai, to aap httpx2 client banana poori tarah skip kar sakte ho. Iske bajay, aap Client constructor ko ek URL pass kar sakte ho, aur woh aapke liye ek default transport construct kar lega. Hum StdioServerParameters object instantiate nahi karte, kyunki streamable_http_client() function ek special parameters object nahi leti. Iske bajay, uske regular parameters hote hain: ek required url, ek optional http_client, aur ek optional terminate_on_close.

Ek aur important detail yeh hai ki koi bhi exception aane par exit stack close kar diya jata hai, kyunki exception aane par __aexit__() call nahi hota. Warna, humare paas ek dangling connected client ho sakta hai jo garbage collect nahi hota. Yahi woh tareeka hai jisse aap ensure karte ho ki failed connection ke baad koi resource leak na ho.

stdio vs Streamable HTTP — kab kaunsa

Dono transports ka comparison ek baar phir yaad rakho: stdio local servers ke liye hai, jahan server host application ke saath chalta hai, aur client use subprocess ke roop me launch karta hai. Streamable HTTP remote servers ke liye hai, jahan server kahin aur host hota hai aur URL se access kiya jata hai. Enterprises jo pehle se REST APIs serve karne ka experience rakhte hain, woh khaas taur par remote servers provide karke MCP ke saath experiment kar rahe hain, taaki woh access control, auth aur execution environment ko control kar sakein.

Dono ko support karna best practice hai: stdio ko hamesha support karo, aur Streamable HTTP ko add karo agar aap remote server deploy karne ya apni application me remote servers add karne ka support dene ka plan rakhte ho. Is chapter ke baad, aapke paas ek aisa client hoga jo dono transports se connect kar sakta hai, aur aap use case ke hisaab se appropriate transport choose kar sakte ho.

from contextlib import AsyncExitStack
from typing import Any

import httpx2
from mcp.client import Client
from mcp.client.streamable_http import streamable_http_client


class MCPClient:
    def __init__(self, name: str, server_url: str) -> None:
        self.name = name
        self.server_url = server_url
        self._client: Client | None = None
        self._exit_stack = AsyncExitStack()
        self._connected: bool = False

    async def connect(self, headers: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> None:
        if self._connected:
            raise RuntimeError("Client is already connected")

        try:
            if headers:
                http_client = await self._exit_stack.enter_async_context(
                    httpx2.AsyncClient(
                        headers=headers,
                        timeout=httpx2.Timeout(30.0, read=300.0),
                        follow_redirects=True,
                    )
                )
                transport = streamable_http_client(
                    url=self.server_url, http_client=http_client
                )
                self._client = Client(transport)
            else:
                self._client = Client(self.server_url)

            await self._exit_stack.enter_async_context(self._client)
        except Exception:
            await self._exit_stack.aclose()
            raise
        self._connected = True

    async def get_available_tools(self) -> list[Any]:
        """
        Retrieve tools that the server has made available.
        """
        pass

    async def use_tool(
        self, tool_name: str, arguments: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    ):
        """
        Given a tool name and optionally a dictionary of arguments, execute
        the tool
        """
        pass

    async def disconnect(self) -> None:
        """
        Clean up any resources
        """
        if self._exit_stack:
            await self._exit_stack.aclose()
            self._connected = False
            self._client = None

← Previous03.2 · stdio transport se server connect karna→ Next03.4 · Server capabilities use karna — tools, resources, prompts
03.4Chapter 3 · Making an Intelligent Application Agentic with MCP Clients

Server capabilities use karna — tools, resources, prompts

Har capability ka pattern ek jaisa hai: pehle discover karo, phir use karo. Tools ke liye list_tools aur call_tool, resources ke liye list_resources aur read_resource, prompts ke liye list_prompts aur get_prompt.

Discovery aur use — do-step workflow

MCP servers kai tarah ki capabilities provide kar sakte hain, jinme MCP primitives tools, resources aur prompts shaamil hain. Ek client developer ke roop me, aap unse instantiated Client object ke through interact karoge, aur aap aam taur par inme se har ek ke liye wahi do-step workflow use karoge: discovery aur use. Har capability ke liye, discovery ek primitive/list request ke through hoti hai, jo Python SDK me list_primitives() methods se wrap ki jati hai. Yeh calls available tools, resources ya prompts ki list wapas karte hain.

Resulting capabilities ko use karne ke liye ek primitive/verb call chahiye hoti hai, jahan verb us primitive par depend karta hai jise call kiya ja raha hai. Python SDK me, yeh calls verb_primitive() form ke methods se wrap ki jati hain, jaise tool/call ke liye call_tool(). Python MCP SDK vibhinn request JSON-RPC messages ko methods me wrap karta hai jinhe aapka client seedha call kar sakta hai. Lekin unhe apne client object methods se call karna aksar ek acha idea hota hai, taaki aap logging, retries, method parameters aur koi bhi aur customizations apne server calls me add kar sakein, ya tool call se wapas aaye data ko application tak pahunchne se pehle process kar sakein.

Protocol server ko client ko notification messages bhejne bhi allow karta hai, aur phir receiver par hai ki woh notifications ko jaise chahe handle kare. Streamable HTTP connections ke liye, yeh notifications kisi bhi aur message ki tarah bheji jayengi, lekin JSONRPCNotification ke roop me bheji jayengi. Python SDK me Client class ka listen() function MCP clients ko un notifications ko consume karne deta hai.

Tools — discover karna

Tools woh sabse common resource hain jo MCP servers provide karte hain, aur iska acha reason hai: agentic workflows ko aksar base LLM ki abilities augment karne ke liye tools chahiye hote hain. Tools simply ek deterministic function hain jinhe LLM decide karke call kar sakta hai agar zaroorat ho. Naturally, function code me kuch bhi kar sakta hai jo aap soch sakte ho — numbers calculate karne se lekar playlist banane tak. MCP servers clients ko in tools ko discover aur use karne dete hain.

Python SDK ka use karke tools discover karne ke liye, aapka client self._client.list_tools() call karega, jo ek ListToolsResult object wapas karta hai, jisme tools property hoti hai. Yeh server ke dwara available karaye gaye tools ki list hold karta hai, jahan tools ke properties hote hain: name, description, input_schema aur annotations. Client class is result ko by default ek time to live ke saath cache karti hai. Jab TTL pass ho jata hai ya client ko list changed notification milti hai, to cache empty kar diya jata hai. Yeh TTL optionally server ke dwara set kiya jata hai: server cacheability control karta hai, aur client bas use use karta hai.

Wrapper class design ke saath, hum list_tools() jaise functions ko call karke results ko Agent ke chat loop me ek variable me store kar sakte hain. Phir hum ek simple _refresh() function implement karke control kar sakte hain ki data kab refresh karna hai. list_tools() ko seedha call karna basic use cases ke liye theek ho sakta hai, lekin agar aap ek aisa client bana rahe ho jo alag-alag capabilities wale alag servers ke liye use hoga, to apna function likhna advantageous ho sakta hai jisme kuch guardrails, logging aur kuch bhi ho jo aapke users ko abstracted chahiye.

async def get_available_tools(self):
    if not self._connected:
        raise RuntimeError("Client not connected to a server")
    tools_result = await self._client.list_tools()
    if not tools_result.tools:
        logger.warning("No tools found on server")
    available_tools = [
        {"name": tool.name,
         "description": tool.description,
         "input_schema": tool.input_schema}
        for tool in tools_result.tools
    ]
    return available_tools

Yeh method Client object ke list_tools() method ka ek simple wrapper hai, jo khud tools/list request ko wrap karta hai. Simple hote hue bhi, example dikhata hai ki aap basic guardrails kaise implement kar sakte ho, jaise server connection status check, aur zyada detailed logging, jaise empty tool result check. Method MCP-native tool object list ko name, description aur input_schema keys wali dictionaries ki list me convert bhi karta hai. Isse Anthropic Messages API ke saath compatibility ensure hoti hai. Aap is pattern ko extend karke retries add kar sakte ho, MCP ke tool format ko doosre LLM ke compatible format me translate kar sakte ho, aur aur bhi bahut kuch.

Tools — use karna aur tool-use loop

Ab jab aapke client ke paas tools hain, to unka kya karna hai? Use karna, of course. get_available_tools() example ki tarah, hum Client object ke call_tool() function ko wrap karenge, thodi si logging add karenge aur alag-alag available response types ko handle karenge. call_tool() function ek CallToolResult wapas karta hai, jo apne content field me SDK ke content types me se kisi ki list hold karta hai: TextContent, jisme result kisi bhi tarah ka text hota hai aur text property me store hota hai; ImageContent, jisme image data Base64-encoded string ke roop me data property me store hoti hai; AudioContent, jo ImageContent ki tarah hi hoti hai; aur EmbeddedResource, jo tools ke response ke hisse ke roop me embedded resources wapas kar sakta hai, aam taur par extra context ya data caching ke liye.

Ek key point yeh hai ki tool-use requests content ki lists wapas karte hain, aur kuch cases me, jaise EmbeddedResource response ko additional context ke roop me use karna, iski expectation rakhni chahiye aur use handle karna chahiye. use_tool() wrapper method pehle check karta hai ki client server session se connected hai ya nahi, aur agar nahi hai to exception raise karta hai. Phir hum call_tool() call karte hain, tool ka naam aur arguments pass karke. Agar content list empty nahi hai, to hum har item ko iterate karte hain, uske type ko check karte hain, aur proper string representation ko results list me add karte hain. Agar content empty hai, to hum user ko warning dikhate hain, aur aakhir me results list wapas karte hain.

Client class ka call_tool() method do additional arguments leta hai: progress_callback aur read_timeout_seconds. Pehla aapko ek function provide karne deta hai jo har baar call hota hai jab client ko us specific tool call ke liye progress notification milti hai — bas shart yeh hai ki woh async ho aur float progress, optional float total aur optional string message accept kare. Isse aap long-running tool call ke liye user ko progress bar dikhane jaise kaam kar sakte ho. Doosra aapko ek timeout threshold set karne deta hai, taaki client potentially hanging tool calls ko terminate kar sake.

Host application me tools ko use karne ke liye, agent loop ko update kiya jata hai: model ko tools parameter me available tools diye jate hain, aur tool_choice ko "auto" par set kiya jata hai, taaki model decide kar sake ki user query answer karne ke liye kaunsa tool use karna hai. Aap type ko "any" bhi set kar sakte ho, taaki model available tools me se koi bhi — lekin kam se kam ek — tool use kare, ya ek tool ka naam aur type "tool" add karke model ko specific tool use karne ke liye force kar sakte ho, ya "none" karke model ko koi bhi available tool use karne se rok sakte ho.

Phir result inspect kiya jata hai: agar response ka stop_reason tool_use hai, to model kisi tool ya tools ke results ka wait kar raha hai. Tool-use message blocks response contents se banaye jate hain, aur phir tools ko ek loop me execute kiya jata hai. Results se ek dictionary banayi jati hai, jisme type tool_result, tool_use_id model ke tool-use message response se ID, aur content tool call ka result hota hai. Yeh saare conversation_messages list me add kiye jate hain. Jab saare tool calls ho jayein, to results aur original user question LLM ko evaluation ke liye wapas bheje jate hain. Kyunki user ko wapas karne se pehle kai tool calls kiye ja sakte hain, isliye yeh sab ek while loop me wrap kiya jata hai. Agar koi tool-call responses nahi hain, to latest response se text blocks extract karke print kiye jate hain, aur poora main() ek try/finally block me wrap kiya jata hai taaki user ke application quit karne par connection proper scope se disconnect ho jaye.

Resources — data ko context banana

Resources host application aur LLM ko MCP server ke dwara serve kiye gaye data ki access dete hain — database records, images, text files aur aur bhi bahut kuch. Resources par kai actions liye ja sakte hain: resources/list ya list_resources() server se available resources ki list maangta hai; resources/templates/list ya list_resource_templates() resource URI templates ki list maangta hai, jo aapko doosri jaankari ke basis par resource ka URI dynamically construct karne dete hain — Python SDK me yeh strings f-strings jaisi dikhti hain, jinme variable sections curly braces me enclosed hote hain; resources/read ya read_resource() server ke dwara di gayi file ko access karta hai, data ko text ya blob format me LLM ko bhejta hai; aur subscriptions/listen client ko changes ke liye listen karne ko kehta hai — ya to available resources ki list ke liye, ya diye gaye resource URIs ki list me kisi bhi resource me changes ke liye.

Wrappers ka pattern tools jaisa hi hai: get_available_resources() aur get_available_resource_templates() connection check karte hain, appropriate list method call karte hain, result check karte hain aur use wapas karte hain, empty result par warning ke saath. Dono list methods ek optional cursor parameter bhi lete hain, results ko paginate karne ke liye. get_resource() wrapper ek resource URI leta hai, resource ko read karta hai, aur use caller ko text string ya Base64-encoded data string ke roop me wapas karta hai. Resources aur resource templates ke properties lagbhag same hote hain: name, description, mime_type, size aur annotations. Resources me uri property hoti hai, jabki resource templates me uri_template hoti hai.

Host application me resources ka use ek interesting tareeke se dikhaya gaya hai: ek naya Agent class banaya jata hai, jo client objects hold karta hai aur resources se interact karta hai. Isme _select_resources() method hai, jo ek LLM ka use karke user prompt ke basis par relevant resources select karta hai — available resources ki dictionary banakar, use aur user prompt ko ek selection prompt me inject karke, aur LLM se JSON array me resource names maangkar. Phir _load_selected_resources() selected resources ko unki URI se load karta hai, content ko type ke hisaab se parse karta hai — text ke liye "[Resource: name]" prefix ke saath text block, images ke liye Base64 image block — aur context_messages list banata hai, jo user prompt ke saath ek hi message me bundle karke LLM ko bheji jati hai.

Is example me ek tip bhi hai: aap resources ko apne model me load karne ke kai tareeke handle kar sakte ho, jo aapki desired UX par heavily depend karega. Aap file-picker UI use kar sakte ho, Example 3-17 jaisa LLM-based selector, ek specialized system prompt jisme sirf URIs hon, resource templates, ya bas saare resources ko seedha user ya system prompts me load kar sakte ho. Agar aap saare resources up front load karte ho, to aap zyadatar popular models me prompt caching ka fayda utha sakte ho — static data ko har user prompt ki shuruaat me inject karke cache hits maximize karo, jo token cost ko drastically reduce karte hain.

Prompts — user ke control me

Prompts MCP servers ke dwara provide kiye gaye teen main primitives me se aakhri hain. Yeh application user ke dwara control kiye jane ke liye design kiye gaye hain, jise pick karna chahiye ki kaunsa prompt use karna hai. Har prompt definition ka ek unique identifier name hota hai, ek optional human-readable description, aur optional arguments, jo dictionaries ki list hoti hai, jinme name, optional human-readable description, aur optional required Boolean hota hai jo batata hai ki argument required hai ya nahi. Phir client implementation ya prompt use karne wali host application par hai ki woh har argument ke liye values inject kare. Yeh dynamic prompts kehlate hain.

Example ke liye, ek simple code-review prompt lo: "Review the following Python code for bugs and style issues: a + b = 3". Yeh kuch had tak useless hai. Kai cases me, hum prompt me variables use karna chahte hain taaki use zyada generalizable banaya ja sake — jaise "Review the following {language} code for bugs and style issues: {code}." Ab aap language aur code variables pass kar sakte ho, aur server filled-out prompt wapas karega. Python SDK me Client class ka list_prompts() method Prompt objects ki list wapas karta hai, aur get_prompt() me prompt ka naam aur arguments dekar aapko PromptMessage objects ki list milti hai, jo ready-to-use messages hote hain jinhe plain dictionary me convert karke seedha LLM ko bheja ja sakta hai.

Wrappers ka pattern phir wahi hai: get_available_prompts() connection check karta hai, prompts ki list leta hai, aur empty result par warning dekar use wapas karta hai. load_prompt() prompt ka naam aur arguments leta hai, server se prompt load karta hai, aur MCP PromptMessage objects ko application ko wapas karta hai. Host application me prompts ka use resources wale pattern jaisa hai: Agent class me available_prompts dictionary hoti hai, display_prompts() user ko prompts aur unke arguments dikhata hai, _collect_prompt_arguments() user se har argument ki value poochta hai — required argument na mile to ek baar phir poochta hai — aur _use_prompt() prompt ko load karke use conversation messages me inject karta hai.

Ek warning me bataya gaya hai ki agar aapka prompt role "assistant" hai, to kuch models, jaise Claude, ek initial turn ko us role ke saath respond nahi kar payenge. Agar aap is situation ki expectation rakhte ho, to use appropriately handle karo — ya to assistant message prompts ko discard karke, ya "assistant" role wale prompt ko ek "user" turn ke baad insert karke. Run loop me, user "prompts" type karke prompts dekh sakta hai aur ek ko naam se select kar sakta hai, ya normal query path se resources aur tools ke saath baat kar sakta hai.

import asyncio
import os
from pathlib import Path

from anthropic import Anthropic
from client import MCPClient
from dotenv import load_dotenv

load_dotenv()

LLM_API_KEY = os.environ["LLM_API_KEY"]
anthropic_client = Anthropic(api_key=LLM_API_KEY)

mcp_client = MCPClient(
    name="calculator_server_connection",
    command="uv",
    server_args=[
        "--directory",
        str(Path(__file__).parent.parent.resolve()),
        "run",
        "calculator_server.py",
    ],
)

print("Welcome to your AI Assistant. Type 'goodbye' to quit.")


async def main():
    await mcp_client.connect()
    available_tools = await mcp_client.get_available_tools()
    tool_names = ", ".join(tool["name"] for tool in available_tools)
    print(f"Available tools: {tool_names}")
    while True:
        prompt = input("You: ")
        if prompt.lower() == "goodbye":
            print("AI Assistant: Goodbye!")
            break
        message = anthropic_client.messages.create(
            max_tokens=4096,
            messages=[
                {
                    "role": "user",
                    "content": prompt,
                }
            ],
            model="claude-sonnet-5",
        )
        for response in message.content:
            print(f"Assistant: {response.text}")
    await mcp_client.disconnect()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

import logging
from contextlib import AsyncExitStack
from typing import Any

from mcp.client import Client
from mcp.client.stdio import StdioServerParameters, stdio_client

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class MCPClient:
    def __init__(
        self,
        name: str,
        command: str,
        server_args: list[str],
        env_vars: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.name = name
        self.command = command
        self.server_args = server_args
        self.env_vars = env_vars
        self._client: Client | None = None
        self._exit_stack: AsyncExitStack = AsyncExitStack()
        self._connected: bool = False

    async def __aenter__(self) -> "MCPClient":
        await self.connect()
        return self

    async def __aexit__(self, exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb) -> None:
        await self.disconnect()

    async def connect(self) -> None:
        """
        Connect to the server set in the constructor.
        """
        if self._connected:
            raise RuntimeError("Client is already connected")

        server_parameters = StdioServerParameters(
            command=self.command,
            args=self.server_args,
            env=self.env_vars if self.env_vars else None,
        )

        transport = stdio_client(server_parameters)

        self._client = Client(transport)

        await self._exit_stack.enter_async_context(self._client)
        self._connected = True

    async def get_available_tools(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        if not self._connected:
            raise RuntimeError("Client not connected to a server")

        tools_result = await self._client.list_tools()
        if not tools_result.tools:
            logger.warning("No tools found on server")
        available_tools = [
            {
                "name": tool.name,
                "description": tool.description,
                "input_schema": tool.input_schema,
            }
            for tool in tools_result.tools
        ]
        return available_tools

    async def use_tool(
        self, tool_name: str, arguments: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    ):
        """
        Given a tool name and optionally a dictionary of arguments, execute
        the tool
        """
        pass

    async def disconnect(self) -> None:
        """
        Clean up any resources
        """
        if self._exit_stack:
            await self._exit_stack.aclose()
            self._connected = False
            self._client = None
