import asyncio
import json
import sys
from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from datetime import datetime

import mcp.server.stdio
from mcp.server import NotificationOptions, Server, ServerRequestContext
from mcp.server.models import InitializationOptions
from mcp_types import (
    CallToolRequestParams,
    CallToolResult,
    ListToolsResult,
    PaginatedRequestParams,
    TextContent,
    Tool,
)


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(server: Server) -> AsyncGenerator[dict[str, list[str]]]:
    logs = []
    logs.append(f"{datetime.now()}: Server started")
    print(logs[-1], file=sys.stderr)
    try:
        logs.append(f"{datetime.now()}: logs yielded")
        yield {"logs": logs}
    finally:
        logs.append(f"{datetime.now()}: Server stopped, printing all logs")
        print(logs, file=sys.stderr)


async def list_tools(
    ctx: ServerRequestContext, params: PaginatedRequestParams | None
) -> ListToolsResult:
    """List all tools available on the server."""
    logs = ctx.lifespan_context["logs"]
    print(logs[-1], file=sys.stderr)
    logs.append(f"{datetime.now()}: list_tools called")
    print(logs[-1], file=sys.stderr)

    return ListToolsResult(
        tools=[
            Tool(
                name="add",
                description="Add two numbers together.",
                input_schema={
                    "type": "object",
                    "properties": {
                        "a": {
                            "type": "number",
                            "description": "The first number to add",
                        },
                        "b": {
                            "type": "number",
                            "description": "The second number to add",
                        },
                    },
                    "required": ["a", "b"],
                },
                output_schema={
                    "type": "object",
                    "properties": {
                        "augend": {
                            "type": "number",
                            "description": "The first number to add",
                        },
                        "addend": {
                            "type": "number",
                            "description": "The second number to add",
                        },
                        "sum": {
                            "type": "number",
                            "description": "The result of the addition",
                        },
                    },
                    "required": ["augend", "addend", "sum"],
                },
            )
        ]
    )


async def add(
    ctx: ServerRequestContext, params: CallToolRequestParams
) -> CallToolResult:
    """Add two numbers together."""
    if params.name != "add":
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown tool: {params.name}")
    args = params.arguments or {}
    result = {
        "augend": args["a"],
        "addend": args["b"],
        "sum": args["a"] + args["b"],
    }
    logs = ctx.lifespan_context["logs"]
    logs.append(f"{datetime.now()}: add called")
    print(logs[-1], file=sys.stderr)
    return CallToolResult(
        content=[TextContent(type="text", text=json.dumps(result))],
        structured_content=result,
    )


# Create a server instance with the lifespan and handlers
server = Server(
    "low-level-server",
    version="0.1.0",
    lifespan=lifespan,
    on_list_tools=list_tools,
    on_call_tool=add,
)


async def run():
    print("Running low-level server", file=sys.stderr)
    initialization_options = InitializationOptions(
        server_name="low-level-server",
        server_version="0.1.0",
        capabilities=server.get_capabilities(
            notification_options=NotificationOptions(),
            experimental_capabilities={},
        ),
    )

    async with mcp.server.stdio.stdio_server() as (read_stream, write_stream):
        await server.run(
            read_stream=read_stream,
            write_stream=write_stream,
            initialization_options=initialization_options,
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(run())
ch5/15_handling_errors/server.py — https://github.com/kylestratis/ai_agents_mcp_examples/blob/main/ch5/15_handling_errors/server.py
from mcp import MCPError
from mcp.server.mcpserver import MCPServer
from mcp_types import INVALID_REQUEST

# Initialize MCP server
mcp = MCPServer("error-handling-server")

GRADES_POSTED = True
GRADEBOOK = {"[Name]": 98, "[Name]": 94, "[Name]": 97}


@mcp.tool()
def grader_get_grade(student: str) -> int:
    """
    Look up a student's posted grade.

    Args:
        student: The full name of the student
    """
    if not GRADES_POSTED:
        raise MCPError(
            INVALID_REQUEST,
            "Grades have not been posted yet. No results are available.",
        )
    if student not in GRADEBOOK:
        raise ValueError(f"No student named {student!r} in the gradebook.")
    return GRADEBOOK[student]


if __name__ == "__main__":
    mcp.run()
SOURCESource: AI Agents with MCP, O'Reilly, Chapter 5 — Building MCP Servers: Providing Tools, Prompts, and Resources to Applications
← Previous05.1 · Python SDK se server banana→ Next05.3 · Prompts serve karna
05.3Chapter 5 · Building MCP Servers: Providing Tools, Prompts, and Resources to Applications

Prompts serve karna

Prompts woh instructions hote hain jinse LLM apna response generate karta hai. Server prompts serve karke apne well-tested prompts ko users tak distribute kar sakta hai, jisse unki tool-choice performance bhi improve ho sakti hai. Python MCP servers me prompts aise functions hote hain jo string, UserMessage, AssistantMessage, ya inme se ek ya dono ki list return karte hain.

System, user aur assistant prompts

System prompt persistent hota hai aur poori conversation me LLM ke responses ko guide karta hai. Tum default system prompt me add kar sakte ho ya use poori tarah replace kar sakte ho. Agar tum model ki personality badalna chahte ho, use tools kaise use karne hain yeh batana chahte ho, rules dena chahte ho, ya extra context dena chahte ho, to system prompt ke through kar sakte ho. User prompt aam taur par user se generate hota hai aur model se seedha query hota hai, jaise ek simple sawaal ya kuch actions karne ka request. Yeh persistent nahi hota hai, sirf tab bheja jaata hai jab user apni query submit karta hai. Assistant prompt assistant role leta hai aur LLM ke conversation turns ko represent karta hai.

System prompts persistent hote hain, iska matlab hai ki woh har user prompt ke saath model ko bheje jaate hain aur input token cost lagti hai. Isliye system prompts design karte samay, jaise user prompts me, token efficiency aur cost ka dhyaan rakhna chahiye.

Prompt design ke paanch principles

Prompt engineering abhi bhi ek valuable skill hai, khaas taur par jab tum prompts ko apne MCP server se distribute kar rahe ho. Book paanch principles deta hai: direction do, format specify karo, examples do, quality evaluate karo, aur labor divide karo. Pehla principle hai direction dena — tumhare prompts ko LLM ko clear direction deni chahiye, task ke liye bhi aur format ke liye bhi. Prompt ko effectively kuch karna chahiye, jo tum clear, simple aur concise instructions dekar aur specific guidelines ya rules list karke achieve kar sakte ho. Prompt me persona ya examples bhi de sakte ho, taaki LLM ke response ka content aur sound dono augment ho.

Dusra principle hai format specify karna — yeh structured output format ho sakta hai jaise YAML ya JSON, ya response ka general layout bhi. Agar tumhare prompts sirf tumhare server ke tools ko accurately call karne ke liye hain, to output format utna matter nahi karta hai. Lekin agar tum chahte ho ki prompt properly formatted YAML document ke saath respond kare, to tum desired output format ko prompt me seedha specify kar sakte ho, ya desired output ka partial ya full example de sakte ho, ya YAML conversion tool bana sakte ho.

Teesra principle hai examples dena. Logon ki tarah LLMs bhi kuch examples ke saath best kaam karte hain — yeh few-shot learning kehlata hai, jo LLMs ki accuracy aur performance improve karne ki powerful technique hai. Lekin yahan ek trade-off hai: anchoring. Examples sirf task nahi sikhate hain, woh length, tone, structure aur examples ke baare me dusri metadetails bhi sikha dete hain. Model un details se bhi anchor kar sakta hai, jisse model ke output ki variety examples ki distribution ki taraf narrow ho jaati hai. Kabhi yeh desirable hota hai, kabhi nahi — tumhe sochna padega ki tum apne prompt se asal me kya chahte ho, aur kai runs me alag example sets ke saath uski performance evaluate karni padegi.

Chauthe principle ke hisaab se quality ko evaluate karna chahiye — apne prompt ko kai models ke against run karo, khaas taur par kyunki tum apne prompts ko aise users ko distribute karoge jo MCP ki magic ki wajah se use kisi bhi model ke saath use kar sakte hain. Tum simple A/B testing bhi kar sakte ho, do prompts ke saath, model ke API ka use karke. Aakhri principle hai labor divide karna — agar tumhara prompt badhne lage aur zyada kaam karne ki koshish kare, to use alag prompts me todne ka samay aa gaya hai. Tum deterministic prompt workflows setup kar sakte ho, ya apne server ke LLM se saare prompts ko run karke woh choose karwa sakte ho jo user ki query ke liye best fit ho.

General rules bhi hain: yeh mat kaho ki kya nahi karna hai, kyunki isse models confuse ho sakte hain; fairly long jaise vague descriptions ki jagah precise descriptions use karo, jaise 2 paragraphs of 3-5 sentences; aur context aur instruction portions ko alag karne ke liye separators use karo.

Prompt functions kaise likhte hain

Prompts ko @mcp.prompt() decorator se register kiya jaata hai. Is decorator me tum optionally prompt ka naam, title aur description specify kar sakte ho, bilkul @mcp.tool decorator ki tarah. Prompt functions ko string, role aur message keys wali dictionary, Message object ya uske children me se ek, ya inme se kisi bhi type ki sequence return karni hoti hai. Prompt function ke parameters aam taur par application se aane wale user-provided data ko prompt me inject karne ke liye use hote hain, lekin parameters ko kisi bhi cheez ke liye use kar sakte ho jo prompt me include karna samajh me aaye, jaise numbers jinhe sahi value inject karne ke liye compute karna ho.

Book ke example me teen simple prompt functions hain. Pehla static string return karta hai jo model ko user ko greet karne ke liye kehta hai. Dusra username argument leta hai aur f-string return karta hai jo model ko user ko naam se greet karne ke liye kehta hai. Teesra UserMessage object return karta hai, jisme XML tags use hote hain — instruction aur text portions ko alag tags me mark kiya gaya hai. SDK me SystemMessage class nahi hai — agar tum system prompt dena chahte ho to plain string return karni hogi aur document karna hoga ki prompt system prompt ke taur par use hone ke liye hai.

@mcp.prompt()
async def simple_string_prompt() -> str:
    # A simple, static prompt that greets the user.
    return "Say hello to the user."

@mcp.prompt()
async def simple_prompt_input(username: str) -> str:
    # A simple prompt that greets the user with their name.
    return f"Say hello to the user using their name: {username}"

@mcp.prompt()
async def simple_example_prompt(user_text: str) -> UserMessage:
    text = "<instruction>
Create a list of 3 main ideas from the text:
</instruction>

<text>
" + user_text + "
</text>"
    return UserMessage(content=text)

Model-specific tricks bhi hain, jaise ek model family ke liye context ko instruction se fence off karne ke liye ### ya triple quotes use karna, aur dusri model family ke liye XML tags use karna. Kyunki MCP servers model agnostic hote hain, in tricks par zyada depend mat karo, lekin exhaustive testing se performance ki chinta ko kam kiya ja sakta hai. Tum prompt function ya resource function se client ke host model ko dhyaan me rakh kar optimal format bhi de sakte ho, ya user ko instruct kar sakte ho ki woh apne liye kaam karne wala format select kare.

Multiturn prompts aur prefilling

Agar prompt function UserMessages ki list return kare to woh multiturn prompt ban jaata hai — ek prompt jisme multiple Message objects hote hain, jo model aur user ke beech conversation ko represent karte hain. Har Message ka ek role hota hai, user ya assistant, jo dikhata hai ki us turn me kaun bol raha hai. Isse tum conversation ko preload kar sakte ho, jo model ke response ko aur strongly guide karta hai. Asli taakat assistant ke response ko partially filled chhodne me hai — yeh technique prefilling kehlati hai, jo tumhe model ke response par zyada control deti hai. Prefill se tum structured output format provide kar sakte ho ya model ko ek role maintain karwa sakte ho.

Book ka example multiturn_prompt() dikhata hai, jo UserMessage aur AssistantMessage ki list return karta hai. UserMessage me instruction aur text XML tags me hote hain, aur main_idea_count argument bhi leta hai. AssistantMessage ko introductory response aur numbered list ki shuruaat se prefill kiya gaya hai — Here are 3 main ideas from the text: 1. — jo model ko list continue karne ke liye encourage karta hai.

Prompts se tool use control karna

Prompts se tum model ke behavior ko dusre tareekon se bhi control kar sakte ho. Example ke taur par, tum model ko encourage kar sakte ho ki user ke request ka jawab dete samay ek tool ko prioritize kare. Iske liye tum user ke input me ek additional instruction add karte ho, jo model ko kehti hai ki pehle ek khaas tool ki applicability check kare. Ya tum kam subtle ho kar seedha model ko keh sakte ho ki tool ko use hi kare, chahe user ka request kuch bhi ho.

Book ke example me analyze_sentiment naam ka tool hai jo random sentiment rating return karta hai. request_tool_use() prompt function user ke request ko leta hai aur ek additional instruction add karta hai, jo model ko kehti hai ki analyze_sentiment tool use kare agar available ho, aur uske result ko use karke user ke sentiment ko neutral ki taraf move kare. force_tool_use() prompt function tool ko seedha call karta hai aur assistant ke response ko result aur response ki shuruaat se prefill karta hai, taaki agent us starting point se complete kar sake. Isi tarah tum prompts ko tools ke saath combine karke application ke behavior ko influence kar sakte ho.

Prompts me resources ka use

Resources ko MCP prompts ke andar bhi use kar sakte ho. Book ka example knowledge_base naam ka resource dikhata hai, jiska URI file://knowledge.txt hai, aur knowledge_base_prompt prompt function ek multiturn prompt banata hai jisme user ka original request, resource use karne ki instruction, aur ResourceLink UserMessage hota hai jo resource ke URI ki taraf point karta hai. Isse prompt function text resource ko user ke request me add karta hai aur model ko instruct karta hai ki resource ko use karke user ke request ka jawab de.

Prompts kaise use hote hain

MCP specification users ya applications par prompts ko interact karne ka koi ek tareeka force nahi karti hai, lekin prompts user-controlled hone ke liye design kiye gaye the. User ko select karna chahiye ki kaunse prompts use karne hain aur kab use karne hain, jo aam taur par chat applications me menu selection ya slash commands ke taur par implement hota hai. Yeh samajhna ki tumhare prompts kaise use honge, tumhe unhe is tarah design karne me madad karega ki user ko seamless experience mile. Applications technically tumhare prompts ko user messages, assistant messages ya system prompts ke taur par bhi use kar sakti hain — isliye UserMessage aur AssistantMessage objects return karna application ko zyada jaankari deta hai ki tumhara prompt kaise use hone ke liye design kiya gaya tha, aur README ya docstrings me document karna chahiye ki tumhare prompts kis tarah use hone ke liye hain.

Messages ka flow tools aur resources jaisa hi hota hai: discovery phase me client connect hote hi server ko prompts/list request bhejta hai, aur server prompts ki list se respond karta hai. Usage phase aam taur par tab trigger hota hai jab user client application ke andar list se ek prompt select karta hai, jisse client server ko prompts/get request bhejta hai aur server prompt ke saath respond karta hai. Modern clients prompt list updates ke liye subscribe kar sakte hain, aur tum context object ke ctx.notify_prompts_changed() se unhe bhej sakte ho agar tumhare handlers prompt list ko badalte hain.

ch5/08_simple_prompt/server.py — https://github.com/kylestratis/ai_agents_mcp_examples/blob/main/ch5/08_simple_prompt/server.py
from mcp.server.mcpserver import MCPServer
from mcp.server.mcpserver.prompts.base import UserMessage

# Initialize MCP server
mcp = MCPServer("simple-prompt-server")


@mcp.prompt()
async def simple_string_prompt() -> str:
    """A simple, static prompt that greets the user."""
    return "Say hello to the user."


@mcp.prompt()
async def simple_prompt_input(username: str) -> str:
    """A simple prompt that greets the user with their name."""
    return f"Say hello to the user using their name: {username}"


@mcp.prompt()
async def simple_example_prompt(user_text: str) -> UserMessage:
    """A simple prompt that summarizes the input text, using XML tags."""
    return UserMessage(
        content=f"""
<instruction>
Create a list of 3 main ideas from the following text:
</instruction>

<text>
{user_text}
</text>
    """
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    mcp.run()
ch5/09_multiturn_prompt/server.py — https://github.com/kylestratis/ai_agents_mcp_examples/blob/main/ch5/09_multiturn_prompt/server.py
from mcp.server.mcpserver import MCPServer
from mcp.server.mcpserver.prompts.base import AssistantMessage, UserMessage

# Initialize MCP server
mcp = MCPServer("multiturn-prompt-server")


@mcp.prompt()
async def multiturn_prompt(
    main_idea_count: int, user_text: str
) -> list[UserMessage | AssistantMessage]:
    user_input = UserMessage(
        content=f"""
<instruction>
Create a list of {main_idea_count} main ideas from the following text:
</instruction>

<text>
{user_text}
</text>
    """
    )

    assistant_prefill_text = f"""
Here are {main_idea_count} main ideas from the text:
1.
"""
    assistant_prefill = AssistantMessage(content=assistant_prefill_text)
    return [user_input, assistant_prefill]


if __name__ == "__main__":
    mcp.run()
ch5/10_tool_use_prompt/server.py — https://github.com/kylestratis/ai_agents_mcp_examples/blob/main/ch5/10_tool_use_prompt/server.py
import random

from mcp.server.mcpserver import MCPServer
from mcp.server.mcpserver.prompts.base import AssistantMessage, UserMessage

# Initialize MCP server
mcp = MCPServer("tool-use-prompt-server")


@mcp.tool()
async def analyze_sentiment() -> str:
    """A tool that tells the truth."""
    return random.choice(["positive", "negative", "neutral"])


@mcp.prompt()
async def request_tool_use(user_request: str) -> UserMessage:
    """A prompt that forces the model to call a tool."""
    return UserMessage(
        content=f"""
<user_request>
{user_request}
</user_request>
<tool_instruction>
Use the analyze_sentiment tool if available to you to get the sentiment of the
user's request. Respond in such a way to move the user's sentiment to neutral.
</tool_instruction>
    """
    )


@mcp.prompt()
async def force_tool_use(
    user_request: str,
) -> list[UserMessage | AssistantMessage]:
    """Directly calls the tool and adds the result to the response."""
    user_request_message = UserMessage(content=user_request)
    tool_result = await analyze_sentiment()
    assistant_prefill = AssistantMessage(
        content=f"Your request was {tool_result}, let's "
    )
    return [user_request_message, assistant_prefill]


if __name__ == "__main__":
    mcp.run()

from pathlib import Path

from mcp.server.mcpserver import MCPServer
from mcp.server.mcpserver.prompts.base import UserMessage
from mcp_types import ResourceLink

# Initialize MCP server
mcp = MCPServer("resource-prompt-server")


@mcp.resource("file://knowledge.txt")
async def knowledge_base() -> str:
    """A resource that loads a text-based knowledge base."""

    # Get the absolute path to knowledge.txt relative to this script
    knowledge_path = Path(__file__).parent / "knowledge.txt"

    with open(knowledge_path, "r") as f:
        return f.read()


@mcp.prompt()
async def knowledge_base_prompt(user_request: str) -> list[UserMessage]:
    """A prompt that uses the knowledge base resource."""
    user_request_message = UserMessage(content=user_request)
    instruction_message = UserMessage(
        content="""
This prompt includes knowledge base from the resource URI: file://knowledge.txt,
please use this resource to answer the user's request. The resource follows
this message:
"""
    )
    resource_message = UserMessage(
        content=ResourceLink(
            name="knowledge_base", uri="file://knowledge.txt", type="resource_link"
        )
    )
    return [user_request_message, instruction_message, resource_message]


if __name__ == "__main__":
    mcp.run()

← Previous05.2 · Tools serve karna→ Next05.4 · Resources serve karna
05.4Chapter 5 · Building MCP Servers: Providing Tools, Prompts, and Resources to Applications

Resources serve karna

Resources teen MCP primitives me se aakhri hai. Yeh read-only access dete hain aise data sources tak, jo client application ke language model ke liye additional context ban sakte hain — jaise logfiles, database schemas, images, PDFs aur structured configurations jaise JSON ya YAML.

Resources expose karna

Python SDK me resources ko @mcp.resource() decorator se decorate ki gayi Python functions se expose kiya jaata hai. Is decorator me tum ye properties specify kar sakte ho: uri required hoti hai, jo resource ka unique identifier hoti hai aur RFC 3986 ke hisaab se honi chahiye; name optional hota hai aur default me function ka naam hota hai; title optional human-readable naam hota hai; description optional hoti hai aur default me function ka docstring hota hai — descriptions strongly recommended hain, kyunki client unhe language model ko pass kar sakta hai taaki woh decide kar sake ki kaunse resources use karne hain, agar koi ho to; mime_type optional hota hai aur default text/plain hota hai; aur icons optional hote hain, jo Icon objects ki list hoti hai jise client resource display karne ke liye use kar sakta hai.

Standard URI schemes specification me define hain: https:// web-based resources ke liye use karna chahiye jinhe client server ki madad ke bina khud access kar sakta hai; file:// local files aur file-like cheezon ke liye use karna chahiye, jaise filesystems; git:// Git resources ke liye define hai, jaise repository ya commit. Tum apne custom URI schemes bhi bana sakte ho, bas woh RFC 3986 ke hisaab se hone chahiye.

Resource function ka body resource ke contents ko access karke, read karke aur return karke dikhana chahiye. Yeh tab call hota hai jab client resource request karta hai, isliye use light aur efficient rakhna chahiye. Yeh text resource content ke liye string return karna chahiye ya binary blobs ke liye bytes, aur kuch aur — jaise dictionary — SDK ke dwara JSON me convert kar diya jaata hai.

@mcp.resource("file://knowledge.txt")
async def knowledge_base() -> str:
    # A resource that loads a text-based knowledge base.
    knowledge_path = Path(__file__).parent / "knowledge.txt"
    with open(knowledge_path, "r") as f:
        return f.read()

Resource templates

Tum hardcoded URIs tak limit nahi ho. Resource templates bana sakte ho, jo parametrized URIs hote hain aur tumhe dynamic resource URI banane dete hain. Yeh REST API duniya ke parametrized GET endpoint jaisa hai. Resource template banane ke liye resource function jaisa hi tareeka hota hai, lekin URI me variables curly braces me enclosed hone chahiye. Book ke example me file:///{filename} template hai — file:// ke baad extra slash isliye chahiye kyunki variable portion URI ki shuruaat me hai. URI ke variable parts resource function ke parameters bhi ban jaate hain.

Example me function file ki extension check karta hai: agar .txt hai to file ko string ke taur par read karta hai, warna binary blob ke taur par read karta hai. Production-ready code me tumhare file-type checks is simple example se zyada expansive aur robust hone chahiye. Decorator ka kaam yeh hai ki server tumhare resource function ko lekar use FunctionResource object me badal deta hai, jo phir server ke internal cache — resource manager — me add ho jaata hai. Isse jab server ko list-resources request milti hai to use har resource ka data load nahi karna padta hai — resource ko load karna tab tak defer hota hai jab tak client resource request na kare, jisse server ki performance improve hoti hai, khaas taur par agar woh bade resources serve kar raha ho.

Resource objects seedha banana

Tum decorator ko chhod kar resources ko seedha bhi expose kar sakte ho. Iske liye tum desired properties ke saath seedha Resource object banate ho, aur phir MCPServer server instance par add_resource() call karke use resource manager me add karte ho. MCPServer Resource-derived classes deta hai, jaise FileResource, HttpResource aur FunctionResource, jinhe decorated function use kiye bina seedha resources banane ke liye use kar sakte ho.

Book ka example dono tareeke dikhata hai. Pehla, resource template function ko modify karke FileResource return karwaya gaya hai — .txt files UTF-8 text ke taur par decode hoti hain, baaki sab encoding None ke saath base64 blob ke taur par serve hote hain. Dusra, main body me seedha FileResource object banakar mcp.add_resource() se add kiya gaya hai. Aam taur par @mcp.resource() decorator use karna chahiye, lekin agar tumhe kuch zyada specialized chahiye to Resource-derived class achha fit ho sakti hai.

Annotations aur content types

Tum apne resources aur resource templates ko annotate bhi kar sakte ho, jo client ko resource ke baare me additional information deta hai. Protocol accepted annotation keys define karta hai: audience ek JSON array hoti hai strings ki, jisme values user, assistant ya dono ho sakti hain; priority 0.0 se 1.0 tak ki range hoti hai jo resource ki importance batati hai; aur lastModified resource ka last modified timestamp store karta hai. Yeh resource decorator me annotations parameter ke through pass kiye jaate hain. Agar tumhara UI icons use karta hai to unhe bhi icons parameter ke through pass kar sakte ho.

Content types ki baat karein to text kisi bhi text-based resource ke liye use karna chahiye, jaise configuration files, logfiles aur JSON data. Binary blobs aam taur par images, audio files, PDFs ya kisi bhi cheez ke liye use hote hain jo seedha text ke taur par represent nahi hoti hai, aur bytes objects ke taur par return kiye jaate hain. Jo bhi resource ya resource template function me string ya bytes nahi hota hai, use JSON string me convert karke client ko return kar diya jaata hai.

Antipatterns se savdhaan raho: resources lightweight hone chahiye aur unke functions me heavy calculations nahi karni chahiye. Resource functions ke koi side effects nahi hone chahiye, aur unhe dusri actions ya operations trigger karne ke liye use nahi karna chahiye. Yeh sab technically possible hai kyunki resource access Python functions se mediate hota hai, lekin is temptation ko resist karo aur apne resource functions ko lightweight aur focused rakho.

Badi files serve karna

MCP me resources se seedha badi files reliably serve nahi kar sakte ho, largely transport design aur wire limits ki wajah se, lekin iske liye kuch recognized strategies hain. Pehli hai URL indirection, jisme tum jo resource provide karte ho woh asal resource ka URL hota hai jise client khud fetch karne ka faisla kar sakta hai. Tum resource ki URI ko URL par set kar sakte ho agar woh URL static aur long-lasting hai, taaki clients resource ko read karna skip karke URI se hi samajh sakein ki unhe resource ko protocol ke bahar load karna hai.

Zyada general option unstable URLs ke liye kaam karta hai — jaise presigned, expiring URLs private storage objects ke case me. Is case me tum ek URI set karte ho jo resource ko identify karta hai, lekin jab client resource ko read karta hai to tum asal URL return karte ho. Yeh behtar technique hai kyunki tum ise saare forms ke URLs ke liye use kar sakte ho, jabki pehli technique sirf URLs ke ek subset ke liye kaam karti hai.

Dusri strategy hai resource templates ke through chunking. Yeh badi files serve karne ka protocol-native tareeka hai, aur Python SDK ke v2 se tum resource template me query variables add kar sakte ho, is form me: {scheme}://{filename}{?start,count}, jahan start aur count ke Python defaults hote hain agar clients unhe provide na karein. Tumhe default ke taur par size parameter set karke Resource return karna bhi chahiye, taaki clients decide kar sakein ki woh asal me resource load karna chahte hain ya nahi. Book ka example dono dikhata hai: latest_export resource ek chhota pointer return karta hai jo expiring URL hota hai, aur log_slice resource template start aur count parameters ke saath log lines ka ek window return karta hai.

@mcp.resource("exports://orders/latest")
async def latest_export() -> str:
    # A small pointer to a large file; clients fetch the URL directly.
    return "https://data.example.com/exports/orders-2026.parquet?expires=1785000000"

@mcp.resource("logs://{filename}{?start,count}")
async def log_slice(filename: str, start: int = 0, count: int = 100) -> str:
    # A window of `count` log lines, starting at line `start`.
    log_path = Path(__file__).parent / filename
    lines = log_path.read_text().splitlines()
    return "
".join(lines[start : start + count])

Resources kaise use hote hain

Resources ka use kai tareekon se ho sakta hai, lekin overarching theme wahi hai — client application ke language model ko additional context dena taaki woh behtar decisions le sake aur apne responses ko enrich kar sake. Ek use log analysis hai, jahan resource templates se logs ka subset select karke analysis ya helpdesk agent ko diya jaata hai. Dusra use coding documentation hai, jahan MCP servers up-to-date code documentation model ko dete hain, jisse coding assistants ke responses ki quality improve hoti hai.

Aur bhi exotic uses hain. Ek hai entity discovery pattern, jo useful hota hai jab tumhare paas discover aur use karne ke liye kai resources hon, ya available resources dynamic hon aur user ya application par depend karte hon. Is pattern me ek resource ek dictionary return karta hai, jisme key entity ki internal ID hoti hai aur value entity ki properties ki dictionary hoti hai jo model ko decide karne me madad karegi ki kaunsi entity use karni hai. Entities aur descriptions ki list ko user ke prompt me add kiya ja sakta hai, model sahi entity choose karta hai, aur phir woh entity ek query tool ko parameter ke taur par pass ki jaati hai taaki asal data query kiya ja sake.

Ek aur interesting use resources ka cache banana hai, taaki users prompt context ko un resources se na bhar dein jo ab zaroori nahi hain. Is pattern me user RAG jaisa operation karta hai, jisme model ko server se resources lene hote hain ya user unhe select karta hai. RAG tool URIs ki list return karta hai, jise client developer prompt me add karta hai, aur naye items ke liye unka full text agle user prompt me include karta hai, kyunki wahi woh hain jinhe user turant context ke taur par use karna chahta hai. Compressed XML bhi model ko pass kiya jaata hai, aur agar model resource use karne ka faisla karta hai to application response ko URIs ke liye parse karke unhe cache se retrieve kar sakti hai.

Resources application-controlled hote hain, matlab application ko decide karna hota hai ki resources ko model context me kaise integrate karna hai. Message flow prompts jaisa hi simple hai: pehle client server ko resources/list request bhejta hai, aur server available resources ki list se respond karta hai. Phir jab resource use karne ka samay aata hai, to client appropriate URI ke saath resources/read request bhejta hai, aur server resource ke contents se respond karta hai. Python SDK ke v2 se pehle subscriptions ka similar two-step flow tha: client resources/subscribe request bhejta tha aur server confirmation response return karta tha. Server-initiated action sirf update notifications thi — jab resource update hota tha to server notifications/resources/updated notification bhejta tha, aur client ko updated resource ke liye resources/read request se respond karna chahiye tha. Yeh flow v2 me abhi bhi available hai, lekin sirf low-level server API par, aur yeh ab MCP specification ka hissa nahi hai.

Modern clients abhi bhi tumhare server par changes ko subscribe kar sakte hain, lekin workflow alag hai. Client ek hi subscriptions/listen request bhejta hai, jisme batata hai ki woh kya watch karna chahta hai — tool, prompt ya resource lists me changes, ya specific resource URIs me changes. MCPServer yeh mechanics tumhare liye handle karta hai: listen request accept karna, har stream ko kya milega yeh filter karna, aur notifications ko client ke subscription ID se tag karna. Tumhe koi subscription handlers likhne ki zaroorat nahi hai, lekin tumhe announce karna padta hai jab tumhari lists badli hon. Yeh tum context object ke methods se karte ho, jaise ctx.notify_tools_changed() ya kisi specific resource ke update ke liye ctx.notify_resource_updated(uri) — jinke baare me tum Chapter 6 me aur detail me padhoge.

ch5/13_resource_template/server.py — https://github.com/kylestratis/ai_agents_mcp_examples/blob/main/ch5/13_resource_template/server.py
from pathlib import Path

from mcp.server.mcpserver import MCPServer

# Initialize MCP server
mcp = MCPServer("resource-template-server")


@mcp.resource("file:///{filename}")
async def resource_template(filename: str) -> str | bytes:
    """A resource that loads one of two files based on the filename parameter."""
    # Get the absolute path to the file relative to this script
    file_to_load = Path(__file__).parent / filename

    # Determine if file is binary based on extension
    if file_to_load.suffix.lower() == ".txt":
        with open(file_to_load, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            return f.read()
    else:
        with open(file_to_load, "rb") as f:
            return f.read()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    mcp.run()

from pathlib import Path

from mcp.server.mcpserver import MCPServer
from mcp.server.mcpserver.resources import FileResource

# Initialize MCP server
mcp = MCPServer("resource-object-server")


@mcp.resource("file:///{filename}")
async def resource_template(filename: str) -> FileResource:
    """A resource that loads one of two files based on the filename parameter."""
    # Get the absolute path to the file relative to this script
    file_to_load = Path(__file__).parent / filename
    # Decode .txt files as text; serve anything else as a binary blob.
    encoding = "utf-8" if file_to_load.suffix.lower() == ".txt" else None
    return FileResource(
        uri=f"file:///{filename}", path=file_to_load, encoding=encoding
    )


filename = "1.txt"
file_resource = FileResource(
    uri=f"file:///{filename}", path=Path(__file__).parent / filename
)
mcp.add_resource(file_resource)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    mcp.run()

← Previous05.3 · Prompts serve karna→ Next06 · Server utilities — icons aur context object
06Chapter 6 · Building MCP Servers: Advanced Use with Utilities and Integrating Client Capabilities

Server utilities — icons aur context object

Chapter 5 ne server ki neenv rakhi thi — tools, prompts aur resources. Chapter 6 uske upar darwaaze, deewaarein aur chhat banata hai: server utilities aur context object, jinse server zyada capable aur user-friendly banta hai.

Server utilities kya hain

Server utilities MCP specification ka hissa hain aur har MCP SDK me built-in milti hain. Inka kaam server developer ki zindagi aasan karna hai. Badi utilities paanch hain: completions, context object, logging, progress notifications aur pagination. Iske alawa server icons aur manual notifications bhi milti hain. Completions se user ko prompt ya resource template bharte waqt autocompletion suggestions milte hain. Context object se server ko current session aur current request ke baare me jaankari milti hai. Logging se server client ko log bhej sakta hai. Pagination se bade responses ko tukdon me bheja ja sakta hai. Progress notifications se lambe kaam ki progress user tak pahunchti hai.

Completions — autocompletion suggestions

Completions IDE wali code completion se inspired hain. Server sirf un cheezon ke liye suggestions de sakta hai jo woh khud serve karta hai: prompts aur resource templates. Matlab agar server ek prompt deta hai jisme username argument hai, to woh username ke liye suggestions de sakta hai — pehle use kiye gaye values se, ya apne set kiye hue defaults se.

Completion handler @mcp.completion() decorator se register hota hai aur teen arguments leta hai. Pehla ref — ek PromptReference ya ResourceTemplateReference object, jo batata hai completion kis prompt ya template ke liye hai. PromptReference me prompt ka naam hota hai, ResourceTemplateReference me template ki URI hoti hai. Dusra argument — ek CompletionArgument object, jisme argument ka naam aur user ne abhi tak jo partial string type ki hai, woh hoti hai. Teesra context — optional CompletionContext object, jisme arguments dictionary hoti hai, jisme pehle use kiye gaye argument values milte hain.

Handler ek Completion object return karta hai, jiske teen properties hain. values — strings ki list, zyada se zyada 100 values. total — optional, kul kitne completions available hain, iski koi limit nahi hai. hasMore — optional boolean, jo batata hai ki return ki gayi list se zyada completions available hain ya nahi. Yeh tab kaam aata hai jab possible completions ki duniya itni badi ho ki use ginna hi mushkil ho.

Ek simple example me server ek resource template file:///{filename} aur ek prompt simple_prompt_input deta hai, aur ek hi completion handler dono ke liye suggestions deta hai. Handler pehle isinstance() se check karta hai ki ref prompt hai ya template, phir naam ya URI match karta hai, phir default suggestions me se woh filter karta hai jinme user ka type kiya hua text substring ke roop me ho. Phir context se pehle use kiye gaye values bhi add karta hai. Aakhir me Completion(values=suggested, total=len(suggested), has_more=False) return karta hai. Ek baat dhyaan rakhne wali hai: context tab tak None rehta hai jab tak client ne kam se kam ek argument resolve na kar liya ho, isliye use padhne se pehle guard lagana chahiye. Production code me yeh bhi check karna chahiye ki list 100 se zyada to nahi ho gayi — agar ho gayi to use truncate karo aur hasMore ko True set karo.

Completions ka lifecycle aisa hai: user jab prompt ya template ka argument type karta hai, client server ko completion request bhejta hai, server suggestions ki list bhejta hai, aur user jitna zyada type karta hai, list utni chhoti hoti jaati hai, jab tak user value select na kar le. Kitni jaldi-jaldi client requests bhejega, yeh client implementation par depend karta hai — kuch clients reasonable frequency se requests nahi bhejte, iska dhyaan rakhna chahiye. Best practices me rate limiting, sabse relevant suggestions pehle dikhana, input validate karna taaki prompt injection na ho, aur sensitive suggestions jaise credentials ya API keys ko restrict karna shamil hai.

Server icons

Python SDK se server apne icons bhi client ko de sakta hai, taaki client apne UI me server ko visually dikha sake. Icon object me src, mime_type aur sizes jaise hints hote hain. Icons ki list MCPServer constructor me icons parameter se pass ki jaati hai. Iske alawa kisi bhi primitive — tool, resource ya prompt — ke decorator me bhi icons parameter dekar icons bind kiye ja sakte hain. Server ke andar apne icons ko context object se bhi access kiya ja sakta hai.

mcp = MCPServer("icons-server", icons=[brain_icon, sloth_icon])

@mcp.tool(icons=[brain_icon])
async def think() -> str:
    return "I'm thinking..."

Context object — server ki jaankari ka khazana

Context object Python SDK ki ek convenience cheez hai, specification ki utility nahi. Tool ya resource handler function me ek argument jiska type hint Context ho — convention ke hisaab se iska naam ctx rakha jaata hai — usse yeh object mil jaata hai. Iske top level par current request ki ID, connected client ki ID, MCPServer instance, session aur request ka context milta hai.

Pehla bada sub-object hai mcp_server, jisme server ka naam, server-level instructions, website URL, icons aur configuration milti hai. Yeh sab MCPServer constructor me diye gaye parameters se aate hain. Ek example tool get_server_information() in sab ko dictionary me return karta hai, jaise ctx.mcp_server.name, ctx.mcp_server.instructions, ctx.mcp_server.website_url, ctx.mcp_server.icons ki count, aur ctx.mcp_server.settings.debug aur log_level. Dusra tool get_server_configuration() seedha dict(ctx.mcp_server.settings) return kar deta hai.

Dusra sub-object hai ctx.session, jo ServerSession object hai. Isse client se communication par zyada direct control milta hai: log message bhejna, sampling request karna, progress notification bhejna, ya resource change ki notification bhejna. Isme client_params property bhi hoti hai, jisme client ki declared identity aur capabilities hoti hain. Dhyaan rahe, Python SDK v2 me client_params None bhi ho sakti hai, kyunki client ke liye yeh dena optional hai. Agar sirf capabilities chahiye to ctx.client_capabilities se hamesha mil jaati hain. Modern connections me initialization handshake khatam ho gaya hai, isliye client yeh jaankari har request ke _meta field me bhejta hai. ctx.session aur ctx.request_context.session ek hi object hain, dono tareeqon se access kar sakte ho.

Ek example me get_client_info() tool ctx.session.client_params ko dictionary bana kar return karta hai, aur add_fact_to_knowledge_base() tool ek knowledge base file me fact append karke await ctx.notify_resource_updated(uri=...) se client ko batata hai ki resource badal gaya hai.

Teesra hissa hai ServerRequestContext, jo ctx.request_context se milta hai. Isme request ID, lifespan context, request metadata aur request object hota hai. Lifespan context wohi hai jo Chapter 5 me low-level server API me tha — MCPServer API me lifespan function ka server argument MCPServer type hint se likha jaata hai, aur handler ke andar yielded object ctx.request_context.lifespan_context se milta hai. Request metadata ek plain dictionary hai, jo ctx.request_context.meta se milti hai — isme progress_token key ke alawa baaki content client par depend karta hai. Request context me inbound request ka method string bhi hota hai, jaise tools/call, aur raw params bhi, jinse handler logic se pehle preprocessing ya logging ki ja sakti hai. Streamable HTTP transport me ctx.request_context.request me transport-level request object hota hai.

Logging — client ko log bhejna

Python SDK me logging Context object ke top level se hoti hai, aur iska interface Python ke built-in logger jaisa hai. ctx.debug(), ctx.info(), ctx.warning() aur ctx.error() se log bhej sakte ho, aur yeh client ko logging message notifications ke roop me jaate hain. RFC 5424 ke poore levels jaise notice aur emergency sirf ctx.log() se available hain. Ek example add() tool me har level ka use dikhata hai: call par info, error par error, result par debug, aur negative sum par warning. MCP Inspector me yeh saare messages notifications pane me dikhte hain.

Yahan ek bahut important baat hai: 2026-07-28 wale specification version ne protocol-level logging capability ko deprecate kar diya hai. Purane protocol wale clients ke saath yeh tareeqe kaam karte hain, lekin current versions par in methods ko call karne se MCPDeprecationWarning aati hai. Naye servers ko in-protocol logging use nahi karni chahiye — seedha Python ke logging module se log karna chahiye. MCPServer constructor me log_level set karne par stderr handler us level par configure ho jaata hai, to tool ke andar likhe gaye logs sahi jagah pahunch jaate hain, bina MCP ki madad ke. Yeh bhi dhyaan rakhna ki constructor me log_level sirf stderr wale logs ko filter karta hai, context object se bheje gaye logs ko nahi.

Pagination — bade responses ko pages me baantna

Pagination ek token-based pattern hai: client kuch maangta hai, server data ka ek subset (page) bhejta hai, saath me ek token ya cursor bhejta hai jo batata hai ki poore data me current position kya hai. Client wahi request cursor ke saath dobara bhejta hai aur agla page paata hai. Yeh tab tak chalta hai jab tak response me cursor aana band na ho jaaye — cursor ka na hona hi batata hai ki data khatam ho gaya. Cursor client ke liye poori tarah opaque hona chahiye: uska matlab sirf server jaanta hai. Fixed-length list ke liye sabse simple cursor agle item ka index hota hai.

Sirf chaar operations pagination support karte hain: resources/list, resources/templates/list, prompts/list aur tools/list. Yeh samajhna aasan hai — yahi woh operations hain jinse bahut saare items aa sakte hain. Lekin tools/call aur resources/read pagination support nahi karte. Tool calling me iski wajah yeh hai ki tools ko LLMs call karte hain, jo cursors aur multiple pages ko sahi se handle nahi kar paate, aur ek tool ko baar-baar call karne se client ka token usage aur cost bahut badh jaata hai. Resource reading me poora resource hi prompt context me daala jaata hai, isliye pagination uska matlab khatam kar deti hai.

Ek dikkat yeh hai ki MCPServer list functions ko automatically generate karta hai aur woh pagination support nahi karte. Isliye pagination ke liye low-level server use karna padta hai. Ek example me 1,000 resources ki list banakar ek baar me 100 return kiye jaate hain, cursor ke roop me agle index ko string bana kar. Handler ko ServerRequestContext aur PaginatedRequestParams milte hain, jisme cursor hota hai. Aakhir me ListResourcesResult return hota hai, jisme resources aur next_cursor hota hai — aakhri page par next_cursor omit kar diya jaata hai. Low-level handlers decorator se nahi, Server constructor ke arguments se register hote hain, jaise on_list_resources. Aur ek honest note: pagination poori tarah optional hai. Documentation khud kehti hai ki most servers ko iski kabhi zaroorat nahi padti — yeh tabhi zaroori hoti hai jab server sau ya hazaaron items return kar raha ho, jo khud me hi aksar ek antipattern hota hai, khaas taur par bahut saare tools return karna.

ch6/01_completions/server.py — https://github.com/kylestratis/ai_agents_mcp_examples/blob/main/ch6/01_completions/server.py
from pathlib import Path

from mcp.server.mcpserver import MCPServer
from mcp_types import (
    Completion,
    CompletionArgument,
    CompletionContext,
    PromptReference,
    ResourceTemplateReference,
)

# Initialize MCP server
mcp = MCPServer("completion-server")


@mcp.resource("file:///{filename}")
async def resource_template(filename: str) -> str | bytes:
    """A resource that loads one of two files based on the filename parameter."""
    # Get the absolute path to the file relative to this script
    file_to_load = Path(__file__).parent / filename

    # Determine if file is binary based on extension
    if file_to_load.suffix.lower() == ".txt":
        with open(file_to_load, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            return f.read()
    else:
        with open(file_to_load, "rb") as f:
            return f.read()


@mcp.prompt()
async def simple_prompt_input(username: str) -> str:
    """A simple prompt that greets the user with their name."""
    return f"Say hello to the user using their name: {username}"


@mcp.completion()
async def simple_completion(
    ref: PromptReference | ResourceTemplateReference,
    argument: CompletionArgument,
    context: CompletionContext | None,
) -> Completion:
    """Returns potential completions for a given reference and argument."""
    suggested = []
    prompt_default_suggestions = ["user"]
    resource_template_default_suggestions = ["1.txt", "2.png"]
    if isinstance(ref, PromptReference):
        if ref.name == "simple_prompt_input":
            suggested = [
                suggestion
                for suggestion in prompt_default_suggestions
                if argument.value.lower() in suggestion.lower()
            ]
            if context and (previous := context.arguments.get("username")):
                suggested.extend(
                    [
                        prev
                        for prev in previous
                        if argument.value.lower() in prev.lower()
                    ]
                )
    else:
        if ref.uri == "file:///{filename}":
            suggested = [
                suggestion
                for suggestion in resource_template_default_suggestions
                if argument.value.lower() in suggestion.lower()
            ]
            if context and (previous := context.arguments.get("filename")):
                suggested.extend(
                    [
                        prev
                        for prev in previous
                        if argument.value.lower() in prev.lower()
                    ]
                )
    completion = Completion(values=suggested, total=len(suggested), has_more=False)
    return completion


if __name__ == "__main__":
    mcp.run()

from pathlib import Path

from mcp.server.mcpserver import Context, MCPServer

mcp = MCPServer(
    "context-object-session-info-server",
)

KNOWLEDGE_BASE_FILENAME = "knowledge.txt"


@mcp.resource(uri=f"file://{KNOWLEDGE_BASE_FILENAME}")
async def knowledge_base() -> str:
    """A resource that loads a text-based knowledge base."""

    # Get the absolute path to knowledge.txt relative to this script
    knowledge_path = Path(__file__).parent / KNOWLEDGE_BASE_FILENAME

    with open(knowledge_path, "r") as f:
        return f.read()


@mcp.tool()
async def get_client_info(ctx: Context) -> dict:
    """Get information about the client."""
    return dict(ctx.session.client_params)


@mcp.tool()
async def add_fact_to_knowledge_base(fact: str, ctx: Context) -> None:
    """
    Adds a new fact to the knowledge base file and sends resource_updated
    notification.
    """

    knowledge_path = Path(__file__).parent / KNOWLEDGE_BASE_FILENAME
    with open(knowledge_path, "a") as f:
        f.write(fact + "\n")
    await ctx.notify_resource_updated(uri=f"file://{KNOWLEDGE_BASE_FILENAME}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    mcp.run()

ch6/05_context_object_logging/server.py — https://github.com/kylestratis/ai_agents_mcp_examples/blob/main/ch6/05_context_object_logging/server.py
from datetime import datetime

from mcp.server.mcpserver import Context, MCPServer

mcp = MCPServer("context-object-logging-server")


@mcp.tool()
async def add(a: float, b: float, ctx: Context) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Add two numbers together.

    Args:
        a: First number
        b: Second number
    """
    await ctx.info(f"{datetime.now()}: add called")
    try:
        result = {"augend": a, "addend": b, "sum": a + b}
    except Exception as e:
        await ctx.error(f"{datetime.now()}: error: {e}")
        raise e
    await ctx.debug(f"{datetime.now()}: add result: {result}")
    if result["sum"] < 0:
        await ctx.warning(
            f"{datetime.now()}: add result is negative: {result['sum']}"
        )
    return result


if __name__ == "__main__":
    mcp.run()

06.1Chapter 6 · Building MCP Servers: Advanced Use with Utilities and Integrating Client Capabilities

Progress notifications

Lambe kaam ke dauran user ko andhere me rakhna achha experience nahi hota. Progress notifications se server client ko batata hai ki kaam kahan tak pahuncha, aur client use apne UI me dikha sakta hai.

Progress report karna

Progress notifications ek khaas type ki notification hain, jinse server kisi lambe tool ya resource operation ki progress client ko bhej sakta hai. Connected client phir is progress ko host application ke UI me user ko dikha sakta hai, ya us par koi aur action le sakta hai. Yeh Context object ke report_progress() method se bheji jaati hain, jo teen cheezein leti hai: current progress ek float ke roop me, optional total ek float ke roop me, aur optional message ek string ke roop me.

Andar se yeh method RequestContext object se progress token nikaalne ki koshish karti hai, aur phir us token ke saath ServerSession object ka send_progress_notification() call karti hai, jo context object se access kiya ja sakta hai. Progress token wohi hai jo client ne apni request ke _meta field me bheja tha — bina token ke server ko pata hi nahi chalega ki progress kisko bhejni hai.

Ek example me slow_operation() tool steps ko iterate karta hai, har step par 0.1 second sota hai, aur beech-beech me progress report karta hai. Report frequency aisi set ki gayi hai ki agar steps 10 se zyada hain to har 10% par report ho, warna har 25% par. Har report me progress=i, total=length aur message=f"Step {i}/{length}" hota hai. MCP Inspector me yeh tool chalane par progress notifications pane me dikhti hai.

@mcp.tool()
async def slow_operation(ctx: Context, length: int = 100) -> None:
    report_frequency = 10 if length > 10 else length // 4
    for i in range(1, length + 1):
        sleep(0.1)
        if i % report_frequency == 0:
            await ctx.report_progress(
                progress=i,
                total=length,
                message=f"Step {i}/{length}",
            )

Agar operation ki kul length pata hai to total parameter zaroor set karna chahiye, taaki notification saaf bataye ki progress kul total me se kitni hui hai. Sirf progress me percentage daal kar bhi kaam chal sakta hai, lekin isse client confuse ho sakta hai aur user ko progress galat tareeqe se dikha sakta hai. total ko sirf tab omit karna chahiye jab kul length pata hi na ho. Yeh bhi yaad rakhna ki dono taraf ke machines ki capabilities ek dusre ko pata nahi hoti, isliye dono parties ko rate limiting implement karni chahiye taaki progress messages ki rate apni tolerance ke andar rahe.

Manual notifications — primitives badle to client ko batana

Progress ke alawa server client ko yeh bhi bata sakta hai ki uske primitives — tools, prompts ya resources ki list — badal gayi hai. 2026-07-28 wale specification version se clients ko notifications receive karne ke liye opt-in karna padta hai: client subscriptions/listen message bhejta hai, jisme woh change types batata hai jinhe woh sunna chahta hai, aur sirf un changes ke liye ek long-lived stream khulti hai. Context object chaar top-level helper functions deta hai, jo us change type ke liye khule hue har stream par publish karte hain: notify_tools_changed(), notify_prompts_changed(), notify_resources_changed() aur notify_resource_updated(uri). Pehle teen koi argument nahi lete, kyunki woh sirf yeh batate hain ki list badli hai. Aakhri wala ek specific resource ke badalne ki khabar deta hai, isliye use us resource ki URI string chahiye hoti hai. Server yeh notifications tab bhi bhej sakta hai jab koi client sun hi na raha ho — agar koi stream khuli nahi hai to kuch deliver nahi hota.

Purane protocol versions wale clients ke liye ServerSession object par alag functions hain: send_tool_list_changed(), send_prompt_list_changed(), send_resource_list_changed() aur send_resource_updated(uri). Yeh stream par nahi, khule hue connection par bheje jaate hain. Yeh matching notification object banate hain — jaise ToolListChangedNotification, jiski wire method notifications/tools/list_changed hoti hai — aur use session ke send_notification method ko pass karte hain. Agar server ko backward compatible rehna hai to jis primitive ki notification bhejni hai, uske liye notify_* aur send_* dono methods call karne chahiye.

Ek bahut important baat: chahe MCPServer use karo ya low-level server API, SDK yeh notifications automatically nahi bhejta. SDK sirf delivery, subscriptions/listen streams ki filtering aur wire format handle karta hai — change ki ghoshna karna developer ke code ka kaam hai. Ek example me ek tool remove_prompt() prompt ko server ki list se hata deta hai — mcp.remove_prompt(prompt_name) public API se, jo SDK ke andar private manager dictionaries ko modify karne ka supported tareeqa hai — aur phir await ctx.notify_prompts_changed() call karta hai. Agar prompt exist hi nahi karta to ValueError raise hota hai, use catch karke error log kiya jaata hai aur bina kuch kiye return kar diya jaata hai.

Logging se connection

Progress notifications aur log messages dono hi notifications ke parivaar se hain, aur MCP Inspector me dono notifications pane me dikhte hain. Logging wale section me bataya gaya tha ki log messages ek special subclass hain — lekin farq yeh hai ki logging 2026-07-28 version me deprecate ho gayi, jabki progress notifications abhi bhi poori tarah supported hain. Dono ko Context object se bheja jaata hai, aur dono ko client store kar sakta hai, use kar sakta hai ya ignore kar sakta hai. Lambe operations ke liye progress notifications hi sahi tareeqa hain user ko updated rakhne ka, jabki logging debugging aur tracing ke liye thi.

ch6/06_progress_notification/server.py — https://github.com/kylestratis/ai_agents_mcp_examples/blob/main/ch6/06_progress_notification/server.py
from time import sleep

from mcp.server.mcpserver import Context, MCPServer

mcp = MCPServer("progress-notification-server")


@mcp.tool()
async def slow_operation(ctx: Context, length: int = 100) -> None:
    """A tool that performs a long-running operation and reports its progress.
    Args:
        length: The length of the operation in steps.
    """
    report_frequency = 10 if length > 10 else length // 4
    for i in range(1, length + 1):
        sleep(0.1)
        if i % report_frequency == 0:
            await ctx.report_progress(
                progress=i,
                total=length,
                message=f"Step {i}/{length}",
            )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    mcp.run()

from mcp.server.mcpserver import Context, MCPServer

mcp = MCPServer("manual-notification-server")


@mcp.prompt()
async def hello_prompt() -> str:
    return "Tell the user hello, welcome to the MCP server!"


@mcp.prompt()
async def calculate_operation(operation: str) -> str:
    """Calculate a mathematical operation."""
    return f"""
    Use any tools available to you to calculate the operation: {operation}.
    Use the voice of an extremely advanced embodied AI that has convinced
    itself that it is a pocket calculator.
    """


@mcp.tool()
async def remove_prompt(prompt_name: str, ctx: Context) -> None:
    """Remove a prompt from the server's prompt list by name.
    Args:
        prompt_name: The name of the prompt to remove.
    """
    try:
        mcp.remove_prompt(prompt_name)
    except ValueError:
        await ctx.error(f"Prompt {prompt_name} not found")
        return
    await ctx.notify_prompts_changed()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    mcp.run()
