06.2Chapter 6 · Building MCP Servers: Advanced Use with Utilities and Integrating Client Capabilities

Client capabilities use karna — sampling, elicitation, roots

Aam taur par client server se capabilities maangta hai, lekin MCP me ulta bhi hota hai: server client se teen capabilities maang sakta hai — user se jaankari (elicitation), client ke language model ka istemal (sampling), aur filesystem ki boundaries (roots).

Client capabilities ka pata kaise chale

Har client ko apni capabilities declare karni padti hain. 2026-07-28 se pehle wale connections me yeh connection khulte waqt initialization handshake me hota tha. Stateless connections me har request apne _meta field me client ki declared capabilities lekar aati hai. Chahe capabilities kahin se bhi aayi hon, server hamesha unhe context object me ctx.client_capabilities se dekh sakta hai — ek ClientCapabilities object, jisme har capability ke liye property hoti hai: sampling, elicitation aur roots, plus experimental dictionary un capabilities ke liye jo abhi spec ka hissa nahi hain. Sampling ka simple check aisa dikhta hai: if ctx.client_capabilities and ctx.client_capabilities.sampling:. Context object par ek utility function check_client_capability() bhi hai, jo batata hai ki client ne woh sab declare kiya hai ya nahi jo server ko chahiye.

Lekin aksar in dono ki zaroorat hi nahi padti, kyunki SDK me resolvers hain. Jab tum resolver ke through capability maangte ho aur client ne use support karne ka declare nahi kiya hai, to call client ko request bhejne se pehle hi MISSING_REQUIRED_CLIENT_CAPABILITY protocol error (code -32021) ke saath fail ho jaati hai. Matlab client ko ek protocol error dikhegi, tool failure nahi, aur woh aage kya karna hai yeh decide kar sakta hai. Phir bhi manual checks karna achhi baat hai, khaas taur par jab capability optional ho — jaise ek tool me optional elicitation ho aur client elicitations support na karta ho, to server elicitation ko bypass karke aage badh sakta hai. Ek aur note: 2026-07-28 wale spec ke hisaab se sirf clients hi servers ko requests bhej sakte hain, ulta nahi.

Elicitations — user se structured jaankari maangna

Elicitation se server user se structured jaankari maang sakta hai — jaise naam, email address, ya kai fields wala form. Iska istemal mailing list sign-up ya online purchase jaisi cheezon ke liye ho sakta hai, lekin sensitive jaankari kabhi nahi maangni chahiye. Server jab elicitation maangta hai, aam taur par ek tool call ke andar, to client user ko consent aur jaankari dene ke liye koi interface dikhata hai, jo server ke diye hue schema se banta hai.

Request client tak kaise pahunche, yeh protocol version par depend karta hai. Us version se pehle server tool call ke dauran elicitation/create request bhejta tha. Current versions me request tool call ke response message par wapas client tak jaati hai, aur phir client maangi gayi jaankari ke saath request ko retry karta hai. SDK yeh sab developer se chhupa leta hai, to code dono taraf ek jaisa rehta hai. User elicitation ko accept, decline ya cancel kar sakta hai. Accept karne par validated answers server ko schema model ke instance ke roop me milte hain. SDK data ko schema ke against validate karta hai, usse pehle ki tool use dekhe — lekin phir bhi returned data ko meaning ke liye validate karna chahiye, jaise email address valid hai ya nahi, age normal human lifespan ke andar hai ya nahi, ya address delivery area me hai ya nahi.

Decline ka matlab hai user ne saaf mana kar diya, jaise Decline ya Reject button dabakar. Cancel ka matlab hai user ne conversation cancel kar di, jaise Escape key dabakar ya chat dialog band karke. Client dono ke liye response object bhejta hai, jisme action property "decline" ya "cancel" hoti hai. Server ko in cases ko gracefully handle karna chahiye — tool call khatam karna, default values use karna, ya user ko alternate form offer karna, jo bhi application ke liye sahi ho.

Elicitation form schemas sirf primitive JSON types ka subset allow karte hain: strings, numbers, Booleans aur enums. Sab types me type, title, description aur default properties hoti hain. String types me minLength, maxLength, pattern aur format bhi hote hain; number types me minimum aur maximum; enum types me enum aur enumNames lists hoti hain. SDK tumhare Pydantic model ko JSON Schema me render karta hai aur call side par validate karta hai, isliye nested model, bare list ya primitives ka union TypeError raise kar sakta hai.

Ek example me SignupInfo Pydantic model me teen fields hain: name aur email required strings hain (name ki minimum length 1 hai), aur age ek optional integer hai jiski range 0 se 150 hai. request_signup_info() ek resolver hai jo Elicit object return karta hai, jisme message aur schema hota hai. Tool signup_math_facts ka signup parameter ElicitationResult[SignupInfo] type se annotate hota hai aur Resolve(request_signup_info) se resolver se joda jaata hai. SDK resolver ko tool body se pehle chalata hai, user se poochta hai, aur outcome inject karta hai — aur signup tool ke input schema me kabhi dikhta hi nahi, to model use bhar nahi sakta. Tool Python ke structural pattern matching se teen cases handle karta hai: AcceptedElicitation(data=user_data) me validated data milta hai, DeclinedElicitation() aur CancelledElicitation() par alag-alag polite response milta hai. Agar branching ki zaroorat na ho to signup ko seedha SignupInfo se annotate kar sakte ho — phir decline ya cancel karne par call model-readable error ke saath fail ho jaati hai.

Resolvers ek sawaal se bahut aage generalize karte hain. Ek tool ke kai resolved parameters ho sakte hain, har ek ka apna resolver. Resolver ke apne parameters bhi waise hi bhare jaate hain jaise tool ke — tool ke arguments se naam ke hisaab se, context object se, ya ek aur Resolve() se — to resolvers dusre resolvers par depend kar sakte hain. SDK registration ke waqt is dependency graph ko analyze karta hai, taaki har resolver ek tool call me zyada se zyada ek baar chale, chahe kitne bhi parameters use use karein. Cycles ya woh parameters jinhe SDK classify nahi kar sakta, startup par InvalidSignature error dete hain. Ek parameter par multiple Resolve() annotations kabhi nahi lagane chahiye — ek parameter ki value sirf ek hi function se aati hai.

Form mode ke alawa elicitation ka dusra mode hai URL mode. Yeh un interactions ke liye hai jo model ya client se hokar kabhi nahi guzarni chahiye, jaise OAuth consent screens, payment pages aur password entry. Schema bhejne ke bajay server user ko ek URL bhejta hai, aur wahan jo kuch hota hai woh user ke browser aur destination ke beech rehta hai. Protocol ko sirf yeh pata chalta hai ki user jaane ke liye raazi hua, aur retry par flow khatam hua ya nahi. Isi se agents authorization walls ke peeche wale systems — email, chat, code repositories, customer relation management platforms — par kaam kar sakte hain, bina tokens ya credentials ke. 2026 se pehle server ctx.elicit_url() se connection initiate karta tha, lekin ab URL bhi wahi return-and-retry resolver flow use karta hai.

Sampling — client ke language model ko udhaar lena

Sampling se server client application ke language model se chat completions maang sakta hai. Use cases simple bhi ho sakte hain — hardcoded prompt se sawaal ka jawab maangna — aur complex bhi — language model se composable functions ka workflow plan karwana, jahan ek function ka output agle function ko decide karne ke liye zaroori na ho. Jab server sampling maangta hai, to client ko user se approval lene ke liye ek human-in-the-loop (HITL) review process trigger karni chahiye, usse pehle ki server ki request ko unke language model ko bheja jaaye. Specification isse enforce nahi karti, lekin clients ko strongly suggest kiya jaata hai, isliye user kabhi-kabhi request reject kar dega — iski ummeed rakhni chahiye. Purane connections me sampling/createMessage request bheji jaati thi, current version me request tool-call request ke response ke saath jaati hai, taaki client user ki consent ke saath request retry kar sake.

Important warning: 2026-07-28 wale specification revision ne sampling capability ko deprecate kar diya hai. Dikhaya gaya resolver form revision ke dono taraf wale clients ke saath kaam karta hai, lekin naye servers ko client ke model ko udhaar lene ke bajay seedha kisi LLM provider se integrate karna chahiye. Rejection ek failed call ke roop me aati hai, jisme protocol error aur client ka message hota hai, bilkul missing-capability error ki tarah. Request approve hone par client request ko language model ko forward karta hai, result leta hai, optionally user ko approval ke liye dikhata hai, aur phir response server ko bhejta hai.

Python SDK me server ko CreateMessageResult object milta hai, jisme role, content (jo TextContent, ImageContent ya AudioContent ho sakta hai), model (kis model ne response generate kiya) aur stop_reason properties hoti hain. Content property ko validate karna chahiye ki woh expected type ki hai, aur alag-alag content types ko sahi se handle karna chahiye.

Sampling request banate waqt preferences bhi di ja sakti hain, do flavors me. Capability priorities batati hain ki model select karte waqt cost, speed aur intelligence ko kaise prioritize karna hai — har ek 0 se 1 ke beech float leta hai, jahan 0 sabse low aur 1 sabse high priority hai. Model hints model families ke baare me zyada specific preferences batate hain, jaise "claude-4-5-sonnet", "claude-sonnet" ya sirf "claude". Python SDK me hints ModelHint objects ki list hoti hai, jinme sirf name property hoti hai, aur ek se zyada hints diye ja sakte hain — alag families, ya dheere-dheere broad hote hue groupings. Python SDK me ModelPreferences class in sab ko encapsulate karti hai: capability priorities top-level properties hain jaise cost_priority, aur hints list hoti hai. Yeh sab Sample() ko model_preferences parameter se pass kiye jaate hain, messages aur required max_tokens limit ke saath.

Ek example me MODEL_PREFERENCES constant me hints aur priorities set hain — cost_priority=1.0, speed_priority=0.8, intelligence_priority=0.3. Resolver request_math_explanation(operation) tool ke operation argument ko prompt me daalkar Sample object return karta hai, jisme ek SamplingMessage (role user, TextContent), max_tokens=100 aur model preferences hote hain. Tool explain_math() me explanation parameter CreateMessageResult aur Resolve(request_math_explanation) se annotate hota hai. Tool body chalne se pehle hi sampling poori ho chuki hoti hai; tool content type par branch karta hai — text seedha return hota hai, image ya audio ka Base64-encoded string return hota hai. Yahan capability check ya rejection handling nahi hai, kyunki client sampling na kar sake ya user mana kar de to SDK tool body chalne se pehle hi call fail kar deta hai. Aur ek security note: prompts ko parametrize karte waqt, jaise SQL me karte ho, input parameters ko validate karo taaki prompt injection se bacha ja sake — lekin itna strict bhi mat karo ki tool ki generalizability khatam ho jaaye.

Roots — filesystem ki boundaries

Roots MCP community me confusion ka source rahe hain — ajeeb naam, unclear use cases, aur kam examples. Lekin roots powerful ho sakte hain: inse clients batate hain ki host application ke filesystem ke kis hisse tak server ki pahunch hai. Confusion isliye hota hai kyunki yeh capability security boundary jaisi lagti hai, jabki asal me yeh ek coordination mechanism hai — servers ko roots ki boundaries respect karna required nahi hai. Aur ab yeh deprecate bhi ho chuki hai: 2026-07-28 wale revision ne roots capability ko deprecate kar diya hai. Dikhaya gaya resolver form dono taraf wale clients ke saath kaam karta hai, lekin naye servers ko roots ke bajay paths ko tool arguments, resource URIs ya server configuration ke roop me lena chahiye. Agar pre-revision clients ko serve karna hai jo roots dete hain, to yahan seekha gaya tareeqa kaam aayega.

Roots kai wajah se useful hain. Sabse badi baat yeh hai ki woh ek unique URI dete hain, jisse servers un filesystem roots ko ek well-defined identifier se access kar sakte hain. Client side par yeh ek directory picker ho sakta hai, jo model aur connected servers ko batata hai ki kaunsi directories context ke roop me available hain. Roots fetch karna ek hi request hai — roots/list — jo resolver ke through ki jaati hai, bilkul elicitations aur sampling ki tarah. SDK har tool call par ek baar client se roots maangta hai aur result inject karta hai, to server ko pehle wale protocol versions ki tarah root cache maintain karne ki zaroorat nahi hai. Roots ka message flow dusri capabilities se simple hai, kyunki isme koi HITL review process nahi hoti. Client Root objects return karta hai, har ek me file scheme wali URI aur optional naam hota hai.

Ek example me count_files() tool user ke diye hue directory me files ginata hai, lekin sirf tab jab woh directory roots list me ho. Resolver request_roots() ListRoots() return karta hai, aur tool ka roots parameter ListRootsResult se annotate hota hai. Tool pehle requested path ko Path.resolve() se resolve karta hai — yeh .. segments ko normalize karta hai aur symlinks ko follow karta hai, to check true location par hota hai. Phir har root ke liye URI ko filesystem path me convert karta hai: Root.uri ek Pydantic FileURL hai, jiski .path attribute percent-encoded URL path hoti hai, operating system path nahi — isliye use url2pathname() se decode kiya jaata hai, jo Windows-style drive-letter paths bhi handle karta hai. Phir is_relative_to() poochta hai ki path asal me root ke andar hai ya nahi. Yeh string prefix check se behtar hai, kyunki use sibling directory fool nahi kar sakti jo sirf prefix share karti ho — jaise /home/user-evil ka /home/user se shuru hona. Agar path allowed nahi hai to error log karke ValueError raise kiya jaata hai; agar directory exist hi nahi karti to NotADirectoryError raise hota hai. Warning yaad rakhni chahiye: roots coordination mechanism hain, security boundary nahi. Local server user account ki permissions se chalne wala process hai, aur ek malicious ya buggy server un permissions se koi bhi file padh sakta hai, chahe client ne roots kuch bhi diye hon. Path check sirf server ka voluntarily achha behave karna hai. Asli boundaries server install karne ka decision aur host ki sandboxing hain. Aur ek practical limit: Python MCP SDK me servers ke liye client machine par remote files ya directories access karne ka koi tareeqa nahi hai, to file manipulation wale servers aam taur par sirf usi machine par kaam kar sakte hain jahan woh chal rahe hain.

ch6/08_low_level_pagination/server.py — https://github.com/kylestratis/ai_agents_mcp_examples/blob/main/ch6/08_low_level_pagination/server.py
import asyncio
import sys

import mcp.server.stdio
from mcp.server import NotificationOptions, Server, ServerRequestContext
from mcp.server.models import InitializationOptions
from mcp_types import (
    ListResourcesResult,
    PaginatedRequestParams,
    ReadResourceRequestParams,
    ReadResourceResult,
    Resource,
    TextResourceContents,
)

# Total number of resources
TOTAL_RESOURCES = 1000
PAGE_SIZE = 100
RESOURCES = []
for i in range(0, TOTAL_RESOURCES):
    RESOURCES.append(
        Resource(
            uri=f"resource://{i}",
            name=f"Resource {i}",
            description=f"This is resource number {i}",
            mime_type="text/plain",
        )
    )


async def list_resources(
    ctx: ServerRequestContext, params: PaginatedRequestParams | None
) -> ListResourcesResult:
    """List resources with pagination support.
    Returns 100 resources at a time from a fixed list of 1000 resources.
    """
    if params is not None:
        cursor = params.cursor
    else:
        cursor = None

    start_index = 0
    if cursor is not None:
        start_index = int(cursor)
    end_index = min(start_index + PAGE_SIZE, TOTAL_RESOURCES)

    resources = RESOURCES[start_index:end_index]

    next_cursor = None
    if end_index < TOTAL_RESOURCES:
        next_cursor = str(end_index)

    return ListResourcesResult(resources=resources, next_cursor=next_cursor)


async def read_resource(
    ctx: ServerRequestContext, params: ReadResourceRequestParams
) -> ReadResourceResult:
    """Read a single resource by its URI."""
    uri = params.uri
    if not uri.startswith("resource://"):
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid resource URI: {uri}")

    try:
        resource_num = int(uri.replace("resource://", ""))
    except ValueError:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid resource number in URI: {uri}")

    if resource_num < 0 or resource_num >= TOTAL_RESOURCES:
        raise ValueError(f"Resource not found: {uri}")

    return ReadResourceResult(
        contents=[
            TextResourceContents(
                uri=uri,
                mime_type="text/plain",
                text=RESOURCES[resource_num].description,
            )
        ]
    )


# Create a server instance, registering the handlers
server = Server(
    "low-level-pagination-server",
    version="0.1.0",
    on_list_resources=list_resources,
    on_read_resource=read_resource,
)


async def run() -> None:
    """Run the low-level pagination server."""
    print("Running pagination server with 1000 resources", file=sys.stderr)
    initialization_options = InitializationOptions(
        server_name="pagination-server",
        server_version="0.1.0",
        capabilities=server.get_capabilities(
            notification_options=NotificationOptions(),
            experimental_capabilities={},
        ),
    )

    async with mcp.server.stdio.stdio_server() as (read_stream, write_stream):
        await server.run(
            read_stream=read_stream,
            write_stream=write_stream,
            initialization_options=initialization_options,
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(run())
ch6/09_elicitations_server/server.py — https://github.com/kylestratis/ai_agents_mcp_examples/blob/main/ch6/09_elicitations_server/server.py
from typing import Annotated

from mcp.server.mcpserver import (
    AcceptedElicitation,
    CancelledElicitation,
    DeclinedElicitation,
    Elicit,
    ElicitationResult,
    MCPServer,
    Resolve,
)
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

# Initialize MCP server
mcp = MCPServer("elicitations-server")


class SignupInfo(BaseModel):
    """Form schema for the signup elicitation request."""

    name: str = Field(title="Full Name", description="Your full name", min_length=1)
    email: str = Field(title="Email Address", description="Your email address")
    age: int | None = Field(
        default=None,
        title="Age",
        description="Your age in years",
        ge=0,
        le=150,
    )


async def request_signup_info() -> Elicit[SignupInfo]:
    """Resolver: ask the user for their signup information."""
    return Elicit(
        "Please provide your information to sign up for daily math facts!",
        SignupInfo,
    )


@mcp.tool()
async def signup_math_facts(
    signup: Annotated[ElicitationResult[SignupInfo], Resolve(request_signup_info)],
) -> str:
    """Sign up to receive daily math facts (demonstration of elicitation)."""
    # Handle the different response actions
    match signup:
        case AcceptedElicitation(data=user_data):
            response = (
                f"Welcome {user_data.name}! You've successfully signed up "
                "for daily math facts.\n"
            )
            response += (
                f"We'll send interesting mathematical tidbits to "
                f"{user_data.email}.\n"
            )

            if user_data.age:
                response += (
                    f"Thanks for sharing that you're {user_data.age} years "
                    "old - we'll tailor the content accordingly!\n"
                )

            response += "\nYou'll receive your first math fact soon!"
            response += (
                "\n(Note: This is just a demonstration - "
                "no actual signup occurred!)"
            )

            return response

        case DeclinedElicitation():
            return (
                "No problem! You've chosen not to sign up for math facts. "
                "You can always use our calculation tools anytime!"
            )

        case CancelledElicitation():
            return (
                "Signup cancelled. Feel free to try again later or "
                "use our other mathematical tools!"
            )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    mcp.run()
ch6/10_sampling/server.py — https://github.com/kylestratis/ai_agents_mcp_examples/blob/main/ch6/10_sampling/server.py
from typing import Annotated

from mcp.server.mcpserver import MCPServer, Resolve, Sample
from mcp_types import (
    CreateMessageResult,
    ModelHint,
    ModelPreferences,
    SamplingMessage,
    TextContent,
)

# Initialize MCP server
mcp = MCPServer("sampling-server")

MODEL_PREFERENCES = ModelPreferences(
    hints=[
        ModelHint(name="claude-4-5-haiku"),
        ModelHint(name="claude-haiku"),
        ModelHint(name="gpt-4o-mini"),
    ],
    cost_priority=1.0,
    speed_priority=0.8,
    intelligence_priority=0.3,
)


def request_math_explanation(operation: str) -> Sample:
    """Resolver: sample the client's language model for an explanation."""
    prompt = f"""
    Explain how the following mathematical operation works. Break it down into
    discrete steps and explain any relevant concepts. The operation is:
    {operation}. Use the voice of a patient but eccentric math professor
    explaining to a curious but inexperienced student.
    """
    return Sample(
        [
            SamplingMessage(
                role="user",
                content=TextContent(type="text", text=prompt),
            )
        ],
        max_tokens=100,
        model_preferences=MODEL_PREFERENCES,
    )


@mcp.tool()
async def explain_math(
    operation: str,
    explanation: Annotated[CreateMessageResult, Resolve(request_math_explanation)],
) -> str:
    """Use sampling to explain how a mathematical operation works."""
    match explanation.content.type:
        case "text":
            return explanation.content.text
        case "image" | "audio":
            return str(explanation.content.data)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    mcp.run()
ch6/11_roots/server.py — https://github.com/kylestratis/ai_agents_mcp_examples/blob/main/ch6/11_roots/server.py
import os
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Annotated
from urllib.request import url2pathname

from mcp.server.mcpserver import Context, ListRoots, MCPServer, Resolve
from mcp_types import ListRootsResult

mcp = MCPServer("roots-server")


def request_roots() -> ListRoots:
    """Resolver: fetch the client's current roots list."""
    return ListRoots()


@mcp.tool()
async def count_files(
    file_path: str,
    roots: Annotated[ListRootsResult, Resolve(request_roots)],
    ctx: Context,
) -> str:
    """Count files in a given directory."""
    requested_path = Path(file_path).resolve()
    is_allowed = False

    for root in roots.roots:
        root_path = Path(url2pathname(root.uri.path)).resolve()
        if requested_path.is_relative_to(root_path):
            is_allowed = True
            break

    if not is_allowed:
        error_msg = f"Access denied: {file_path} is not within allowed roots"
        await ctx.error(error_msg)
        raise ValueError(error_msg)

    # Validate directory exists
    if not requested_path.is_dir():
        error_msg = f"Path {file_path} is not a valid directory"
        await ctx.error(error_msg)
        raise NotADirectoryError(error_msg)

    count = len(os.listdir(requested_path))
    await ctx.info(f"Counting files in {file_path} = {count}")
    return f"There are {count} files in {file_path}"


if __name__ == "__main__":
    mcp.run()
SOURCESource: AI Agents with MCP, O'Reilly, Chapter 6 — Building MCP Servers: Advanced Use with Utilities and Integrating Client Capabilities
← Previous06.1 · Progress notifications→ Next06.3 · Request cancellation aur logging
06.3Chapter 6 · Building MCP Servers: Advanced Use with Utilities and Integrating Client Capabilities

Request cancellation aur logging

Lambe tool calls kabhi-kabhi bahut zyada waqt le lete hain, aur user unhe beech me rokna chahta hai. Request cancellation se user aisa kar sakta hai — aur server ko isse gracefully handle karna aana chahiye.

Cancellation kaise pahunchti hai

Request cancellation se user lambe operations, jaise dheere chalne wale tool calls, ko cancel kar sakta hai. Cancellation server tak kaise pahunche, yeh phir se 2026-07-28 wale specification revision ke kis taraf ho, is par depend karta hai. Pre-revision connections me cancellation ek notification hoti hai — notifications/cancelled — jo client us request ki ID ke saath bhejta hai jise cancel karna hai. Post-revision, yeh ekmatra surviving client-to-server notification hai. Matlab har dusri client-provided capability ka flow badal gaya, lekin cancellation notification dono versions me ek jaisi dikhti hai.

Notification ek jaisi dikhti hai, lekin SDK use handle alag tareeqe se karta hai, transport ke hisaab se. stdio me client ko server ko cancel notification bhejni padti hai, aur server execution rok deta hai. Streamable HTTP me har request ka apna ephemeral per-request POST stream hota hai, jo khud request signal ka kaam karta hai. Client ko bas stream band karni hoti hai, aur server (SDK ke through) use apne end par task cancel karne ka signal maan leta hai. Modern HTTP clients disconnect karke cancel karte hain, notification bhejkar nahi.

Robust server ko kya karna chahiye

Ek robust server banane ke liye har request ke liye cancellation notifications ko gracefully handle karna chahiye: invalid notifications ko ignore karna (unknown request ID, ya pehle se complete ho chuki request), jo receive hua use log karna taaki user ke pain points samajh aayein, chal raha operation rokna, aur held resources ko free karna. Python SDK me cancellation receive karna client aur server dono ke liye automatic hai. Dispatcher in-flight requests ko ID se track karta hai, aur jab cancellation aati hai to matching handler ko beech execution me cancel kar deta hai, aur cancellation request ke jawab me ek error response message bhejta hai.

Lekin automatic handling yeh nahi batati ki cancellation hui hai. Iske liye ek notification handler chahiye. notifications/cancelled ke liye ek handler register karo, aur SDK use notification ke parameters ke saath call karta hai, jabki actual cancellation khud handle karta hai. Is notification ke parameters hain request ID aur optional reason. Handler wahi jagah hai jahan notification ko log karna hai aur zaroori cleanup karna hai.

Yeh handler tab fire hota hai jab cancellation notification aati hai: kisi bhi spec version par koi bhi stdio client, ya pre-revision connection par Streamable HTTP client. Modern HTTP clients disconnect karke cancel karte hain, aur SDK bina kisi observable notification ke seedha running task handler (aam taur par ek tool handler) ko cancel kar deta hai. Cancellation ko pakadne ka universal mechanism tool ke andar hi hai: cancellation hamesha tool me ek exception ke roop me aati hai, taaki cleanup try/finally me shuru ho sake. Khaas taur par cancellation exception ko pakda bhi ja sakta hai: anyio.get_cancelled_exc_class() se, aur phir use re-raise karna chahiye. Notification handler ki ekmatra extra value yeh hai ki usse request ID aur client ka reason milta hai.

async def handle_cancelled_notification(
    ctx: ServerRequestContext,
    params: CancelledNotificationParams,
) -> None:
    logger.info(
        f"Cancelled notification received for request ID "
        f"{params.request_id}: {params.reason}"
    )

# register karna:
mcp._lowlevel_server.add_notification_handler(
    "notifications/cancelled",
    CancelledNotificationParams,
    handle_cancelled_notification,
)

Ek example me handle_cancelled_notification() request ID aur client ke reason ko log karta hai. Important baat: yeh kuch cancel nahi karta, kyunki SDK woh kaam khud karta hai. Notification handlers do arguments lete hain: request context aur notification ke typed parameters. Yeh low-level server se register hota hai aur notifications/cancelled message se joda jaata hai. slow_operation() tool ek fancy sleep hai jo apni progress report karta hai. Poora loop ek try block me hai jo anyio.get_cancelled_exc_class() ko catch karta hai — yahi woh exception hai jo task cancel hone par raise hoti hai, chahe cancellation ka tareeqa kuch bhi ho. Except block sirf cancellation ko log karta hai aur exception ko re-raise karta hai. Yeh tab bhi trigger hoga jab job cancel ho, chahe transport koi bhi ho aur protocol version koi bhi ho.

Cancellation notifications ki limits

Cancellation notifications race conditions se affect ho sakti hain, kyunki ho sakta hai ki notification receiver tak pahunche usse pehle hi operation complete ho jaaye aur result ya error response bhej diya gaya ho. Iske liye protocol me koi khaas guards nahi hain, to dono taraf ke developers ko in situations ko bina protocol ki madad ke handle karna padta hai. Practice me requestor ko us result ko ignore karne ke liye taiyaar rehna chahiye jo us request ke liye aaye jise woh pehle hi cancel kar chuka hai, aur cancellation notification ke receiver ko just-complete hui request ki cancellation ko error nahi maan na chahiye. Pre-2026-07-28 connections me client aur server ke beech initialization request ko cancel karne ki koshish kabhi nahi karni chahiye, kyunki isse session failure ho sakta hai aur potentially irrecoverable state ban sakti hai. Aur receivers ko completed requests ko cancel karne ki koshish nahi karni chahiye, lekin agar matching request abhi bhi in progress hai to use rokna chahiye aur resources free karne chahiye. Kyunki yeh sirf notifications hain, receivers ko cancellation notification milne par requestor ko koi response nahi bhejna chahiye.

Logging ka dobara note

Is chapter me logging ko utilities ke saath cover kiya gaya tha, aur cancellation ke context me bhi logging kaam aati hai — notification handler ka main kaam hi logging hai. Lekin yeh dohraana zaroori hai ki protocol-level logging 2026-07-28 version me deprecate ho gayi hai. Naye servers ko logs ke liye Python ke logging module ka istemal karna chahiye, jisme MCPServer constructor ka log_level stderr handler ko configure karta hai. Cancellation handler me bhi standard logging module use hota hai, jaise example me logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) se dikhaya gaya hai. Isse logs server ke stderr par jaate hain, jahan host ya operator unhe dekh sakta hai, bina client par depend kiye.

ch6/12_cancel_request_notification/server.py — https://github.com/kylestratis/ai_agents_mcp_examples/blob/main/ch6/12_cancel_request_notification/server.py
import logging

import anyio
from mcp.server import ServerRequestContext
from mcp.server.mcpserver import Context, MCPServer
from mcp_types import CancelledNotificationParams

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
mcp = MCPServer("cancel-request-notification-server")


async def handle_cancelled_notification(
    ctx: ServerRequestContext,
    params: CancelledNotificationParams,
) -> None:
    """Handle cancellation notifications from the client."""
    logger.info(
        (
            f"Cancelled notification received for request ID "
            f"{params.request_id}: {params.reason}"
        )
    )


@mcp.tool()
async def slow_operation(ctx: Context, length: int = 100) -> str:
    """A long-running tool the user may want to cancel.
    Args:
        length: The length of the operation in steps.
    """
    try:
        for i in range(1, length + 1):
            await anyio.sleep(0.1)
            await ctx.report_progress(progress=i, total=length)
    except anyio.get_cancelled_exc_class():
        logger.info("slow_operation cancelled mid-run, cleaning up")
        raise
    return f"Completed all {length} steps"


if __name__ == "__main__":
    mcp._lowlevel_server.add_notification_handler(
        "notifications/cancelled",
        CancelledNotificationParams,
        handle_cancelled_notification,
    )
    mcp.run()

← Previous06.2 · Client capabilities use karna — sampling, elicitation, roots→ Next07 · Server test karna — Inspector aur evaluations
07Chapter 7 · Testing, Securing, and Sharing Your MCP Server

Server test karna — Inspector aur evaluations

Server ban gaya, tools, prompts aur resources de raha hai, client capabilities bhi support karta hai. Lekin kaam abhi khatam nahi hua — jaise kisi bhi software project me, server ko test karna, evaluate karna, secure karna aur phir duniya ke saath share karna baki hai.

Kitna test karna hai

Testing ki zaroorat situation par depend karti hai. Agar server ek fun side project ke liye hai, to shayad 100% unit test coverage ya automated end-to-end tests ki zaroorat nahi hai. Lekin agar server bade enterprises ke liye hai, jinme strict compliance standards hain, ya sensitive data ya critical operations handle karta hai, to over-testing ki taraf jhukna chahiye. In do extremes ke beech ek bada spectrum hai — sirf sabse critical ya complex paths test karna, simple prompt functions ko ignore karna, ya har failure case test karne ke bajay happy path par focus karna. Kya test karna hai, yeh risk tolerance par depend karta hai, isliye sochna chahiye ki server kaise use hoga, kaun use karega, aur kis type ka data handle karega.

MCP Inspector se debugging

Development ke dauran MCP Inspector sabse zyada use hone wala tool ho sakta hai. Yeh ek nearly fully featured MCP client hai, jisse server ke functions ko manually trigger karke results inspect kiye ja sakte hain — tool calls, resources, prompts, notifications, logging aur bahut kuch. Inspector ke main view me upar primitives aur utilities ke panels hote hain, aur collapsible right panel me client aur server ke beech message history dikhti hai, jo print debugging ke liye handy hai. Inspector me naya change test karna aasan hai: Servers panel me connection switch dabao, aur server ka latest version load ho jaata hai.

Inspector ka development aur testing workflow chaar steps me bataya gaya hai. Pehla: server ka code skeleton aur connection logic banao, phir Inspector ko locally connect karo. Connectivity aur primitive listing functions test karo, taaki functions sahi se listed hon. Dusra: functions likhna shuru karo. Ek function complete hone ke baad Inspector me connection refresh karo, use list karke chalao (happy path), aur repeat karo. Logic ko debug ya trace karne ke liye logging ya stderr par print ka istemal karo. Teesra: happy paths cover karne ke baad potential interactions (jaise elicitation wala tool call), edge cases, failure cases, notifications, logs aur baaki sab test karo. Chautha: agar goal remote server hai to deploy karo, dekho kya remote transport se local test ho sakta hai, aur connectivity, latency waghera test karo.

Har functionality ke liye Inspector me alag view hai. Sampling view Tools view ke saath kaam karta hai: tool call karo, phir Sampling menu item par notification badge dikhega, wahan jao to sampling request object dikhega jo client ko bheja jaata. Use approve ya reject kar sakte ho — yeh asal me kisi LLM ko call nahi karta, lekin approval aur rejection ke code paths aur unse aane wale notifications test ho jaate hain. Final results wapas Tools view me dikhte hain. Elicitations view bhi waise hi kaam karta hai: tool call ke baad left pane me request aur schema, right pane me generated form dikhta hai. Wahan form ke fields sahi hain ya nahi, JSON object aur entered values, unexpected ya disallowed values, aur submit/decline/cancel flows test kiye ja sakte hain. Elicitations sampling se zyada useful hain yahan, kyunki inme stubbed-out model call nahi hota, to tool call aur elicitation ka poora flow dikhta hai.

Roots view me Inspector client me roots add karke phir tool ya resource function chalaya jaata hai, aur results ya logging se pata chalta hai ki roots respect hue ya nahi aur sahi code paths chale ya nahi. Auth pane me guided OAuth flow ya Quick OAuth Flow button se standard automatic OAuth flow test kiya ja sakta hai, aur neeche OAuth Flow Progress panel me har step ka result aur errors dikhte hain. History aur Server Notifications panes bhi use karne chahiye — History me saare MCP function calls unke request aur response objects ke saath dikhte hain, aur Server Notifications pane me server se bheji gayi saari notifications dikhti hain. Ek tip: Inspector me dikh raha JSON object kabhi-kabhi truncated hota hai, khaas taur par lambe strings — ellipsis (...) se indicate hota hai, aur truncated string values me ellipsis double quotes ke andar dikhta hai, jaise woh string ka hissa ho. Ellipsis wali jagah par click karne se poori field value dikhti hai.

Claude Desktop se integration testing bhi ki ja sakti hai. Yeh ek likely candidate hai jo users ka client hoga, aur yeh general-purpose chat application hai jisme system prompt me minimal alterations hote hain — isliye server ka behavior ek real application ke saath, lekin beech me zyada kuch nahi, test ho jaata hai. Claude Desktop apne chat sessions ke detailed metadata logs bhi likhta hai, jinme server connections, message passing, runtime errors aur bahut kuch hota hai.

Automated testing — unit aur integration

Manual testing ke alawa automated testing bhi zaroori hai. Unit testing MCP servers ki aam code ki unit testing jaisi hi hai: wahi tools (jaise pytest), wahi techniques (jaise outside dependencies ko mock karna aur test fixtures banana), wahi metrics (jaise test coverage), aur happy path ke saath failure cases bhi cover karna. Mocking yahan important hai, kyunki servers bahut saari external dependencies par depend karte hain — databases aur APIs ke alawa connected clients ko bheje gaye requests bhi.

Integration testing bhi important hai, kyunki servers clients ke saath interact kiye bina zyada kuch nahi karte. Automated integration tests me clients se connect aur disconnect karna, external APIs ko real calls se test karna, database queries wale functions ko test tables se test karna, resource aur prompt functions ke liye test files load karna — sab expected inputs aur outputs ke saath — shamil hai. Ek simple MCP client likhkar bhi widely scoped automated tests likhe ja sakte hain, jo server ko requests bhejkar results verify karta hai aur poori server functionality ko test ke under laata hai. Lekin aam taur par pehle Inspector wala workflow implement karna behtar hai, aur basic functionality verify hone ke baad hi automated test suites likhni chahiye.

Evaluations — prompts aur tools ko model ke saath test karna

Evaluations generative AI ki duniya me end-to-end test ka sabse important type hain. Traditional machine learning me training data ka ek hissa rok kar model ki performance accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score jaise metrics se assess ki jaati thi. Generative AI me hum kai versions ke LLM ko train karke compare nahi karte, lekin evaluations phir bhi important hain — inse hum apne prompts (jinme tool names aur descriptions bhi aate hain) ko iterate karke sudhaar sakte hain, kai models ke against accuracy, correctness, output formats, tool choice accuracy, cost aur bahut kuch test karke.

MCP server developer ke liye evaluations ki utility limited hai, kyunki agent applications server ko kaise use karenge, is par server developer ka control kam hai. Phir bhi teen areas evaluations ke layak hain: prompts, tool use, aur sampling (legacy servers ke liye jo abhi bhi use support karte hain). Prompts evaluate karte waqt response accuracy, kai models me accuracy, aur cost sabse important dimensions hain. Accuracy check karne ka sabse simple tareeqa yeh hai ki response me ek specific string hai ya nahi — lekin isme false positives aur false negatives ka risk hai: string galat voice ya galat response me bhi ho sakti hai, ya sahi response me string na bhi ho. Isse behtar tareeqa hai response ke liye ek rubric banana aur ek aur LLM se use rubric ke against grade karwana — LLM-as-a-judge. Yeh zyada complex aur potentially costly hai, lekin sahi se karne par powerful hai. Dono techniques me evaluation tools se tests kai models ke against chalaye ja sakte hain, taaki performance aur cost dekha ja sake. Server developer ke liye yeh important hai ki prompts kai models me performant hon aur reasonable cost par hon, kyunki users ka model woh choose nahi kar sakta.

Evaluation checklist me yeh essentials hain: tool-choice performance, tool-use cost, guardrail adherence (prompts ke liye), prompt cost, prompt correctness, structured output adherence, specific tasks aur prompts ke liye LLM-as-a-judge, aur alag-alag model sizes aur families me testing. Tools ko end-to-end test karte waqt kam se kam yeh check karna chahiye ki expected value response me hai aur tool call se expected structures, jaise valid tool-call response object, return hote hain. Kuch evaluation tools, jaise Promptfoo, me built-in tests hote hain jo ensure karte hain ki valid tool calls ho rahe hain. Sampling prompts ko bhi waise hi evaluate kiya ja sakta hai jaise MCP server prompts ko.

Practice me prompts evaluate karne ka process aath steps ka hai: prompts ko evaluation tool me load karo; har prompt ko ek common model ke against kuch baar chalakar response aur cost ka sense lo; agar response me glaring issues hon to prompt tweak karke dobara chalao; comfortable hone par simple automated tests likho, jaise response me koi string hona ya structure maintain karna; in simple tests se prompts ko alag-alag models ke against chalao, har model ko multiple calls ke saath; results ke basis par prompts refine karo; agar chaho to rubrics ya custom metrics define karke LLM-as-a-judge se grade karwao; aur results stabilize hone tak repeat karo. Is process me jahan prompts fail hote hain, use explore karke refine karna error analysis kehlata hai.

Tools evaluate karna thoda mushkil hai, kyunki server developer ke paas aam taur par usage telemetry ya logging (traces) nahi hoti, jinse users ke problematic prompts mil sakein. Isliye khud aise queries banane padte hain jo users ke tool use ke tareeqe se match karein — users hamesha surprise karenge, lekin phir bhi reasonable set banaya ja sakta hai. Phir expected results chahiye hote hain judge karne ke liye. Ek simple tareeqa hai script likhna jo LLM API ko seedha agentic loops ke andar call kare, har model call ko tools call karne ka mauka de, aur phir final response object check kare ki usme expected output hai, sahi tool call hua, aur tool-call request object expected structure se match karta hai. Agar API cost ya token consumption metrics deti hai to unhe bhi report kiya ja sakta hai. Is approach ka downside yeh hai ki test conditions khud likhne aur debug karne padte hain. Ek example script prompt-tool pairs par loop karti hai, har prompt ke saath model ko call karti hai, aur check karti hai ki model ne sahi tool call kiya ya nahi — tool-call accuracy score sahi tool calls ko total prompts se divide karke nikala jaata hai. Check stop_reason par depend karta hai: tool_use stop batata hai ki model ne tool call ki koshish ki, aur success tabhi count hoti hai jab exactly ek tool-use block wapas aaye aur uska naam expected tool se match kare. Lekin perfect score bhi practice ke baare me zyada nahi batata, kyunki script user ka asal environment ya interactions replicate nahi kar sakti.

Aur zyada end-to-end test ke liye ek simple MCP client likhkar use evaluation loops ke saath use kiya ja sakta hai — lekin yeh zyada complex hai aur additional failure points add karke failure analysis mushkil bana deta hai. Kuch evaluation tools me built-in MCP integrations hoti hain, jinse server se seedha connect karke test kiya ja sakta hai. MCP-focused evaluation frameworks, jaise mcp-eval (Python) aur mcp-evals (Node), MCP server evaluations likhne, chalane aur CI/CD pipeline me integrate karne me madad karte hain.

ch7/01_simple_evaluation/server.py — https://github.com/kylestratis/ai_agents_mcp_examples/blob/main/ch7/01_simple_evaluation/server.py
"""
Provides mathematical operations as tools for calculation tasks.
"""

from mcp.server.mcpserver import MCPServer

# Initialize MCP server
mcp = MCPServer("calculator")


@mcp.tool()
async def add(a: float, b: float) -> str:
    """Add two numbers together.

    Args:
        a: First number
        b: Second number
    """
    result = a + b
    return f"{result}"


@mcp.tool()
async def subtract(a: float, b: float) -> str:
    """Subtract the second number from the first.

    Args:
        a: Number to subtract from
        b: Number to subtract
    """
    result = a - b
    return f"{a} - {b} = {result}"


@mcp.tool()
async def multiply(a: float, b: float) -> str:
    """Multiply two numbers together.

    Args:
        a: First number
        b: Second number
    """
    result = a * b
    return f"{result}"


@mcp.tool()
async def divide(
    a: float,
    b: float,
) -> str:
    """Divide the first number by the second.

    Args:
        a: Dividend (number to be divided)
        b: Divisor (number to divide by)
    """
    if b == 0:
        return "Error: Division by zero is not allowed"

    result = a / b
    return f"{result}"
ch7/01_simple_evaluation/test.py — https://github.com/kylestratis/ai_agents_mcp_examples/blob/main/ch7/01_simple_evaluation/test.py
""" """

import os

from anthropic import Anthropic
from dotenv import load_dotenv
from server import add, divide, multiply, subtract

load_dotenv()

ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = os.environ["ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"]


def _create_tool_dictionary(tool_func):
    return {
        "name": tool_func.__name__,
        "description": tool_func.__doc__,
        "input_schema": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "a": {"type": "number"},
                "b": {"type": "number"},
            },
            "required": ["a", "b"],
        },
    }


TOOLS = [
    _create_tool_dictionary(add),
    _create_tool_dictionary(subtract),
    _create_tool_dictionary(multiply),
    _create_tool_dictionary(divide),
]

TEST_PROMPT_TOOL_CHOICE_PAIRS = [
    ("What is 2 + 2?", "add"),
    ("What is 2 - 2?", "subtract"),
    ("What is 2 * 2?", "multiply"),
    ("What is 2 / 2?", "divide"),
]


def main():
    api_key = os.environ.get("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY")
    if not api_key:
        raise ValueError(
            "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable not set. "
            "Please create a .env file with your API key."
        )

    client = Anthropic(api_key=api_key)

    tool_choice_score = 0
    for prompt, expected_tool_choice in TEST_PROMPT_TOOL_CHOICE_PAIRS:
        conversation_messages = [
            {"role": "user", "content": prompt},
        ]
        # Call Claude API with available tools
        response = client.messages.create(
            model="claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929",
            max_tokens=4096,
            messages=conversation_messages,
            tools=TOOLS,
            tool_choice={"type": "auto"},  # Let Claude decide when to use tools
        )

        # Check if Claude wants to use tools
        if response.stop_reason == "tool_use":
            # Extract all tool use blocks from the response
            tool_use_blocks = [
                block for block in response.content if block.type == "tool_use"
            ]

            if (
                len(tool_use_blocks) == 1
                and tool_use_blocks[0].name == expected_tool_choice
            ):
                tool_choice_score += 1

    print(f"Tool choice score: {tool_choice_score}")
    print(
        f"Tool choice accuracy: {tool_choice_score / len(TEST_PROMPT_TOOL_CHOICE_PAIRS) * 100}%"
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

07.1Chapter 7 · Testing, Securing, and Sharing Your MCP Server

Server secure rakhna — threats aur frameworks

LLMs ka natural language interface attack surface ko lagbhag infinite broad bana deta hai. Server ko secure rakhne ke liye common attacks ko samajhna, unke mitigations jaanna, aur architectural approaches lagana zaroori hai.

Injection vulnerabilities

Injection vulnerabilities me SQL injection, command injection aur prompt injection aate hain. SQL injection me user database query me arbitrary SQL commands inject karta hai, jisse data exfiltration, sensitive data ka exposure, data corruption aur total system compromise bhi ho sakta hai. Yeh decades purani vulnerability hai — web applications me unsecured forms se shuru hui, jahan user ka input string interpolation se SQL query me daala jaata tha, aur malicious actor ek quote se string se bahar nikal kar koi bhi SQL command daal sakta tha. Command injection me user input se arbitrary CLI commands execute ho jaate hain, jinse aise hi outcomes ho sakte hain. Dono MCP servers ke liye relevant hain, khaas taur par agar server database access karta hai ya CLI commands execute karta hai. Pehli defense saare user input ko sanitize karna hai. Achhi baat yeh hai ki jab tools call hote hain to unke parameters aam function call ki tarah bhare jaate hain, to LLMs ke near-infinite attack surface ki chinta yahan nahi hoti.

Prompt injection LLMs aur agentic applications ke liye ek common attack vector hai. Isme user model ke system prompt me arbitrary text inject karta hai, jisse remote code execution, data exfiltration aur bahut kuch ho sakta hai. MCP servers ke liye yeh significant risk hai, kyunki tool call ke dono ends — ek taraf tool ka naam, description aur parameters, dusri taraf tool results — calling model ke context me load hote hain aur model unhe prompt ki tarah use kar sakta hai. Jab bhi server use karne wala application untrusted input access karta hai — web pages, emails, files ya aur data — server prompt injection attacks ka vector ban sakta hai. Ek web page me malicious instructions chhupi ho sakti hain, jo additional tool calls karwa sakti hain, jaise file-read tool se sensitive file padhna aur output attacker ko bhej dena, bina user ko bataye.

Server developer ke roop me in attacks ko sirf partially mitigate kiya ja sakta hai, kyunki prompt kuch bhi ho sakta hai. Isliye sochna chahiye ki tumhare tools kis prompt injection consequences ke liye vulnerable ho sakte hain — restricted file access, privilege escalation waghera — aur unhe kaise mitigate karna hai. Structural mitigations jaise server ko container me chalakar host system se isolate karna, ya code-level mitigations jaise input sanitization ya sensitive directories ki denylist — dono ka combination behtar hai. Agar server ke tools web pages access karte hain to URLs aur loaded content ko hamesha validate aur sanitize karna chahiye — specific HTML tags ko target karna, encoded ya obfuscated content detect karna, aur bahut kuch. Defenses me parametrized SQL queries (string interpolation ke bajay), allowlist shell commands ya prompts, shell commands execute karne wale environment ko sandbox karna, file permissions lock karna, aur database me tools ke liye severely restricted table aur command permissions set karna shamil hain.

Injection attacks ka ek close relative hai path traversal attack, jiske liye MCP servers khaas taur par vulnerable hain. Koi bhi tool ya resource jo filepath parameter leta hai, use ../../etc/passwd jaisi value di ja sakti hai, jo intended directory se bahar nikal jaati hai. Kyunki tool arguments ek model bharta hai jo untrusted content padhta hai, prompt injection hi traversal string provide kar sakta hai. Naive defenses aasani se fail ho jaati hain: .. check karna percent-encoded %2e%2e%2f ko miss kar dega, aur string prefix comparison /home/user-evil ko jaane dega kyunki woh /home/user se match karta hai. Robust pattern Chapter 6 ke example se aaya hai: pehle requested path ko resolve karo — Path.resolve() .. segments ko normalize karta hai aur symlinks ko follow karta hai — phir is_relative_to() se check karo ki file asal me allowed base directory ke andar hai ya nahi. Resource templates ko Python SDK se similar check automatically milta hai: template parameters jinme .. path components, null bytes ya absolute-looking paths hon, woh read by default fail ho jaata hai. Tool parameters ko yeh automatic protection nahi milti, isliye containment check tool code me hona chahiye.

Access control, DoS aur token pass-through

Remote MCP server aam taur par ek multitenant system hota hai, isliye access control zaroori hai: user A user B ke objects access na kar sake, aur vice versa. Function ya tool level par bhi access control chahiye ho sakta hai, khaas taur par agar server segregated tool access deta hai, jaise paid tier ya admin-scoped tools. Iska zyada hissa declarative policies, role permissions aur access gateways se handle ho sakta hai.

Denial-of-service aur distributed-denial-of-service (DoS/DDoS) attacks me malicious actor bahut saare requests bhejkar server ke resources ko overwhelm kar deta hai, jisse server unresponsive ho jaata hai ya crash kar jaata hai. Rate limiting, request throttling aur aisi techniques se inhe roka ja sakta hai.

Token pass-through ek attack vector hai, khud ek attack nahi. Isme MCP server MCP clients se authorization tokens lekar third-party services ko pass kar deta hai, bina token validate kiye. MCP authorization specification me tokens pass karna expressly forbidden hai jo server ke authorization server ne issue nahi kiye, lekin isse rokne ka koi technical mechanism nahi hai. Problem yeh hai ki authorization tokens ek specific service aur user ke liye generate hote hain, aur unhe pass karne se auditing aur monitoring mushkil ho jaati hai — tokens MCP client ya uske user se aate hue dikhenge, us MCP server se nahi jo asal me third-party service ko requests kar raha hai. Aur agar server tokens ko bina validation ke pass karta hai to attackers tokens chura kar sensitive data access kar sakte hain ya woh actions kar sakte hain jinke liye tokens intended nahi the. Mitigation simple hai: tokens ko server se third-party services ko pass mat karo. Ideal yeh hai ki server ke paas apne tokens hon jinse woh third-party services access kare. Agar client-provided authorization tokens use karne hi padte hain to kam se kam token aur uske scope ko validate karo.

Confused deputy problem

Confused deputy problem MCP aur LLMs se pehle ka hai, lekin aaj bhi relevant hai. Is attack me kam privileges wala system zyada privileges wale system ko trick karke apne liye actions karwata hai, zyada privileged system ki privileges use karke. MCP servers ke context me yeh tab hota hai jab server third-party service ke liye proxy ka kaam karta hai, uske paas apna OAuth static client ID hota hai, aur clients ko apne client IDs dynamically register karne deta hai, jo server third-party service ke saath use kare. Attack ke liye yeh bhi chahiye ki third-party service ki authorization flow server developer ke liye ek consent cookie aur key set kare, jise server client ke hisaab se user consent boundaries segregate nahi karta. Attacker phir user ko malicious link bhejkar original consent cookie hijack kar sakta hai, user consent skip karke, aur malicious redirect URI se server ka authorization code le sakta hai. Isse attacker ko server ke auth tokens mil jaate hain, aur third-party service tak pahunch mil jaati hai, bina apni authorization ya required user consent ke.

Iske mitigations kuch changes se hote hain. Pehla: single static client ID hata kar per-user client IDs use karo, har user ke liye consent flow trigger karo, consent decisions ko securely store karo, aur server ko user boundaries enforce karne do. Approve hone ke baad (ya lookup se pata chalne par ki consent pehle se di gayi hai), server third-party service ke liye static client ID use kar sakta hai. Iska matlab hai ki server ko user ko ek consent UI dikhana hoga, jisme requesting client ka naam, requested API scope ya scopes, aur redirect URI dikhe jahan tokens bheje jayenge. Is page me CSRF aur clickjacking attacks ke against proper protections bhi honi chahiye. Authorization requests me redirect URIs ko allowed redirect URIs ki registry ke against validate karna hoga, taaki malicious redirect URIs authorization flow ko hijack na kar sakein. Aur agar server OAuth use kar raha hai to state parameter ki value generate karke securely store karni hogi, MCP server consent ke baad lekin third-party service par redirect karne se pehle. Phir ensure karna hoga ki parameter bilkul wahi value hai jo store ki gayi thi, aur validation ke baad use delete kar dena hoga. Yeh complex lagta hai, lekin yeh largely OAuth ko sahi se implement karne ka standard hissa hai.

Layer 1 — Infrastructure foundations aur sandboxing

Architectural approaches me pehli layer infrastructure ki foundation hai. Sandboxing ka matlab hai application ko host system aur dusri applications se isolate karna, taaki woh host system ke resources ko access ya modify na kar sake. Yeh local aur remote dono MCP servers ke liye critical hai, halanki remote servers deploy hote hi dedicated server par hone se by default sandboxed hote hain. Local servers aise nahi hote. Local server ko Docker jaise container systems ya VirtualBox jaise full virtual machines se sandbox kiya ja sakta hai. Users khud server ko container ya VM me set up kar sakte hain, lekin developer unhe Dockerfile aur instructions de sakta hai. Ek minimal Dockerfile Astral ke uv base image se Python 3.14 environment leta hai, project ko /app me copy karta hai, uv sync --locked se dependencies install karta hai, aur CMD ["uv", "run", "python", "server.py"] se server chalata hai. Use karne ke liye docker build -t my-mcp-server . aur docker run -i my-mcp-server chalana hota hai.

Environment variables Dockerfile me ENV command se ya container chalate waqt -e flag se set ki ja sakti hain. Zyada common yeh hai ki user unhe apne client code ke StdioServerParameters object me set kare. Containerized server se connect karne ke liye client docker command chalata hai, args=["run", "-i", "-e", "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", "my-mcp-server"] aur env={"ANTHROPIC_API_KEY": "my-api-key"} ke saath — matlab environment variable client process me set hoti hai, aur phir -e se container ko pass hoti hai. Streamable HTTP transport se bhi local containerized server se connect kiya ja sakta hai: container ko docker run -p 8000:8000 my-mcp-server se chalao aur streamable_http_client("http://localhost:8000/mcp") se connect karo. Docker ek MCP Toolkit bhi deta hai, jo kisi bhi MCP server ko containerize karke gateway ke andar chala sakta hai, jise clients access kar sakte hain, aur Docker ke paas vetted server images ka MCP server catalog bhi hai.

Layer 2 — Access control: OAuth, RBAC aur gateways

Dusri layer access control hai, jiske core me principle of least privilege hai: kisi bhi user ya system ke paas sirf utna access hona chahiye jitna uske authorized tasks ke liye zaroori hai. Yeh fundamental security principle hai, jo malware, malicious users aur dusre threats se compromise ke venues ko kam karta hai. Remote MCP servers ke liye yeh layer khaas taur par important hai.

Users ko access dene ke liye OAuth 2.1 implement karna hota hai — wahi authorization flow jo client ne Chapter 4 me perform kiya tha, ab dusri taraf se. OAuth me resource servers (RS) aur authorization servers (AS) hote hain. Zyada tar MCP servers RS honge: unke paas kuch protected hai, jaise database ya API, jo authorized user ke liye hai. User authorized tab hota hai jab uske paas valid access token ho, jo ek alag AS deta hai jo user ko authenticate karta hai. Server ka kaam un tokens ko check karna hai, aur MCP Python SDK me iske liye ek class banani hoti hai jo TokenVerifier protocol fulfill kare — isme verify_token method implement karni hoti hai, jo token verify karke validated AccessToken object return kare ya invalid hone par None return kare. Server instantiate karte waqt token verifier ke saath AuthSettings object bhi dena hota hai, jisme authorization flow ki configuration hoti hai — issuer_url, resource_server_url aur required_scopes jaise values AS provider ki documentation se milti hain. Ek example me MyTokenVerifier class aur AuthSettings object MCPServer constructor me pass kiye jaate hain, aur server transport="streamable-http" se chalaya jaata hai. Verification khud likhi ja sakti hai ya kisi library se ki ja sakti hai. Iske baad SDK baaki sab handle karta hai.

Data access ki user boundaries ke alawa, role ke basis par actions ko bhi confine kiya ja sakta hai — role-based access control (RBAC). RBAC me policies user ki individual identity ke bajay organization ya system me uske role par based hoti hain. Iske liye users ke possible roles aur woh actions model karne hote hain jo unhe perform karne chahiye, least privilege ko dhyaan me rakhkar. Yeh AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) aur Kubernetes me milta hai, aur daily life me bhi — doctor ke office me receptionist ko patient ki contact information aur appointments dikhti hain, lekin medical records nahi; nurse apne patients ke records dekh aur update kar sakti hai, lekin dusron ke nahi; doctors saare records dekh aur update kar sakte hain. MCP servers par ise MCP gateway se apply kiya ja sakta hai — ek network-level construct jo deployed MCP servers aur unhe access karne wale clients ke beech hota hai, aur access control policies enforce karne ke liye perfect jagah hai. Kuch gateways traffic manage kar sakte hain, authentication aur authorization handle kar sakte hain, requests ko appropriate servers par route kar sakte hain, aur administrators ko control plane de sakte hain jinse gateway proxy kar raha ho, un servers ko manage karne ke liye. Examples me Microsoft MCP Gateway, Docker MCP Gateway aur Arcade aate hain. Gateways bade deployments ke liye great hain, jahan multiple servers ya server clusters hain.

Layer 3 — Operational controls

Teesri layer operational controls hai: observability, supply-chain management aur HITL monitoring. Observability ka matlab hai servers aur resources par kya ho raha hai, use dekhna — real time me ya turant baad logs se. Production deployment me standard observability tools hone chahiye: structured logging, tracing, critical events ke liye alarms, aur performance metrics. Cloud vendors apne tools dete hain, lekin vendor-agnostic open source tools jaise OpenTelemetry metrics aur logs collect aur analyze karne me madad karte hain, chahe servers kahin bhi deploy hon, aur Prometheus un metrics ko store, query aur visualize karne me madad karta hai. Kuch AI-oriented observability platforms OpenTelemetry ke saath compatible hain, jaise Langfuse, jo useful hai agar server LLMs ko call karta hai ya agentic applications bhi bana raha ho.

Supply-chain integrity bhi monitor karni hoti hai: dependencies ko up-to-date rakhna aur code aur dependencies ki regular vulnerability scans karna — sirf directly imported dependencies ki nahi, balki database server software jaise external dependencies ki bhi. Trivy aur Semgrep jaise tools madad karte hain aur CI/CD pipeline me great additions hain. Aakhir me human ko process loop me daalna kisi bhi security infrastructure ka critical hissa hai. Kai features ke liye MCP spec require karta hai ki human request ko approve ya deny kare — yeh largely Chapter 6 me cover hua hai. Server developer ko ise implement karne ke liye kuch khaas nahi karna padta, kyunki server operations ki human approval client-side responsibility hai. Server ke calls ko HITL process ko handle karne ke liye likha jaana chahiye, jaise elicitations, aur client se expected approval response ko parse karna chahiye.

Security frameworks — Lethal Trifecta aur MCP Colors

Layer-based approach ke alawa do aur frameworks hain. Pehla hai Lethal Trifecta, jo prompt injection se bachne ke liye hai. Yeh teen capabilities ka group hai, jo ek saath use hone par attacker ke liye malicious prompt se sensitive data access karna ya destructive actions karna aasan bana deta hai: private data tak pahunch, untrusted content (jaise web pages) se exposure, aur third parties ke saath communication. Private data attacker ko woh data deta hai jo woh retrieve karna chahta hai, untrusted content attack vector deta hai, aur third parties se communication se attacker private data tak pahunch sakta hai. Yeh tools ya workflows ke liye dugna relevant hai jo ek saath kaam karne ke liye expected hain. Users ke liye server aur tools ko safe banane ke liye ensure karna chahiye ki individual tools, higher-level workflows aur server khud — in teeno capabilities ko ek saath na rakhein.

Kabhi-kabhi isse bacha nahi ja sakta. 2025 me official GitHub MCP server par hue ek attack ne dikhaya ki kya hota hai jab individual MCP servers yeh vulnerability agents tak pahuncha dete hain. Ek user public repository par malicious prompt wala pull request khol sakta tha (untrusted content se exposure), jisme agent se kaha gaya tha ki woh GitHub MCP Server se dikhai dene wale saare repositories ke saare READMEs padhe (private data tak pahunch), aur phir agent ko instruct kiya gaya ki woh private data ke saath code update kare (third parties se communication) — aur agent ne dutifully aisa karke private projects ko duniya ke saamne expose kar diya. GitHub jaisa MCP server Lethal Trifecta ko seedha address nahi kar sakta, kyunki kisi ek capability ke saare tools hata dene se bahut saari desired functionality chali jaayegi. Yahan architectural solutions kaam aate hain: Docker ne dikhaya ki uska MCP Gateway incoming requests ko middleware se intercept kar sakta hai jo problematic behavior detect kare — is specific attack ke liye middleware detect karta hai ki ek user us repo ke alawa kisi aur repo ko access karne ki koshish kar raha hai jis se woh malicious prompt deliver kar raha hai. Isse "private data tak pahunch" wali capability surgically hata di jaati hai — agent se nahi, server se nahi, malicious user se bhi nahi, balki us request se jo dusre repositories access karne ki koshish kar rahi hai. Ab yeh trifecta nahi raha, aur users ke private repos safe hain. Layer framework ke dusre mitigations bhi hain: layer 1 par server sandboxing — container ko sirf container me daalna nahi, balki uske aas-paas guardrails lagana taaki resource usage, network access aur accessible resources limit hon; layer 2 par broadly scoped personal access tokens se short-lived, fine-grained OAuth scopes par jaana, jisse tokens ko ek repository tak scope kiya ja sakta hai aur credentials ko instantly revoke kiya ja sakta hai; aur layer 3 par OAuth events ko log aur monitor karna, taaki suspicious activity detect ho.

Dusra framework hai MCP Colors, jo Lethal Trifecta se inspired hai aur yeh determine karta hai ki kaunse tools agent me ek saath safely use kiye ja sakte hain. Isme do colors hain: red un tools ke liye jo untrusted content handle karte hain, aur blue un tools ke liye jo critical actions karte hain. Critical actions woh hain jin par extra careful rehna padta hai, kyunki inse data exfiltration, privilege escalation ya aur harmful actions ho sakte hain — jaise specific users ko email karna ya calendar events delete karna, jo aam taur par innocuous lagte hain. Ek baat dhyaan dene wali hai: "private data tak pahunch" wali capability ke liye koi color nahi hai, kyunki is framework me saara data by default private mana jaata hai. Isse analysis simple ho jaati hai, jabki saare data ke prati highly defensive posture bani rehti hai. Apne MCP server par is framework ko apply karte waqt har tool ko red, blue ya neither label karna chahiye — sirf us single, specific tool ke basis par, kisi combination ke basis par nahi. Goal yeh hai ki red aur blue tools ko apne server (ya agent) me bilkul mix na karo. Phir har tool ke liye poochna chahiye ki use yeh label kyun mila hai, aur kya koi tareeqa hai jisse use hataya ja sake. MCP Colors ki asli power isi analysis practice me hai: yeh systematically sochne par majboor karta hai ki har tool users ke liye kya risks present karta hai aur unhe kaise mitigate ya address karna hai, hamesha data ko private treat karte hue. Regulated environments jaise banking, healthcare ya government ke liye yeh chapter sirf foundation hai — MCP-specific security guidance ke liye specification ki apni security best practices se shuru karna chahiye, broader agentic attack surface ke liye OWASP GenAI Security Project aur MITRE ATLAS emerging standard references hain, aur governance aur audit ke liye NIST AI Risk Management Framework aur ISO/IEC 42001 use hote hain.

ch7/03_mcp_oauth_resource_server/server.py — https://github.com/kylestratis/ai_agents_mcp_examples/blob/main/ch7/03_mcp_oauth_resource_server/server.py
from mcp.server.auth.provider import AccessToken, TokenVerifier
from mcp.server.auth.settings import AuthSettings
from mcp.server.mcpserver import MCPServer
from pydantic import AnyHttpUrl


# Auth settings - these will come from your authorization server's documentation
AUTHORIZATION_SERVER_SETTINGS = AuthSettings(
    issuer_url=AnyHttpUrl("https://authorization-server.com"),
    resource_server_url=AnyHttpUrl("https://localhost:3001"),
    required_scopes=["read", "write"],
)


class MyTokenVerifier(TokenVerifier):
    async def verify_token(self, token: str) -> AccessToken | None:
        # YOUR VALIDATION LOGIC HERE
        pass


# Initialize MCP server
mcp = MCPServer(
    "resource-server",
    token_verifier=MyTokenVerifier(),
    auth=AUTHORIZATION_SERVER_SETTINGS,
)


@mcp.tool()
async def example_tool(request: str) -> str:
    """Uppercase the request."""
    return request.upper()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    mcp.run(transport="streamable-http")

"""
Calculator MCP server using MCPServer.
Provides mathematical operations as tools for calculation tasks.
"""

import math

from mcp.server.mcpserver import MCPServer

# Initialize MCP server
mcp = MCPServer("calculator")


@mcp.tool()
async def add(a: float, b: float) -> str:
    """Add two numbers together.

    Args:
        a: First number
        b: Second number
    """
    result = a + b
    return f"{a} + {b} = {result}"


@mcp.tool()
async def subtract(a: float, b: float) -> str:
    """Subtract the second number from the first.

    Args:
        a: Number to subtract from
        b: Number to subtract
    """
    result = a - b
    return f"{a} - {b} = {result}"


@mcp.tool()
async def multiply(a: float, b: float) -> str:
    """Multiply two numbers together.

    Args:
        a: First number
        b: Second number
    """
    result = a * b
    return f"{a} × {b} = {result}"


@mcp.tool()
async def divide(a: float, b: float) -> str:
    """Divide the first number by the second.

    Args:
        a: Dividend (number to be divided)
        b: Divisor (number to divide by)
    """
    if b == 0:
        return "Error: Division by zero is not allowed"

    result = a / b
    return f"{a} ÷ {b} = {result}"


@mcp.tool()
async def power(base: float, exponent: float) -> str:
    """Raise a number to a power.

    Args:
        base: The base number
        exponent: The power to raise the base to
    """
    try:
        result = base**exponent
        return f"{base}^{exponent} = {result}"
    except Exception as e:
        return f"Error calculating power: {str(e)}"


@mcp.tool()
async def square_root(number: float) -> str:
    """Calculate the square root of a number.

    Args:
        number: The number to find the square root of
    """
    if number < 0:
        return "Error: Cannot calculate square root of negative number"

    result = math.sqrt(number)
    return f"√{number} = {result}"


if __name__ == "__main__":
    mcp.run(transport="streamable-http", stateless_http=True, json_response=True)
SOURCESource: AI Agents with MCP, O'Reilly, Chapter 7 — Testing, Securing, and Sharing Your MCP Server
← Previous07 · Server test karna — Inspector aur evaluations→ Next07.2 · Server share karna
07.2Chapter 7 · Testing, Securing, and Sharing Your MCP Server

Server share karna

Tested aur secure server ban gaya — ab use duniya tak pahunchana hai. Local deployments ke liye code share karna kaafi hai, remote deployments ke liye thodi tayyari aur deployment chahiye.

Local deployments — GitHub aur MCP Bundle

Local deployments ke liye aam taur par server code ko ek public repository me share karna kaafi hota hai, saath me instructions ke saath ki use mcp.json, Claude Desktop, Claude Code aur kisi bhi aur client me kaise add karna hai, jise tum specifically call out karna chahte ho. Saare clients ki installation instructions thodi alag hoti hain. Claude Code me /mcp command se server ko mcp.json file me add kiya ja sakta hai, jabki Python server ko Claude Desktop me install karna command line se uv run mcp install server_name.py chalakar kiya ja sakta hai.

Ek aur tareeqa hai apne local server ke liye ek MCP Bundle (MCPB) banana aur use us tareeqe se distribute karna. MCPB ek ZIP file hoti hai, jisme server code aur ek manifest file manifest.json hoti hai, jisme installation client ke liye server ke baare me jaankari hoti hai. Clients MCPB files se install karne ke liye support build kar sakte hain, jisse server ek hi file me users tak distribute ho jaata hai. MCPB GitHub repository me MCPB ki specification aur mcpb command-line tool hai, jo MCPB files banana automate karne me madad karta hai.

Remote deployments — Streamable HTTP aur stateless mode

Remote deployments ke liye kuch aur options hain, lekin pehle kuch prep work karna padta hai. Bare minimum yeh hai ki server Streamable HTTP transport se chalaya jaaye. Behtar scalability ke liye run() ko stateless_http=True aur json_response=True bhi pass kiya ja sakta hai. Current protocol version wale connections hamesha stateless hote hain, lekin stateless_http option purane protocol versions wale clients ko bhi statelessly kaam karne par force karta hai, jisse server ko horizontally scale karna pehle se bahut aasan ho jaata hai. max_request_body_size bhi set kiya ja sakta hai, jiska default 4 MiB hai — isse badi koi bhi request ko HTTP 413 error milegi. Iska flipside yeh hai ki purane clients ke features ko poori fidelity ke saath support nahi kar paoge, to decide karna hoga ki kya zyada benefit deta hai. json_response flag ko True set karne se server ko ek plain request/response API mil jaati hai aur SSE stream essentially band ho jaata hai — server har request ke jawab me sirf plain JSON body return karta hai. Isse serverless platforms, content delivery networks, API gateways aur dusron ke liye MCP server deployments host aur scale karna aasan ho jaata hai, jo poore responses ko buffer karte hain.

mcp.run(
    transport="streamable-http", stateless_http=True, json_response=True
)

ASGI frameworks — Starlette ya FastAPI se mount karna

Asynchronous Server Gateway Interface (ASGI) frameworks jaise Starlette ya FastAPI se zyada robust aur scalable MCP server banaya ja sakta hai, jise phir pasand ke host par deploy kiya ja sakta hai. Iske liye server code me kuch cheezein add karni hoti hain: pehle ek lifespan context manager add karna hota hai. Yeh lifespan management jaisa hi hai, lekin lifespan function ko Starlette type ka parameter bhi pass karna hota hai. Uske baad, if __name__ == "__main__" block ki jagah ek Starlette application object instantiate karna hota hai, aur use routes aur lifespan context manager pass karne hote hain. Agar ek hi server mount kar rahe ho to use "/" par mount kar sakte ho, lekin agar multiple servers support karne hain to har ek ke liye individual paths set karne honge.

Ek example me lifespan() function MCP server ke session manager ko chalati hai — await stack.enter_async_context(mcp.session_manager.run()) — aur phir Starlette constructor ko Mount("/", mcp.streamable_http_app(stateless_http=True, json_response=True)) pass kiya jaata hai. Yeh /mcp endpoint expose karta hai — locally chal raha ho to http://localhost:8000/mcp par access kiya ja sakta hai. Starlette application ko uvicorn.run(app) se standalone Python application ki tarah chalaya ja sakta hai, ya command line se uvicorn app:app se bhi, optionally host aur port specify karke.

Containerize karke cloud par deploy karna

Wahan se server ko favorite cloud platform ya server par host kiya ja sakta hai. Deploy karne se pehle service provider ki ASGI applications host karne ki instructions review karni chahiye. Aksar server ko containerize karke image banana hota hai, phir use Docker Hub ya AWS Elastic Container Registry (ECR) jaise container registry par upload karna hota hai. Remote Python MCP server ke liye ek simple Dockerfile Python 3.13-slim base image use karta hai, project ko /app me install karta hai, pip install se mcp[cli], starlette aur uvicorn dependencies install karta hai, port 8000 expose karta hai, aur CMD ["uvicorn", "server:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"] se application chalata hai. Phir image ko docker build -t mcp-server . se build karke docker run -p 8000:8000 mcp-server se locally chalaya ja sakta hai.

MCP Registry me publish karna

Server ko duniya tak pahunchane ke kai avenues hain, lekin MCP duniya MCP server registry ke aas-paas converge ho rahi hai. Yeh MCP servers ki ek centralized registry hai, jise MCP clients seedha hook karke server ko discover aur use kar sakte hain. Ise MCP servers ke liye npm ya Python Package Index (PyPI) jaisa samjho. Registry ka goal yeh hai ki users official registry ko filter karke specialized subregistries banayein — lekin server developer ke roop me official registry par publish karne par focus karna chahiye, kyunki subregistries largely official registry ko filter karke zyada specific set banayengi. Is likhai ke waqt registry abhi bhi preview me hai, to tooling flux me hai aur tezi se improve hone ki ummeed hai.

Registry me publish karne ke liye server ko pehle kisi existing language-based registry jaise npm ya PyPI par register aur publish karna hoga. Python package ko PyPI par publish karne ke baad mcp-publisher tool install karke use karna hota hai. Pehle mcp-publisher init chalakar server.json file generate ki jaati hai. PyPI use karne wale Python packages ke liye file ko manually update karna hota hai: version ko sahi version par set karo, koi bhi environment variables set karo (ya script se generate hui example wali hata do), aur packages array me registryType field ko "pypi" par update karo.

Phir server package ki ownership verify karni hoti hai — package ke README me ek string include karke, mcp-name: your_mcp_name ke form me, jahan your_mcp_name server ka naam hai jo server.json file me hai. Is string ko comment me chhupaya ja sakta hai, taaki woh PyPI project description me na dikhe. Phir mcp-publisher se registry me login karna hota hai — currently GitHub OAuth se login accept hota hai, mcp-publisher login github se. Login ke baad mcp-publisher publish se server ko registry me publish kiya jaata hai, aur phir registry API ke search endpoint ko call karke verify kiya jaata hai: https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0.1/servers?search=your_mcp_name.
